articles.title: पार्टी निर्माणमा सि जिनपिङको अवधारणाबारे नेपालमा चर्चा
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपालसहित विश्वमा राजनीतिक दलको निर्माण र त्यसको प्रभावकारी संचालनका लागि चिनियाँ राष्ट्रपति सि जिनपिङको अवधारणा उपयोगी हुने विज्ञहरुले बताएका छन् । फ्रेन्डस अन क्लाउडले काठमाडौंमा गरेको कार्यक्रममा राजनीतिज्ञ जगन्नाथ खतिवडा, परराष्ट्रविद डा गोपाल खनाल, पूर्व राजदूत महेशराज दाहाल, अनुसन्धानकर्ता डा। दीपक देवकोटा र क्लाउडका अध्यक्ष शोभित उप्रेतीले पार्टी निर्माणमा राष्ट्रपति सी का विभिन्न आयामबारे धारणा राखेका हुन् ।

कार्यक्रममा बो्ल्दै पूर्व राजदूत दाहालले राष्ट्रपति सिको अध्ययनशिल बानी नै पार्टी र राष्ट्र निर्माणका लागि आधारशिला बनेको उल्ले गरे ।

दाहालका अनुसार श्रम शिविरमा हुँदा पनि निकै अध्धयन गर्ने सी लामो र नयाँ सोचका थिए । सृजनशीलता परिवर्तनकारी सोचका धनी सीले पार्टी सदसयता पाउन पनि निकै संघर्ष गरेकाले पार्टी कस्तो हुनुपर्छ भन्ने पनि उनले राम्रोसँग बुझेका थिए ।

राम्रो दृष्टिकोण भए पार्टी र देश बन्छ भन्ने कुरा उनले प्रमाणित गरेर देखाए । भ्रष्टाचार विरुद्वका कार्यक्रम र दल भित्रको शुद्वतामा उनको जोड थियो । नेतृत्वको जिम्मेवारी र कर्तव्य । प्रविधि विकास, जनताको सहभागीता, विज्ञानमा लगानी उनको पार्टी निर्माणका प्रमुख साधन हुन ।

यस्तै , डा दिपक देवकोटाले राष्ट्रपति सीले राज्यबाट डर नभई भरोसा जगाउने काम गरेर सफलता प्राप्त गरेको धारणा राखे । जनतालाई केन्द्रमा राखेर पार्टी र देश निर्माण गर्न उनी सफल भए ।

जनताले विश्वास गर्ने पार्टी बनाउन राष्ट्रपति सी ले सुशासन र सुरक्षालाई प्राथमिकता दिएको उनले बताए । परराष्ट्र विद डा गोपाल खनालले विश्वव्यापी सुशासन अभियान र नयाँ युगका लागि चिनियाँ विशेषतासहितको समाजवाद नै सि जिनपिङको पार्टी निर्माणको स्पष्ट अवधारणा भएको बताए ।

पार्टी नियम र देश कानुनबाट चल्छ भन्ने कुरा राष्ट्रपति सी ले स्थापित गरेको उनको भनाइ छ । जनतालाई विकास दिने सोच नै सिको सोच भएको खनालको निष्कर्ष छ।

आर्थिक अनियमितता गर्ने ७० लाख भन्दा बढीलाई चीनमा कारबाही गरिएको जानकारी दिंदै खनालले राष्ट्रपति सी को सुशासन अभियानको प्रशंसा गरे ।

नेता जगन्नाथ खतिवडाले अनुशासन, अनुगमन र आत्मसमीक्षाको सुत्र न‌ै राष्ट्रपति सि को पार्टी र देश निर्माणको आधारशिला रहेको धारणा राखे ।

राष्ट्रपति सि ले विचार निर्माण, राजनीति निर्माण र संगठन निर्माणमा जोड दिंदै पार्टीमा गुणस्तरीय सदस्यलाई मात्र स्थान दिएको खतिवडाले बताए । चीन जस्तो शक्तिशाली राष्ट्र हाम्रो छिमेकी भएकाले दलीय एकता तथा दीर्घकालीन सोच र योजनाका साथ अघि बढ्ने कुरा नेपालले सिक्नुपर्ने खतिवडा बताउँछन् ।

articles.title: ग्लोबल आइएमई बैंकमा नागरिक एपबाटै खाता खोल्न सकिने
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । ग्लोबल आइएमई बैंक लिमिटेडले नागरिक एपसँगको सहकार्यमा नागरिक एपमार्फतै बैंक खाता खोल्न सकिने नयाँ सुविधा सुरु गरेको छ ।

राष्ट्रिय परिचयपत्रका आधारमा नागरिक एपमा आबद्ध नेपाली नागरिकले बैंकको वेबसाइटमा उपलब्ध क्यूआर कोड स्क्यान गरी व्यक्तिगत बचत खाता अनलाइनबाटै खोल्न सक्नेछन् ।

यो सेवा १८ वर्ष वा सोभन्दा माथिका राष्ट्रिय परिचयपत्र भएका तथा नागरिक एपमा आबद्ध व्यक्तिका लागि उपलब्ध हुनेछ । खाता खोल्ने क्रममा बैंकले ग्राहकको पूर्वसहमतिमा आवश्यक व्यक्तिगत विवरण नागरिक एपबाट सुरक्षित रूपमा प्राप्त गर्ने भएकाले पुनः विवरण भर्नुपर्ने झन्झट हट्ने, गोपनीयता कायम रहने र सूचनाको सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित हुने बैंकले जनाएको छ ।

नागरिक एपमार्फत खोलिएको खाता सञ्चालनका लागि भने ग्राहकले नजिकको शाखामा गई वा भिडियो केवाईसीमार्फत प्रमाणीकरण गर्नुपर्नेछ ।

बैंकका अनुसार सरकारी डिजिटल पूर्वाधारको उपयोग गर्दै सुरु गरिएको यो सेवाले खाता खोल्ने प्रक्रियालाई थप सहज, सुरक्षित, पारदर्शी र प्रविधिमैत्री बनाउनेछ । ग्राहकलाई आधुनिक डिजिटल बैंकिङ अनुभव प्रदान गर्ने विश्वास बैंकको छ ।

ग्लोबल आइएमई बैंक ७७ वटै जिल्लामा शाखा सञ्जाल विस्तार गर्ने निजी क्षेत्रको पहिलो वाणिज्य बैंक हो ।

हाल बैंकले ३४२ शाखा, ३६८ एटिएम, १४७ शाखारहित बैंकिङ सेवा, ६९ एक्सटेन्सन तथा राजस्व सङ्कलन काउन्टर र ३ वटा वैदेशिक प्रतिनिधि कार्यालयसहित १ हजारभन्दा बढी सेवा केन्द्रमार्फत सेवा दिँदै आएको छ ।

articles.title: मेलम्चीमा स्थानीय उत्पादन प्रवर्द्धनका लागि ‘कोशेली घर’ उद्घाटन
articles.summary:
मेलम्ची । स्थानीय कृषि र हस्तकला उत्पादनलाई प्रवर्द्धन गर्ने उद्देश्यले सिन्धुपाल्चोकको मेलम्ची बजारमा नयाँ व्यावसायिक केन्द्र “कोशेली घर” सञ्चालनमा आएको छ। साउन ८ देखि हरेक दिन बिहान ७ बजेदेखि राति ७ बजेसम्म खुल्ने यो कोशेलीघरको उद्घाटन नगरप्रमुख आइतमान तामाङले गरेका छन् ।

नगरप्रमुख तामाङले कोशेलीघरबाट ताजा फलफूल तथा तरकारी, घरेलु अचार, मह, भान्साका आवश्यक परिकार, हस्तकला सामग्री, अण्डा, माछा, गेडागुडी, चिया, कफी तथा हर्बल सामग्रीलगायत स्थानीय रैथाने उत्पादनको सीधा बिक्री वितरणमा जोड दिने बताए । उनले यहाँ राखिने विशेष परिकार तथा उत्पादनहरू आवश्यक परेमा जिल्ला बाहिर पनि पठाइने समेत जनाए ।

कोशेलीघरले स्थानीय उत्पादक र उपभोक्तालाई एउटै छानामुनि प्रत्यक्ष भेटघाटको व्यवस्था गराउँदै बजारसम्म पहुँच सहज बनाउने लक्ष्य लिएको प्रमुख तामाङले बताए ।

साथै प्रमुख प्रशासकीय अधिकृत निमेष मिश्रले ‘फार्म देखि किचनसम्म अवधारणाअनुरूप उत्पादक र उपभोक्ताको मागअनुसार नयाँ वस्तु तथा उत्पादनहरू परिष्कृत गरी सार्वजनिक गरिने र उद्यमीहरूको भेटघाट हुने उपयुक्त स्थलको रूपमा यसलाई विकास गर्ने योजना रहेको बताए । प्रारम्भिक अनुमान अनुसार नगरपालिकाले दैनिक हजारौंले यहाँबाट किनमेल गर्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

मेलम्ची आसपासका सरकारी तथा निजी कार्यालयका कर्मचारी, घुम्न आउने पर्यटक, स्थानीय टोल तथा छिमेकी पालिकाका बासिन्दाहरू प्रमुख लक्षित ग्राहक रहने कोशेलीघरबाट स्थानिय रोजगारी र व्यवसायिक गतिविधिलाई थप सक्रिय बनाउन मद्दत पुग्ने उपस्थित उपभोक्ताले विश्वास व्यक्त गरिएको थियो ।

articles.title: २४ औं अनसन शुरु, समर्थनसँगै विरोध पनि बढ्दै
articles.summary:
कैलाली । धनगढीस्थित कृष्ण मन्दिर धर्मशालामा डा. गोविन्द केसीको सत्याग्रह दोस्रो दिन पनि जारी छ । स्वास्थ्य क्षेत्र सुधारका पाँचबुँदे माग अघि सार्दै उनले शहीद दशरथचन्द स्वास्थ्य विज्ञान विश्वविद्यालय र चिकित्सा शिक्षा आयोगमा स्वार्थ बाझिने नियुक्ति खारेज गर्न, चिकित्सा शिक्षा ऐन संशोधन गर्न, छात्रवृत्ति कटौतीको निर्णय फिर्ता लिन र मापदण्ड नपुगेका निजी मेडिकल कलेजमा थप सिट स्वीकृति रोक्न सरकारसँग माग गरेका छन् ।

विगतका सहमति कार्यान्वयन, चिकित्सा शिक्षालाई गैरनाफामूलक बनाउने तथा भ्रष्टाचार र अपराधका आरोपमाथि निष्पक्ष अनुसन्धानको मागसमेत डा. केसीले गरेका छन् । डा. केसीले आफू विश्वविद्यालयको विरोधमा नभई स्वार्थ बाँझिने नियुक्तिको विरोधमा सत्याग्रहमा बसेको स्पष्ट पारेका छन् ।

यता शहीद दशरथचन्द स्वास्थ्य विज्ञान विश्वविद्यालय संघर्ष समितिले भने डा. केसीलाई सत्याग्रह स्थगित गर्न आग्रह गरेको छ ।

संयोजक लोकराज पाण्डेको नेतृत्वमा प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारीलाई भेटेको टोलीले आन्दोलनका कारण विश्वविद्यालय सञ्चालन र विकासको प्रक्रिया प्रभावित हुन सक्ने भन्दै आवश्यक पहल गर्न अनुरोध गरेको हो ।

उता, कृष्ण मन्दिर धर्मशाला व्यवस्थापन समितिले पूर्वसूचना बिना अनिश्चितकालीन सत्याग्रह सुरु गरिएको भन्दै डा. केसीलाई स्थान खाली गर्न पत्र दिएको छ । तर डा. केसीले व्यवस्थापन समितिसँग सहमतिमै सत्याग्रह सुरु गरेको दाबी गर्दै केही स्वार्थ समूहले आन्दोलन कमजोर पार्ने प्रयास गरिरहेको आरोप लगाए ।

उनले दबाब र अवरोधका बाबजुद आफ्ना मागबाट पछि नहट्ने र आवश्यक परे फुटपाथमै बसेर पनि सत्याग्रहलाई निरन्तरता दिने बताएका छन् ।

चिकित्सा शिक्षा सुधारको मागसँगै डा. केसीको आन्दोलन जारी रहँदा विश्वविद्यालय सञ्चालनमा असर पर्ने चिन्ता भने स्थानीय स्तरमा बढ्दै गएको छ ।

articles.title: २ लाख ऋण, १४ लाख तिर्दापनि जग्गा बैंकको कब्जामा !
articles.summary:
सप्तरी । सप्तरीको विष्णुपुर–६ मा माय जलपा बचत तथा ऋण सहकारीका अध्यक्षले ऋणीहरूको धितो जग्गा फिर्ता नगरी आफ्नै परिवारको नाममा नामसारी गरेर बैंकमा धितो राखेको आरोप लागेको छ । बैंकले लिलामी सूचना प्रकाशित गरेपछि पीडितहरू ठगीको तथ्य थाहा पाएसँगै जग्गा फिर्ता र दोषीमाथि कारबाहीको माग गर्दै न्यायको खोजीमा भौतारीरहेका छन् ।

सप्तरीको विष्णुपुर गाउँपालिका–६ रञ्जितपुरकी रेणु देवी दासले २०७२ सालमा माय जलपा बचत तथा ऋण सहकारी संस्था लिमिटेडबाट छोरीको विवाहका लागि दुई लाख रुपैयाँ ऋण लिएकी थिइन् । उनले ब्याजसहित पटक–पटक गरेर करिब १४ लाख रुपैयाँ तिरेर तीन वर्षअघि नै ऋण चुक्ता गरिन् । तर सहकारीका अध्यक्ष दिलिप यादवले घरको लालपुर्जा फिर्ता दिन आलटाल गर्दै आएका छन् ।

अहिले मल्टीपर्पस् फाइनान्स बैंकले उक्त घरजग्गा लिलामीको सूचना प्रकाशित गरेपछि सहकारी अध्यक्षको कर्तुत सार्वजनिक भएको छ भने पीडित परिवार न्यायको खोजीमा भौतारिएको छ । अनुसन्धानका क्रममा सहकारीका अध्यक्ष यादवले जग्गा आफ्नो पत्नी सुनिता यादवको नाममा नामसारी गराई सोही जग्गा धितो राखेर बैंकबाट ऋण लिएको आरोप लागेको छ । बैंकले लिलामी सूचना जारी गरेपछि मात्रै पीडितले आफ्नो जग्गा अर्कैको नाममा रहेको थाहा पाएका हुन् ।

लिलामी सूचना देखेपछि रेणु दास बैंक पुगेर आफ्नो जग्गाबारे जानकारी मागेकी थिइन् । बैंकले ऋण बराबरको रकम तिरेपछि मात्रै जग्गा फिर्ता गर्न सकिने जनाएको उनको भनाइ छ । त्यसपछि उनले सहकारी अध्यक्षलाई बैंक जान आग्रह गरे पनि उनले अस्वीकार गर्दै सम्पर्कबाट टाढिएका छन् ।

यस्तै स्थानीय पुलकित मुखियाले पनि ५० हजार रुपैयाँ ऋण लिएर धितो राखेको एक कठ्ठा जग्गा ऋण चुक्ता गर्दा समेत फिर्ता नपाएको र आफ्नो नामबाटै नामसारी गरिएको आरोप लगाएका छन् ।

पीडितहरू सहकारीका सञ्चालकले सम्पत्ति बेचेर फरार हुने आशंकामा छन् । उनीहरू आफ्नो जग्गा फिर्ता गराइ दोषीमाथि कारबाही गर्न सम्बन्धित निकायसँग न्यायको माग गरिरहेका छन् ।

articles.title: उजाड पाखामा चिया खेती, गाउँमै रोजगारी
articles.summary:
दोलखा । दोलखाको कालिञ्चोक गाउँपालिका–४ सुन्द्रावतीमा व्यावसायिक चिया खेतीले गाउँमै रोजगारी सिर्जना गरेको छ । बाँझो जमिन हरियो चिया बगानमा रूपान्तरण भएपछि महिला, ज्येष्ठ नागरिक र युवाले दैनिक १८ सय रुपैयाँसम्म आम्दानी गर्दै स्थानीय आर्थिक गतिविधिमा उल्लेख्य टेवा पु¥याएका छन् ।

दोलखाको कालिञ्चोक गाउँपालिका–९ सुन्द्रावतीमा व्यावसायिक चिया खेतीले गाउँको स्वरूप फेरिएको छ । रोजगारीको अभावका कारण हुने युवा पलायन र बाँदर आतंकजस्ता समस्याको समाधान गर्दै चिया खेती स्थानीयका लागि आयआर्जनको भरपर्दो माध्यम बनेको छ ।

पहिले उत्तिसको घारीले ढाकिएको र झुसुले किराको समस्याले विद्यालयका विद्यार्थीसमेत प्रभावित थिए । तर यो क्षेत्र वडा कार्यालयको पहलमा सफा गरी इलामबाट ल्याइएका २५ हजार चियाका बिरुवासहित हरियो चिया बगानमा रूपान्तरण गरिएको छ ।

प्रारम्भिक परीक्षण सफल भएपछि यसको व्यवस्थापनको जिम्मा स्थानीयको सहभागितामा बनेको सुन्द्रावती चिया विकास समूहलाई हस्तान्तरण गरिएको छ । ७–८ वर्षको अन्तरालमा यहाँ उत्पादित चियाले बजार पाउन थालेको छ ।

प्रति किलो १०० रुपैयाँका दरले चियाको मुना टिप्ने व्यवस्था भएपछि महिला, ज्येष्ठ नागरिक र परीक्षा दिएर बसेका विद्यार्थीले गाउँमै रोजगारी पाएका छन् । बिहानदेखि साँझसम्म काम गर्ने मजदुरले दैनिक १८ सय रुपैयाँसम्म आम्दानी गरिरहेका छन् ।

वडा कार्यालयको बजेट र लगानीमा अघि बढाइएको यस योजनामा चालु आर्थिक वर्ष मात्रै ४ लाख रुपैयाँ थप लगानी गरिएको छ । चिया प्रशोधन सहज बनाउन ६ लाख रुपैयाँ लागतमा तीन प्रकारका आधुनिक प्रशोधन मेसिनसमेत सञ्चालनमा ल्याइएको छ ।

स्थानीय सरकारको सही योजना र निरन्तर लगानी भए बाँझो जमिनलाई पनि आम्दानीको स्रोत बनाउन सकिने उदाहरण सुन्द्रावतीको चिया खेतीले प्रस्तुत गरेको छ ।

articles.title: मारुती सिमेन्टद्वारा जयन्ती मेमोरियल ट्रस्टलाई CPR तालिमका लागि म्यानिकिन हस्तान्तरण
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । हालको परिवेशमा विशेषगरी युवापुस्तामा अस्वस्थ जीवनशैली, अत्यधिक तनाव तथा हृदयसम्बन्धी आकस्मिक समस्याका घटनामा वृद्धि हुँदै गएको अवस्थालाई मध्यनजर गर्दै CPR (Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation) तालिमको आवश्यकता बढ्दै गएको छ।

यही आवश्यकतालाई महसुस गर्दै मारुती सिमेन्ट लिमिटेड ले आफ्नो सामाजिक उत्तरदायित्व (CSR) अन्तर्गत देशभर CPR तालिम सञ्चालन गर्ने उद्देश्यका साथ जयन्ती मेमोरियल ट्रस्ट लाई आवश्यक CPR Training Manikin हस्तान्तरण गरेको छ।

उक्त सामग्री हस्तान्तरण कार्यक्रम दुवै संस्थाका सञ्चालक तथा पदाधिकारीहरूको उपस्थितिमा सम्पन्न भएको हो। कार्यक्रममा मारुती सिमेन्ट लिमिटेडले समाजप्रतिको आफ्नो उत्तरदायित्व निर्वाह गर्ने प्रतिबद्धतालाई व्यवहारमा उतार्दै स्वास्थ्य सचेतना अभिवृद्धिमा सहयोग पुर्‍याउन पाउँदा खुशी लागेको जनाएको छ।

जयन्ती मेमोरियल ट्रस्टले प्राप्त CPR Training Manikin को प्रयोग गरी देशभर निःशुल्क वा पहुँचयोग्य CPR तालिम सञ्चालन गर्ने, आकस्मिक हृदयाघात वा अन्य आपत्कालीन अवस्थामा सर्वसाधारणले समयमै प्राथमिक उपचार प्रदान गर्न सक्ने जनशक्ति तयार गर्ने लक्ष्य रहेको जनाएको छ।

ट्रस्टका अनुसार CPR सम्बन्धी ज्ञान र सीपको विस्तारले आकस्मिक अवस्थामा बहुमूल्य जीवन बचाउन महत्वपूर्ण योगदान पुग्ने विश्वास गरिएको छ। यस सहकार्यले समुदायमा स्वास्थ्य सचेतना बढाउनुका साथै जीवनरक्षा सम्बन्धी सीप विकासमा महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका खेल्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

articles.title: सैनिक कल्याणकारी भवन ठेक्का प्रकरण : निर्माण व्यवसायीमाथि चरम अन्याय र अर्बौँको लगानी जोखिममा !
articles.summary:
काठमाडौँ । काठमाडौँको न्यूरोड महाँकालस्थानस्थित सैनिक कल्याणकारी कोषको स्वामित्वमा रहेको व्यावसायिक भवन भाडामा लिई अर्बौँ रुपैयाँ लगानी गरेको श्रीजयन्ती निर्माण सेवा प्रा. लि. चरम प्रशासनिक थिचोमिचो र अन्यायमा परेको निश्कर्ष निकालिएको छ ।

भवन हस्तान्तरणमा सेनाकै तर्फबाट भएको ढिलाइ, काठमाडौँ महानगरपालिकासँगको नक्सा पास विवाद र कोभिड–१९ को महामारीका कारण उत्पन्न विषम परिस्थितिलाई नजरअन्दाज गर्दै कल्याणकारी निर्देशनालयले उल्टै निर्माण व्यवसायीमाथि एकतर्फी रूपमा करोडौँ बक्यौताको भार थोपरेको पाइएको हो । यस विषयमा अहिले सर्वोच्च अदालतमा मुद्धा पुगेको छ । साथै यस विषयमा मानव अधिकार आयोगमा पनि उजुरी परेको छ ।

प्राप्त दस्तावेज तथा पत्राचारका अनुसार सैनिक कल्याणकारी कोष र श्रीजयन्ती निर्माण सेवा प्रा. लि. बीच २०७६ माघ १६ गते महाँकालस्थानस्थित ‘कल्याणकारी भवन’१५ वर्षका लागि भाडामा लिने सम्झौता भएको थियो । सम्झौताको मुख्य सर्त नै भवन विधिवत रूपमा पूर्ण निर्माण भई हस्तान्तरण भएपछि मात्र भाडा लागू हुने भन्ने थियो । तर, बोलपत्र जारी गर्दाकै बखत उक्त भवनको नक्सा पास नभएको र मापदण्ड विपरीत बढी निर्माण गरिएको भन्दै काठमाडौँ महानगरपालिकाले काम रोकेपछि सम्झौताको प्रारम्भिक चरणमै विवाद उत्पन्न भएको थियो । सैनिक कल्याणकारी निर्देशनालयको आफ्नै आन्तरिक र कानुनी त्रुटिका कारण समयमा भवन हस्तान्तरण हुन नसकेको बताइन्छ ।

पुरक सम्झौताको उल्लंघन र कोभिडको मार

भवन हस्तान्तरण हुन नसकेपछि दुवै पक्षबीच वि.सं. २०७८ मङ्सिर २८ गते पुरक सम्झौता गरियो, जसमा भवन हस्तान्तरणको मिति २०७८ असार १ कायम गर्ने प्रयास गरियो । तर, सो अवधिमा देशव्यापी रूपमा फैलिएको कोभिड–१९ को दोस्रो लहर र लकडाउनका कारण भवन पूर्ण रूपमा तयार भई व्यापारिक प्रयोजनका लागि हस्तान्तरण हुनै सकेन ।

व्यापार व्यवसाय ठप्प भएको र बैंक तथा वित्तीय संस्थाबाट कर्जा प्रवाह नभएको यस्तो गम्भीर आर्थिक मन्दीको समयमा नेपाल सरकार रक्षा मन्त्रालयले समेत भाडामा छुट दिन निर्देशन जारी गरेको थियो । सैनिक कोषको आफ्नै कार्यदलले भाडामा ५० प्रतिशत छुट दिने राय पेस गरेपनि निर्देशनालयका केही अधिकारीहरूको बदनियतका कारण व्यवसायीले पाउनुपर्ने उक्त कानुनी छुट रकम उपलब्ध गराइएन ।

प्रशासनको उल्झन

निर्माण कम्पनीका एकल शेयरधनी खगेन्द्र बुढामगरका अनुसार, खण्डहर अवस्थामा रहेको भवनलाई अर्बौँ रुपैयाँ निजी लगानी गरेर मासिक ५ करोड ६३ लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी भाडा उठ्ने सुनिश्चित व्यावसायिक केन्द्र बनाएपछि सैनिक कोषका केही अधिकारीहरूको ‘गिद्धे नजर’ यसमा परेको हो ।

कम्पनीले पटक–पटक पारदर्शी हिसाब मिलानका लागि लिखित अनुरोध गर्दा समेत त्यसलाई बेवास्ता गर्दै उल्टै पानी र बिजुलीको लाइन काट्ने, लिफ्ट प्रयोग गर्न नदिने र कम्पनीका कर्मचारीहरूमाथि कार्यस्थलमै भौतिक आक्रमण गर्नेसम्मका निकृष्ट कार्यहरू भएका छन् । जसले गर्दा व्यवसायी मानसिक र आर्थिक रूपमा पूर्णतः धराशयी हुने अवस्थामा पुगेका छन् ।

निष्पक्ष छानबिन र हिसाब फरफारकको माग

नेपाली सेनासँग लामो समयदेखि विकट भूगोल र ब्यारेकहरूमा समेत निर्माण कार्य गरी व्यावसायिक सम्बन्ध कायम राखेको यस कम्पनीले रक्षा मन्त्रालय, प्रधानसेनापति कार्यालय र बालाध्यक्ष विभागमा बोधार्थ दिँदै एक उच्चस्तरीय निष्पक्ष छानबिन टोली गठन गर्न माग गरेको छ । कम्पनीले सैनिक कल्याणकारी कोषलाई कुनै रकम तिर्नु बुझाउनु पर्ने बाँकी नरहेको, उल्टै कल्याणकारी कोषको तर्फबाट भएको सम्झौता उल्लंघन र अनाधिकृत रकम असुलीका कारण आफूले अर्बौँ रुपैयाँ क्षतिपूर्ति पाउनुपर्ने दाबी गरेको छ । राज्यको शक्तिशाली अंगको आडमा एउटा वैधानिक निर्माण व्यवसायीको निजी सम्पत्ति र लगानीमाथि गरिएको यो चरम दोहनले नेपालमा निजी क्षेत्रको लगानी कति असुरक्षित छ भन्ने गम्भीर प्रश्न खडा गरेको छ ।

भवन ठेक्कामा करिब २० करोड हिनामिना आरोप

काठमाडौँको न्यूरोड महाँकालस्थानस्थित सैनिक कल्याणकारी कोषको स्वामित्वमा रहेको व्यावसायिक भवन ठेक्का प्रकरणमा तत्कालीन सैनिक कल्याणकारी निर्देशनालयका उच्च अधिकारी र कर्मचारीहरूको मिलेमतोमा झण्डै २० करोड रुपैयाँ बराबरको ठूलो आर्थिक हिनामिना भएको गम्भीर आरोप लागेको छ । श्रीजयन्ती निर्माण सेवा प्रा। लि। का एकल शेयरधनी खगेन्द्र बुढामगरले सैनिक कल्याणकारी कोषका तत्कालीन उच्च अधिकारी र हालका प्रमुख अवकाशप्राप्त जर्नेल सुनिल राज विष्ट,कर्मचारीहरू नानिराम थापा र कर्णबहादुर तामाङ लगायतले शक्तिको दुरुपयोग गरी अर्बौँको निजी लगानी डुबाउन खोजेको आरोप लगाएका छन् ।

श्री जयन्ती निर्माण सेवा प्रालिबाट भवन व्यवस्थापन कार्यालयमा पदस्थापन भएका नानिराम थापा,कर्णबहादुर तामाङ लगायत त्यहाँ कार्यरत कर्मचारीहरुको मिलेमतोमा उक्त भवनमा श्री जयन्ती निर्माण सेवा प्रालिले उठाउनुपर्ने भाडा बिजुली महसुल र क्याम्प चार्ज असुल गरेको आरोप लागेको हो ।

त्यस्तै,यो टोलीले निर्माण व्यवसायी खगेन्द्र बुढामगरसँग मात्र होइन,त्यस भवनमा व्यवसाय गरिरहेका विभिन्न व्यापारीलाई नाम सारी तथा राम्रो लोकेशनको पसल उपलब्ध गराइदिने प्रलोभनमा पारी रकम उठाइरहेको बुढाको गम्भीर आरोप छ ।

त्यसैगरी बुढाका अनुसार यी पात्रहरुले अदालतलाई समेत विभिन्न माध्यमबाट दबाब सिर्जना गर्ने र मुद्दालाई कम्जोर बनाएर आफ्नो काला कर्तुतहरु लुकाउन खोजेको उनले बताएका छन् ।

कल्याणकारी निर्देशनालयले बोलपत्र आह्वान गर्दा भवनको नक्सा पास नै नभएको र महानगरको अवरोधका कारण निर्माण कम्पनीले समयमा काम सुरु गर्न नपाएको, भवन पूर्ण रूपमा निर्माण नै नभई र खण्डहर अवस्थामा रहँदा समेत निर्देशनालयले पुरै अवधिको पूर्ण भाडा दाबी गरी पत्र पठाउनु कानुनी रूपमा त्रुटिपूर्ण रहेको, कम्पनीले आफ्नै खर्चमा जडान गरेको ट्रान्सफर्मर, विद्युतीकरण, खानेपानी प्रणाली, र लिफ्ट जस्ता पूर्वाधारहरू कल्याणकारी भवन व्यवस्थापनले एकतर्फी रूपमा नियन्त्रणमा लिई व्यवसायीलाई प्रवेशमा रोक लगाएको आरोप लागेको छ ।

भवन व्यवस्थापनकै केही कर्मचारीहरूले व्यापारीहरूबाट सोझै करिब १ करोड ३५ लाख विद्युत महसुल र क्याम्प चार्ज उठाएको साथै २०७९ साल श्रावण,भदौ र असोज ५ गतेसम्मको पुरै भवन भाडा श्री जयन्ती निर्माण सेवा प्रालिको बैंक ग्यारेन्टीबाट असुल गरेको र त्यहाँ व्यवसायी गरिरहेका ब्यापारीहरुबाट समेत असुल गरी सो रकम हिसाबमा मिलान नगरी गायब पारेको अर्को गम्भिर आरोप पनि छ ।

कम्पनीको नाममा रहेको मिटर तथा बिलिङ सफ्टवेयर नक्कली हस्ताक्षर प्रयोग गरी अनाधिकृत रूपमा नामसारी गरिएको र कम्पनीले अर्बौँ खर्चेर बनाएका संरचनाहरू सहमति बिना भत्काएर दोहन गरिएको आरोप छ ।

त्यस्तै,अहिले यस विषयमा मानव अधिकार लगायतका स्वतन्त्र निकायहरुले वास्तविक छानबिन गरिरहेको र सर्वोच्च अदालतमा समेत मुद्दा चलिरहेको निर्माण व्यवसायी बुढा मगरले जानकारी दिए । उनका अनुसार सर्वोच्च अदालतले १५ श्रावणमा दुबैपक्षलाई छलफलका लागि बोलाएको हुँदा उक्त छलफलबाट सकारात्मक नतिजा आउने बुढा मगरले विश्वास गरेका छन् ।

articles.title: एनसेल अब सरकारको नाममा आउने, सर्वोच्चको बोल्ड फैसलापछि वालेन्द्रको परीक्षा शुरु
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । एनसेल निजी क्षेत्रको अग्रणी सञ्चार माध्यमको रुपमा स्थापित कम्पनी हो। तर, एनसेलले नेपालमा गरिरहेको व्यापार र सेवा प्रवाह भने विवादास्पद नै छ। कर प्रकरणदेखि अन्य विषयमा समेत लम्बेतान विवादमा फसेको एनसेलको सेयर किनबेचपछि भने यसबारेका प्रश्नको सवालमा सर्वोच्च अदालतको आदेशपछि थप कानूनी प्रष्टतासहित अवैध गतिविधिविरुद्ध नेपालले आफ्नो कानूनको कार्यान्वयन गर्न सक्षम छ भन्ने सन्देश दिएको छ ।

लामो समय कर विवादमा फसेको एनसेल नेपालको अग्रणी निजी क्षेत्रको टेलिकम सेवा प्रदायक बन्न पुग्यो। नेपालको टेलिकम क्षेत्रमा नविनताका निम्ति काम गरेको एनसेलले सञ्चारको क्षेत्रमा खेलेको भूमिकामाथि प्रश्न गर्ने ठाउँ छैन्।

अझं भन्नुपर्दा सरकारी स्वामित्वको नेपाल टेलिकमले दिने सेवालाई एनसेलले दिएको चुनौतीकै कारण सञ्चार क्षेत्रले नेपालमा राम्रो स्तरको सेवा प्रवाहमा काम गरेको पाइन्छ। तर, एनसेलको यो राम्रो पाटोसंगै विवाद भने अत्यन्तै महत्वपूर्ण छन्। हरेक वर्ष मनग्य आम्दानी पनि दिएको एनसेलले विदेशमा नोपलबाट ठूलो धनराशी पठाएको छ।

सेवासंगै मेवा पनि दिएको एनसेलले केहि विवाद यस्ता पनि भोग्यो, जुन नेपालको कानूनको प्रत्यक्ष उल्लङ्घन र राज्यविरुद्ध गरेको एकखाले अपराध नै हो। कर छली विवाद लामो समयसम्म लम्बिदा एनसेलले आफ्ना भौतिक संरचनामा क्षति व्यहोर्ने स्थिति बन्यो। अझं, तत्कालीन विप्लव नेतृत्वको नेकपाले एनसेलको कार्यालयमा बम विस्फोट गराएपछि सेक्युरिटी गार्डले ज्यान नै दिने स्थिति बन्यो। यसरी देशभरका विभिन्न क्षेत्रका भौतिक संरचनामा किन आक्रमण भए? यसका पछाडी कारण हुन्, एनसेलले नेपालको कानून पालना गर्न भन्दा बढि मुनाफा आर्जन गर्ने ध्येय राख्नु।

सेयर खरिदबिक्रीको घोटाला

एनसेलले गरेको सेयर खरिदबिक्री भने अस्वभाविकमात्रै थिएन, सार्वभौम मुलुकको स्वाधिनतामाथिको प्रहार नै थियो। नेपालले निर्माण गरेको कानून व्यवसायमैत्री थिएन भनेपनि त्यो कानून नेपालको सार्वभौमसत्तासंग जोडिएको विषय थियो।

नेपालको संसदले निर्माण गरेको कानून नेपालभित्र सबैलाई मान्य र बाध्यकारी हुन्छ। तर, एनसेलको हकमा यो लागू नहुने गरि गरिएको सेयर खरिदबिक्रीमा सर्वोच्चको झड्कापछि भने नेपालले आफ्नो कानूनको पालना निर्वाध गराउनसक्छ भन्ने प्रष्ट सन्देश दिएको छ ।

सेयर खरिदबिक्री अमान्य

सर्वोच्च अदालतका न्यायाधीशद्वय सपना प्रधान मल्ल र टेकप्रसाद ढुंगानाको संयुक्त इजलासले विवादास्पद सेयर खरिदबिक्रीलाई अमान्य र अस्वभाविक भन्दै खारेज गरिदिएको छ।

यसले एनसेलको अध्यक्ष बन्न पुगेका सतिसलाल आचार्य अब कर्मचारीको हैसियतमा पुगेका छन भने एनसेलको सेयर स्वामित्व रेनोल्ड होल्डिङ्स लिमिटेडको वास्तविक मालिक मलेसियन कम्पनी आजियाटाकै रहेको ठहर गरेको छ। सतिसलालको कम्पनी स्पेक्ट्रलाइट युकेले किनेको भनिएको ८० प्रतिशत सेयर अमान्य भएको छ ।

के भन्यो सर्वोच्चले ?

सर्वोच्च अदालतले एनसेलको सेयर स्वामित्व ६ अर्ब हाराहारीमा भएको कारोबारलाई अमान्य र अस्वभाविक भनेको छ । अदालतले सन् २०१६ मा करिब १ खर्ब ४३ अर्ब रुपैयाँमा खरिद गरिएको शेयरलाई अत्यन्तै न्यून मूल्यमा किनबेच गरिएको भन्नुलाई नै कानूनको उल्लङ्घनको रुपमा ठहर गरेको हो। सर्वोच्चले आदेशमा भनेको छ, ’शेयर खरीद बिक्री कारोबारको बारेमा विदेशी लगानी तथा प्रविधि हस्तान्तरण ऐन, २०७५ को दफा १९ को अभिलेख राख्ने व्यवस्थासँग आफूलाई अनुमति दिने, नियमन गर्ने विशेष कानूनको रूपमा रहेको दुर सञ्चार नियमावली, २०५४ को नियम १५ (१) (ट) को व्यवस्थालाई नजरअन्दाज गर्न मिल्ने देखिएन ।

प्रस्तुत संशोधित ऐ. नियम १५ ( १ ) (ट) तथा नेपाल दुर सञ्चार प्राधिकरण ( अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त व्यक्तिको शेयर खरीद बिक्री) विनियमावली, २०७६ को विनियम (१), (३) र विनियम ४ को खण्ड (क) लाई चुनौति दिएको अवस्था पनि रहेको छैन । अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त व्यक्ति विपक्षी एनसेल आजियाटा लिमिटेडको ८०% शेयर धारण गर्ने शेयरवाला आजियाटा इन्भेष्टमेन् (यु.के.) लिमिटेडले आफ्नो शेयर स्पेक्ट्रलाइट यु.के. लिमिटेडलाई मिति २०८० । ८ । १५ (तदनुसार १ डिसेम्बर २०२३) मा बिक्री गरेको तथ्यमा विवाद देखिदैन । उक्त शेयर कारोवार हुनु अगावै नेपाल दुर सञ्चार प्राधिकरणबाट पूर्व स्वीकृति लिनुपर्नेमा नलिएको, विपक्षीबाट पेस भएको लिखित जवाफमा शेयरधनीको शेयर खरीद बिक्री हुँदा प्राधिकरणबाट स्वीकृति लिनुपर्ने व्यवस्था नै छैन भन्ने जिकिर लिएको र मिति २०८० । ८ । १५ (तदनुसार डिसेम्वर १ सन् २०२३) मा भएको शेयर खरीद बिक्री सम्झौताको सम्बन्धमा मिति २०८०।११।१२ मा मात्र स्वीकृतिको लागि प्राधिकरणमा निवेदन पेस गरेको स्थिति देखिएकाले विपक्षी एनसेल आजियाटा लिमिटेडले दुर सञ्चार ऐन, २०५३, दुर सञ्चार नियमावली, २०५४ र नेपाल दुर सञ्चार प्राधिकरण (अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त व्यक्तिको शेयर खरीद बिक्री) विनियमावली, २०७६ र अनुमतिपत्रको शर्तसमेत अक्षरशः परिपालना गर्दै पारदर्शी र विधिसम्मत तरिकाले सेवा संचालन गर्नू भनी विपक्षी एनसेल आजियाटा लिमिटेडको नाममा निर्देशनात्मक आदेश जारी गरिदिएको छ ।’

यसरी हेर्दा अब एनसेलको सञ्चालन एनसेल आजियाटाले नै गर्नुपर्नेछ। यसरी हेर्दा सतिसलालले गरेको कारोबार अवैध ठहर भएको छ भने अब ससितलाल एनसेलको अध्यक्षभन्दा पनि कर्मचारी वा अन्य हैसियतमा पुग्ने भएका छन्।

अब सरकारीकरणको बाटो खुला

नेपालको दूरसञ्चार ऐनले निश्वित अवधिपछि निश्चित कानूनी बाटो पुरा नगरेमा टेलिकम कम्पनी नेपाल सरकारको नाममा स्वतः आउने व्यवस्था गरेको छ। जसअनुसार दूरसञ्चार ऐन, २०५३ को दफा ३३ अनुसार ५० प्रतिशतभन्दा बढी विदेशी लगानी भएका दूरसञ्चार कम्पनीहरूको अनुमतिपत्रको २५ वर्षे अवधि समाप्त भएपछि त्यसको स्वामित्व स्वतः नेपाल सरकारमा हस्तान्तरण हुने व्यवस्था गरेको छ ।

एनसेलले १६ भदौ २०६१ मा अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त गरेकाले १५ भदौ २०८६ मा यसको २५ वर्षे अवधि पुरा हुनेछ । जुन अवधिपछि एनसेलको सेयर स्वामित्वमा वैध वदलाव नआएमा सरकारीकरणको चरणमा प्रवेश गर्ने निश्वित छ ।

उसोतः एनसेल प्रकरणमा नेपाल प्रहरीको केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्यूरो (सीआइबी)ले ठगी, आपराधिक विश्वासघात जस्ता विषयमा अनुसन्धान भने गरिरहेको छ। सर्वोच्चले एनसेलको सेयर स्वामित्व सरकारको नाममा आउने बाटो खुला गरिदिएपनि कानूनी बाटाहरु कसरी अघि बढ्छन्? सरकारी नीति कस्ता बन्छन भन्ने विषयले समेत यो विषयमा थप निर्धारण गर्नेछ ।

अमरेशको सक्रियता

तत्कालीन समयमा स्वतन्त्र रुपमा प्रतिनिधिसभामा निर्वाचित भएका अमरेशकुमार सिंहले एनसेलको सेयर खरिदबिक्रीलाई चुनौती दिदै सर्वोच्चमा रिट दर्ता गराए। अमरेश अहिले राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टीबाट कांग्रेस सभापति गगन थापालाई पराजित गर्दै फेरि सर्लाही निर्वाचन क्षेत्र नम्बर ४ बाट प्रतिनिधिसभा सदस्यमा निर्वाचित भइसकेका छन्।

उनै सिंहले सर्वोच्चमा एनसेल आजियाटा, दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरण, प्रधानमन्त्री कार्यालय, ठूला करदाता कार्यालय, कम्पनी रजिष्ट्रार जस्ता धेरै निकायलाई विपक्षी बनाएर रिट दर्ता गराएका थिए। यहि प्रकरणमा सर्वोच्चको फैसलाले एनसेलको सेयर खरिदबिक्रीलाई अवैध ठहर गरेको हो।

निर्णय अब सरकारको हातमा

नेपालमा विदेशी लगानीका सम्बन्धमा अनेक अफवाहहरु फैलिने गर्छन्। कतिपयले एनसेल प्रकरणले नेपालमा ठूला लगानी नआउने भन्दै यसलाई मोड्ने प्रयास समेत गरेको देखिन्छ। सरकारले पनि मध्यम वर्गलाई ठूलो प्रभाव पर्ने गरि काम गरिरहेको बेला विदेशी लगानीलाई नेपालको कानूनको पालना गर्ने र विवादको समाधानका निम्ति सहजीकरणको बाटो खोज्दै काम गर्ने वातावरण सिर्जना गर्नुपर्ने देखिन्छ ।

एनसेल कब्जा गर्ने सतिसलालसहितको टोलीले नै स्मार्ट टेलिकमको सम्पत्ति कौडीको भाउमा लिलाम सकारेको घटनाबाटै सरकारले कानूनको पालना गराउने र आवश्यक सहजीकरणसहित दण्ड र पुरस्कारको व्यवस्था गर्न आवश्यक देखिन्छ। तर, सरकारले यस्ता विषयलाई कसरी अघि लैजान्छ भन्ने चासो र केहि शंकाहरु भने देखिन्छन। यद्यपी अब कानूनविपरितका विषयलाई दण्ड र विदेशी लगानीलाई प्रोत्साहन गर्ने गरि काम गर्नुको विकल्प भने देखिन्न ।

articles.title: कोलकाताबाट २४ घण्टामै नेपालमा ढुवानी, व्यवसायी उत्साहित
articles.summary:
मोरङ । उद्घाटन भएको करिब ३ वर्षपछि विराटनगरस्थित एकीकृत जाँच चौकीसम्म कार्गो रेलको सेवा पुनः शुरु भएको छ । पारवहन सन्धीको प्रोटोकल संसोधन पछि विराटनगरको एकीकृत जाँच चौकीस्थित नेपालको कस्टम यार्डसम्म कार्गो रेल आएको हो ।

विराटनगर स्थित एकिकृत जाँच चौकीसम्म कार्गो रेलको सेवा पुनः शुरु भएको छ । तत्कालिन प्रधानमन्त्री पुष्पकमल दाहाल प्रचण्ड र भारतका प्रधानमन्त्री नरेन्द्र मोदीले २०८० साल जेठ १८ गते उद्घाटन गरेयता कार्गो रेल आउन सकेको थिएन ।

मोरङको नेमुवास्थित स्वस्तिक आयल इण्डष्ट्रिजले मगाएको तोरी बोकेका ४० वटा कन्टेनरसहितको कार्गो रेल नेपाल भंसार यार्डसम्म आएको हो । रेल आएपछि सुनसरी मोरङ औद्योगिक करिडोरका उद्योगी व्यवसायीहरु उत्साहित भएका छन् ।

कार्गो रेलबाट ढुवानी गर्दा ढुवानी लागत २५ देखि ३० प्रतिशत घट्ने, कोलकाता बन्दरगाहबाट विराटनगरसम्म २४ घण्टामा सामान आईपुग्ने र बाटोमा सामान चोरी हुने समस्या निराकरण हुने भएकाले अन्य क्षेत्रका उद्योगहरुसँग प्रतिस्पर्धा गर्न सहज हुने उद्योगी व्यवसायीहरुले बताएका छन् ।

भारत सरकार अन्र्तर्गतको कन्कोर अर्थात कन्टेनर कर्पोरेशन अफ इण्डिया लिमिटेडको कार्गाे रेलबाट सोमवार एनसिवाई अर्थात नेपाल कस्टम यार्ड सम्म मालवाहक रेल आएको हो ।

कन्कोरका प्रतिनिधि संजिव साहले हप्तामा दुई दिन कोलकाताबाट विराटनगरसम्म कार्गो रेल संचालन गर्ने र यसलाई आवश्यकता अनुसार बढाउदै लैजाने जानकारी दिए ।

पारवहन सन्धीको प्रोटोकल संसोधनपछि विराटनगरको एकीकृत जाँच चौकीस्थित नेपाल कस्टम यार्डसम्म कार्गो रेल आएको हो । कार्गो रेल संचालन पछि विराटनगर आएको कन्टेनर खाली फर्कने भएकाले यहाँबाट वस्तु निर्यातमा पनि सहजता आउने उद्योगी व्यवसायीहरुले बताएका छन् ।

articles.title: प्युजो मोटरसाइकल्स नेपालद्वारा ‘Soirée Francaise’ आयोजना: फ्रान्सेली संस्कृति र जीवनशैलीको अनुभव
articles.summary:
अग्नि ग्रुप अन्तर्गतको प्युजो मोटरसाइकल्स नेपालले ‘Soirée Française – A Night of French Elegance’ शीर्षकमा एक विशेष 'फ्रेन्च फाइन डाइनिङ' कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न गरेको छ। काठमाडौँस्थित ला टेरास (La Terrasse) मा आयोजना गरिएको उक्त कार्यक्रममा प्युजोका विशिष्ट ग्राहक, व्यावसायिक साझेदार तथा फ्रान्सेली संस्कृतिप्रति आत्मियता राख्ने अतिथिहरूको उपस्थिति रहेको थियो।

कार्यक्रमले फ्रान्सको समृद्ध सांस्कृतिक विरासत र त्यसको प्रेरणादायी भावनालाई सम्मान गर्दै आपसी सम्बन्धलाई अझ सुदृढ बनाउने उद्देश्य राखेको थियो।

विश्वकपमा फ्रान्सेली टोलीको भावनाबाट प्रेरित

सन् २०२६ को फिफा विश्वकपमा फ्रान्सेली टोलीले प्रदर्शन गरेको समर्पण, दृढता, उत्कृष्टता र एकताको भावनाबाट प्रेरित भई यो कार्यक्रम आयोजना गरिएको हो। खेलको नतिजाभन्दा माथि उठेर फ्रान्सेली खेल संस्कृतिको अदम्य भावना र त्यसको विरासतलाई सम्मान गर्नु कार्यक्रमको मुख्य पक्ष थियो। यी मूल्यहरू प्युजो ब्रान्डको दीर्घकालीन पहिचानसँग समेत मेल खाने भएकाले सोही भावनालाई कार्यक्रममा प्रतिबिम्बित गरिएको थियो।

नेटवर्किङ र प्रिमियम जीवनशैलीको अनुभव

कार्यक्रममा सहभागी अतिथिहरूले पेरिस-प्रेरित आकर्षक सजावट तथा आत्मीय वातावरणमा विविध परम्परागत फ्रेन्च परिकारको स्वाद लिँदै नेटवर्किङको अनुभव सँगालेका थिए। प्युजोको फ्रान्सेली सम्पदालाई झल्काउँदै आफ्ना ग्राहकहरूप्रति कृतज्ञता व्यक्त गर्न र नेपालमा प्युजो समुदायसँगको सम्बन्धलाई अझ मजबुत बनाउन यस अवसरले सहयोग पुर्‍याएको कम्पनीले जनाएको छ।

ग्राहक केन्द्रित प्रतिबद्धता

यस अवसरमा प्युजो मोटरसाइकल्स नेपालका प्रतिनिधिहरूले गुणस्तरीय गतिशीलता (मोबिलिटी) समाधानका साथै ग्राहकलाई अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय स्तरको जीवनशैली अनुभव प्रदान गर्ने र विश्वव्यापी रूपमा प्युजोले प्रतिनिधित्व गर्ने मूल्य एवम् परम्परालाई निरन्तर अघि बढाउने प्रतिबद्धता पुनः व्यक्त गरे।

कार्यक्रमको समापन फ्रान्सेली संस्कृति, मित्रता र उत्कृष्टताको साझा भावनाप्रति सम्मान व्यक्त गर्दै ‘टोस्ट’ (Toast) का साथ गरिएको थियो। सहभागीहरूले यस अविस्मरणीय अनुभवले प्युजो मोटरसाइकल्स नेपाल र ग्राहकहरूबीचको प्रिमियम सम्बन्धलाई अझ सुदृढ बनाएको विश्वास व्यक्त गरेका छन्

articles.title: राष्ट्रिय इन्जिनियर दिवस घोषणा गर्न इन्जिनियर्स एसोसियसनको माग
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपाल इन्जिनियर्स एसोसियसनका अध्यक्ष सुवासचन्द्र बरालले प्रत्येक वर्ष साउन ३ गते मनाइने इन्जिनियर दिवसलाई सरकारले औपचारिक रूपमा ‘राष्ट्रिय इन्जिनियर दिवस’ घोषणा गरी सरकारी क्यालेन्डरमा समावेश गर्न आग्रह गरेका छन्।

एसोसियसनको ६४औँ इन्जिनियर दिवस समारोहलाई सम्बोधन गर्दै अध्यक्ष बरालले पूर्वाधार र प्रविधि कुनै पनि राष्ट्रको आर्थिक विकास र समृद्धिको मेरुदण्ड भएको उल्लेख गर्दै इन्जिनियरिङ क्षेत्रलाई प्राथमिकतामा राखेर राज्यले दीर्घकालीन नीति अवलम्बन गर्नुपर्ने बताए।

उनका अनुसार नेपालमा दर्ता भएका करिब एक लाख इन्जिनियरमध्ये करिब ६० प्रतिशत युवा छन्। तर पर्याप्त रोजगारी र अवसरको अभावका कारण ठूलो संख्यामा दक्ष जनशक्ति विदेश पलायन भइरहेको भन्दै उनले यसलाई रोक्न तत्काल प्रभावकारी नीति आवश्यक रहेको बताए।

‘युवा इन्जिनियरहरूको सीप, ज्ञान र दक्षताको उचित उपयोग गर्न राज्य, उद्योग र इन्जिनियरिङ समुदायबीच बलियो सहकार्य आवश्यक छ,’ उनले भने।

बरालले यस वर्षको इन्जिनियर दिवस 'Young Mind and Engineering: Shaping Better Nepal' भन्ने मूल नारासहित मनाइएको जानकारी दिँदै विकास निर्माणमा संलग्न प्राविधिकहरूले कार्यस्थलमा असुरक्षा, प्रशासनिक झन्झट र अनावश्यक दबाब झेल्नुपरेको गुनासो गरे। यस्तो अवस्थाले विकास आयोजनाको गति नै प्रभावित भएको उनको भनाइ थियो।

उनले प्राविधिकहरूको क्षमताको अधिकतम उपयोग गर्न पुरस्कार र दण्डको स्पष्ट प्रणाली लागू गर्नुपर्ने आवश्यकता औँल्याए। ऊर्जा, जलस्रोत, कृषि, पर्यटन, सूचना प्रविधि, उद्योग तथा मानव संसाधनलगायत सबै क्षेत्रमा इन्जिनियरहरूको भूमिका निर्णायक रहेको उल्लेख गर्दै बदलिँदो प्रविधिअनुसार सीप विकासमा लगानी बढाउनुपर्नेमा जोड दिए।

सरकारसमक्ष एसोसियसनले इन्जिनियरिङ क्षेत्रसँग सम्बन्धित विभिन्न नीतिगत माग पनि अघि सारेको छ।

अध्यक्ष बरालले विकास निर्माणमा खटिने इन्जिनियरका लागि सुरक्षित कार्य वातावरणको कानुनी प्रत्याभूति, रणनीतिक सरकारी निकायको नेतृत्व तहमा प्राविधिक पृष्ठभूमिका इन्जिनियरहरूको प्रतिनिधित्व, छुट्टै इन्जिनियरिङ सेवा आयोग गठन तथा नेपाल इन्जिनियरिङ प्रशिक्षण तथा अनुसन्धान प्रतिष्ठान स्थापना प्रक्रिया तत्काल अघि बढाउन आग्रह गरे।

त्यसैगरी, युवा इन्जिनियरका लागि पर्याप्त रोजगारी सिर्जना, विकास आयोजनाको सुपरभिजन इन्जिनियरबाटै गराउने व्यवस्था, निजी तथा गैरसरकारी क्षेत्रमा कार्यरत इन्जिनियरहरूको न्यूनतम मासिक पारिश्रमिक ३७ हजार १३५ कार्यान्वयन तथा प्राविधिक त्रुटिलाई स्वतः भ्रष्टाचारको कसुर अन्तर्गत नराख्ने कानुनी व्यवस्था गर्न पनि उनले सरकारसँग माग गरे।

अध्यक्ष बरालले नेपाल इन्जिनियर्स एसोसियसन इन्जिनियरहरूको पेशागत हकहितको संरक्षण, नवप्रवर्तनको प्रवर्द्धन र राज्यसँग इन्जिनियरिङ समुदायलाई जोड्ने साझा संस्थाका रूपमा निरन्तर सक्रिय रहने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गर्दै सम्पूर्ण इन्जिनियर तथा आर्किटेक्टलाई पेशागत नैतिकता र इमान्दारितालाई सर्वोच्च प्राथमिकतामा राखेर समृद्ध नेपाल निर्माणमा योगदान दिन आह्वान गरे।

articles.title: Parliament will be back with little on its plate
articles.summary:
The federal parliament is set to reconvene on Thursday after a fortnight-long recess, but lawmakers are returning to an almost empty legislative agenda. Opposition parties say the government has failed to provide enough business for the legislature.

The House of Representatives will resume its meeting on Thursday, while the National Assembly is scheduled to meet a day later. However, both chambers are expected to have little legislative work, with only eight bills currently under consideration in the lower house and its committees, while the upper house has no legislation awaiting consideration.

Parliament was adjourned on July 15 after the national budget was approved. Speaker DP Aryal and National Assembly Chairman Narayan Dahal had announced a recess until July 30 for the House of Representatives and July 31 for the National Assembly, respectively, saying the break would allow lawmakers to visit their constituencies. Opposition parties, however, argue that the recess was largely forced by the government’s failure to provide enough legislative business.

According to the Parliament Secretariat, only four bills are actively pending in the 275-member House of Representatives. The Nepal Rastra Bank Act (Third Amendment) Bill is under consideration in the Finance Committee, while the Nepal Special Service Act (Revival) Bill and the Rastriya Sewa Dal (National Cadet Corps) Bill are being reviewed by the State Affairs and Good Governance Committee. Another bill to amend and repeal select financial laws is awaiting discussion on the House floor.

Four other bills, which were passed by the National Assembly and sent to the lower house, are under discussion in parliamentary committees. The National Forensic Science Laboratory Bill and the Film Bill are under review by the Education, Health, and Information Technology Committee. The Intangible Cultural Heritage (Protection) Bill and the Tourism Bill are pending before the International Relations and Tourism Committee.

The situation in the 59-member National Assembly is even more limited. The upper house has already cleared all bills sent to it and forwarded them to the lower house. As a result, it currently has no pending legislation or government business scheduled for its July 31 meeting.

Opposition parties have criticised the government over the lack of legislative activity, accusing it of using the recess as a cover for its failure to prepare bills.

“The government has failed to provide business to the House. This is a clear weakness on their part,” said Basana Thapa, chief whip of the main opposition Nepali Congress. She rejected the government’s explanation that lawmakers were given time to visit their constituencies, arguing that parliament was effectively suspended because the cabinet had no bills ready for discussion.

Thapa also warned against the practice of delaying legislation and then pushing bills through parliament without adequate discussion.

“When laws on education and health taxes were rushed through on the strength of parliamentary majority, it created public outcry and had to be rolled back later. Hasty decisions followed by late corrections only erode public trust in the government,” she said.

Yubaraj Dulal, chief whip of the opposition Nepali Communist Party, also warned that the government would face embarrassment if it failed to register new bills before the House resumed.

“The law minister assured us in the Business Advisory Committee that enough bills would be registered to keep parliament busy through September,” Dulal said. “If bills are not registered for tabling when the House opens on July 30, it will be a matter of shame for the government.”

Officials at the Parliament Secretariat acknowledged that legislative work remains limited but said the legislature is not completely without business.

Ekram Giri, spokesperson and head of the House’s Business Management Division, said that apart from the eight bills, four non-legislative motions, including two urgent public importance motions and two resolution motions, have been forwarded to the concerned ministries for discussion.

“It is not that there is an absolute lack of business, but legislative business is certainly minimal,” Giri said. “We expect some bills to be registered in the interim. The government has submitted its list of priority legislation, and coordination with ministries is ongoing.”

Before the adjournment on July 15, Speaker DP Aryal reminded lawmakers that the government had declared the current fiscal year as the ‘Year of Lawmaking and Reform’. He urged MPs to use the recess to collect public feedback on policy implementation and government service delivery.

The government, however, has defended its preparations, saying a number of bills are in the pipeline and will be introduced soon.

Minister for Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs Sobita Gautam said there would be no shortage of legislative work once parliament resumes. She said delays in registering bills were largely due to the government’s immediate focus on passing the national budget after taking office.

“Eight to 10 bills are in the pipeline and will be registered in both Houses before the upcoming sittings,” Gautam told reporters.

She said the government has set an ambitious target of passing 166 bills during the current fiscal year, which began in mid-July. The priority list of legislation has already been submitted to Speaker Aryal and National Assembly Chairperson Dahal.

“Bills will now be registered simultaneously in both the House of Representatives and the National Assembly to ensure both chambers have sufficient business at the same time,” she said.

The government’s ability to meet its legislative target will now depend on how quickly ministries prepare and register new bills, as lawmakers return to a parliament where the immediate workload remains thin.

articles.title: Legal ambiguity over egg extraction from minors poses challenges for investigation, actions
articles.summary:
A month ago, a 17-year-old girl from Lalitpur suddenly fell seriously ill. Persistent vomiting, intense abdominal pain, and repeated fainting spells forced her family to seek urgent medical care. Initial clinical assessments suggested a urinary tract infection, and treatment began accordingly.

However, as her abdomen began to swell visibly, doctors suspected roundworms. When her condition failed to improve, tests were conducted for tuberculosis.

"We paid for very expensive medical examinations, but initially, nobody could diagnose what was wrong," said the victim's mother. "When nothing became clear, doctors decided to perform a video X-ray." According to her, the ultrasound revealed a swelling of her ovaries. Doctors warned that the severe inflammation was impacting her lungs and that a ruptured egg sac could prove fatal.

Recognising the gravity of the situation, the girl’s family immediately rushed her to the Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital in Maharajgunj.

At Teaching Hospital, doctors asked the 17-year-old whether she had ever undergone an egg donation procedure. She initially denied it. Her mother, hearing about egg donation for the first time, was entirely bewildered by the question. As doctors prepared for emergency surgery, the mother briefly left the ward to buy prescribed medicines. In her mother's absence, the girl confided in the medical team. "I was afraid to speak earlier, but I donated my eggs at a clinic in Lalitpur," she admitted.

When the mother returned, doctors informed her of the revelation. "Only then did I understand what had happened to my daughter," said her mother. According to the girl, an acquaintance had persuaded her, claiming that egg donation was a simple, harmless procedure with no health risks, and promised her a payment of Rs30,000.

Believing the acquaintance, the teenager visited the In Vitro Fertilisation (IVF) centre at B&B Hospital in Gwarko, Lalitpur. Medical staff administered injections and instructed her to return a week later. On June 28, doctors extracted her eggs.

Despite undergoing intensive medical treatment, the girl’s health remains fragile. "Doctors told us that if her body recovered with medication, surgery might not be needed. Fortunately, the drugs worked, and her condition stabilised," said her mother, informing that she began eating again and was discharged after a week.

Before leaving, hospital staff advised the family that harvesting eggs from a minor was a serious crime and suggested contacting police. Police officers stationed at the hospital listened to the account and directed the family to file a formal complaint with the District Police Range in Jawalakhel, Lalitpur.

"The family approached us as soon as they learned about the illegal egg extraction," said Superintendent of Police Gautam Mishra of the District Police Range, Lalitpur. "We registered a case under human organ trafficking laws and initiated an investigation."

However, the victim's family alleged that police initially hesitated to take the complaint. Due to a general lack of clarity regarding laws on human egg trade, family members had to repeatedly urge officials to act. Assistance was eventually provided after discussions with the Women and Children Cell of the police.

On July 17, police arrested Radhika Gotame, aged 21, an intermediary from Lamjung currently residing in Lalitpur. Yet, shortly after her arrest, the District Attorney's Office in Lalitpur ordered Gotame's release on personal recognisance.

"She was released on own recognisance after the prosecutors had recorded her statement, but our investigation remains ongoing," said Mishra. "We are probing the broader network involved in this racket."

Assistant District Attorney Bharat Mainali defended the decision, stating that the district court had granted remand for only two days. "Her role was primarily that of an accomplice, and her interrogation was complete," said Mainali. "Hence, the decision was made to continue investigating while keeping her out of detention."

Police sources said that Gotame was released largely because the court refused to issue arrest warrants for Dr Nutan Sharma, a senior consultant obstetrician and gynaecologist at B&B Hospital, and another individual who introduced the teenager to Gotame.

Investigating officers recovered financial evidence, including WhatsApp messages between Dr Sharma and Gotame. Screenshots showed Dr Sharma explaining a temporary issue with her Siddhartha Bank account before confirming a transfer of Rs50,000 to Gotame. Investigators found evidence of two such transactions, including one on June 28. Gotame subsequently paid Rs30,000 to the minor.

Despite this documentary evidence, the court declined to issue arrest warrants under the Human Trafficking and Transportation (Control) Act 2007. Section 4 of the Act defines human trafficking as buying or selling human beings, forcing individuals into prostitution, or illegally removing human organs. Police framed their investigation around human organ trafficking, but SP Mishra admitted that specific statutory provisions addressing reproductive tissue trade are lacking.

"We attempted to arrest Dr Sharma and another suspect, but the court did not grant permission," said an investigating officer. "Without warrants under the Human Trafficking Act, holding the intermediary in custody became legally problematic."

The victim's family expressed deep anger over the court's stance. "My child is struggling between life and death. How can the court let them off simply by claiming there is no specific law?" her mother asked. "Does a lack of clear legislation give anyone the right to endanger a minor's life? Doctors have warned that she may face lifelong infertility. Who will take responsibility for her ruined health?"

Legal experts have strongly criticised the authorities' approach. Advocate Shashi Basnet, a member of the Supreme Court Bar Association, stressed that invasive reproductive procedures performed on a minor without parental consent constitute severe child abuse.

"State prosecutors previously declined to prosecute similar cases citing statutory gaps, and courts are following the same flawed reasoning," said Basnet. "Indirectly, this is clear exploitation of a child. Charges could easily be framed under the Act Relating to Children 2018 to prosecute child abuse and bodily harm."

Commercial egg harvesting and unregulated IVF practices have triggered legal battles in Nepal before. On August 17, 2025, advocates Nirab Gyawali, Dhruba Bhandari, and Ankita Tripathi filed a writ petition in the Supreme Court demanding strict regulation of commercial egg collection. On August 19, 2025, the court issued an interim order directing the government to immediately halt unregulated egg extraction and storage and establish effective monitoring mechanisms.

"The recurrence of such incidents directly defies the Supreme Court's order," said Basnet, adding, "Authorities cannot hide behind the excuse of non-existent laws. Because victims almost always come from economically vulnerable families, these rackets operate with impunity. The state must treat this with utmost gravity."

This is not the first time law enforcement has uncovered commercial egg harvesting rings targeting young women. In July 2025, the Central Investigation Bureau (CIB) of Nepal Police conducted a major operation into illegal egg trading involving Hope Fertility and Diagnostic Clinic in Babarmahal, Kathmandu.

CIB investigations revealed that clinics extracted eggs from young women to supply childless couples, charging couples up to Rs1.8 million while paying donors as little as Rs10,000. The CIB recommended prosecuting a group led by Dr Swasti Sharma.

Although CIB initially sought to press charges under organised crime laws, consultations with government attorneys led to charges being framed under the Children's Act 2018. However, the case sparked fierce public controversy after Attorney General Sabita Bhandari, appointed by the Sushila Karki government formed after the Gen Z protest, decided not to proceed with prosecution.

Critics pointed out a conflict of interest, as Bhandari was a relative of the accused doctor and held financial investments in Hope Fertility. The prosecution waiver claimed that the minors had filled out consent forms listing their age as over 18 and that there was no evidence of forced sexual abuse or physical coercion.

Following widespread outcry, the Ministry of Health and Population formulated the Assisted Reproductive Technology and IVF Operational Guidelines 2025. The guidelines stipulate that egg donors must be between 20 and 35 years old, may donate a maximum of six times in their lifetime, and must provide fully informed consent after being briefed on medical risks. The standards strictly prohibit monetary inducements.

Despite these guidelines, the lack of primary legislation continues to leave room for exploitation, leaving vulnerable young girls at risk and health professionals shielded from prosecution.

Prashant Subedi, the operator of Vatsalya IVF, says that 30 to 40 percent of people seeking IVF treatment require egg or sperm donation, and argues that the practice should be regulated through a legal framework.

“Laws regarding this issue vary from country to country. Some Islamic countries have even banned it. However, if Nepal imposes a complete ban, people will simply travel to India for treatment,” he told Kantipur. “Instead, it would be more appropriate to introduce legislation that permits donation within specified age limits and under clearly defined protocols within Nepal.”

Noting that India introduced legislation on the matter only after extensive deliberation, Subedi said, “At present, the law there allows a married woman who has already given birth to one child to donate eggs once, and those eggs must be stored in designated egg banks.”

articles.title: Sunsari tense despite curfew. Panel begins inquiry into clashes
articles.summary:
A five-member committee formed by the Ministry of Home Affairs on Tuesday began investigating the communal violence in Sunsari’s Dewanganj Rural Municipality that left one person dead and 22 others, including security personnel, injured, as the local authorities imposed a curfew across parts of the district following fresh protests.

The five-member panel, formed by the Ministry of Home Affairs and led by joint secretary Bhupendra Thapa, began its field investigation by visiting those injured in the police firing who are receiving treatment at Neuro Hospital and Nobel Hospital in Biratnagar. Later in the day, the committee held consultations with local stakeholders at the District Administration Office in Inaruwa.

The inquiry comes two days after violence erupted at Kaptanganj in Dewanganj Rural Municipality following a dispute between members of two communities during the annual Bolbam procession.

Police opened fire after the clashes escalated, fatally injuring Om Prakash Mehta, 30, who died while being rushed to hospital, and wounding several others. Police have maintained that they opened fire only after tear gas, baton charges and warning shots failed to disperse the crowd.

The incident has triggered widespread criticism of the security response, with human rights advocates and security experts questioning whether police used excessive force and whether there was a breakdown in command during the operation.

Superintendent of Police Bipin Regmi, a member of the investigation committee, said the panel had been instructed to submit its report within a week.

“We began our field investigation early Tuesday morning,” Regmi told reporters. “As the inquiry is underway, we cannot disclose further details at this stage.”

The government on Monday transferred Sunsari chief district officer Basudev Ghimire, Koshi Province Police chief Deputy Inspector General Binod Ghimire and Sunsari Police chief Keshav Kumar Thebe following mounting public pressure over the handling of the violence. Protesters had demanded action against both the district administration and police leadership.

The transfers, however, failed to calm tensions.

Fresh demonstrations broke out on Tuesday in Bhokraha Narsing Rural Municipality, Koshi Rural Municipality and Inaruwa Municipality, prompting the District Administration Office to impose a curfew from 3:30 pm until further notice.

Under an order issued by newly appointed chief district officer Ishwari Prasad Aryal all movement, public gatherings, rallies, demonstrations and meetings were prohibited within a four-kilometre stretch on either side of the Mahendra Highway from Pakali Chowk in Itahari to the Koshi Barrage bridge, as well as throughout the Inaruwa market area.

As the unrest spread, elected representatives from the affected local governments appealed for restraint. Gafar Ansari Miya, chair of Harinagar Rural Municipality; Ayub Ansari, chair of Koshi Rural Municipality; Ajmal Akhtar Azad, chair of Bhokraha Narsingh Rural Municipality; and Bechen Prasad Mehta, chair of Dewanganj Rural Municipality, issued a joint appeal urging residents not to engage in vandalism, arson or any acts that could disrupt communal harmony. They also demanded an impartial government investigation and strict legal action against those responsible.

“We have initiated continuous dialogue with all stakeholders to maintain law and order and restore normalcy,” Aryal said, urging residents to comply with the curfew and remain indoors unless travel was absolutely necessary.

Dewanganj Rural Municipality chair Mehta said efforts were underway to resolve the crisis through dialogue, including an all-party meeting at the local level. “We are working to ease tensions through talks and consensus,” he said.

The latest restrictions follow an indefinite curfew imposed on Monday in parts of Dewanganj and neighbouring Harinagar Rural Municipality after violence spread beyond the original clash site. Nepal Police, the Armed Police Force, and the Nepali Army have since been deployed across the district. The army is conducting armoured vehicle patrols.

Sunday night’s violence began at around 10 pm in Kaptanganj after the annual Bolbam procession passed through the market playing loud music. Members of another community objected to the volume, leading to an argument that quickly escalated into a violent confrontation.

Police said officers responding to mediate the dispute came under attack from a crowd armed with stones, bamboo poles, sticks, spears and firewood.

According to police, 13 security personnel, including eight Nepal Police officers and five Armed Police Force personnel, were injured in the clash.

Police later opened live rounds to disperse the crowd.

Mehta, a farmer from ward 4 of Dewanganj Rural Municipality, was shot in the abdomen and died while being taken to hospital. Most of the other gunshot victims sustained injuries above the waist or knee, raising questions over whether security personnel followed the legal requirement to use only the minimum force necessary to restore order.

The Local Administration Act, 1971 and the Local Administration Regulations require security personnel to use firearms only as a last resort after other crowd-control measures have failed and adequate warning has been given.

Meanwhile, Minister for Health and Food Hygiene Nisha Mehta arrived in Biratnagar on Tuesday to assess the condition of those injured in the violence. She visited Nobel Medical College Teaching Hospital, Birat Medical College and Teaching Hospital, and Neuro Hospital, directing hospital administrations to ensure uninterrupted treatment for the injured.

Meeting the injured and their families, she assured them that the government would bear the necessary treatment costs and provide the required support. She added that the ministry was directly overseeing the care of those critically injured.

At a social harmony march organised in Duhabi on Tuesday, local resident Arjun Khadka urged the government to bring those responsible to justice and take measures to prevent similar incidents. The march, attended by local residents, civic leaders and Rastriya Swatantra Party lawmaker Ashok Kumar Chaudhary, followed an all-party appeal issued by the District Administration Office calling for restraint and communal harmony.

In Kathmandu, Rastriya Swatantra Party chair Rabi Lamichhane appealed to political parties and the public not to politicise the incident.

In a statement, Lamichhane warned against activities that could undermine Nepal’s religious and cultural diversity and urged people not to be influenced by rumours or provocative messages circulating after the violence.

The party also demanded an independent, impartial and time-bound investigation into the incident, legal action against those responsible, free treatment for those injured and adequate compensation for the family of the deceased.

articles.title: None of Nepal’s three major China trade points fully operational
articles.summary:
Nepal has three major trade border points with China, but for the past several weeks, neither of them are fully operational, disrupting cross-border trade with the northern neighbour and raising fears about supply of goods ahead of major festivals in the country.

While landslides have shut down the trade route to Tatopani, imports and exports through Rasuwagadhi have yet to return to normal after a flash flood swept away the bridge last year, and the monsoon continues to pose a threat. Meanwhile, only limited cargo is moving through the Korala border.

The disruption comes ahead of major religious holidays, including Teej, Dashain and Tihar. Tatopani and Rasuwagadhi, Nepal’s two principal trade gateways with China, together handled imports worth more than Rs93 billion in the last fiscal year, while Korala, which opened for international trade only last year, processed imports worth Rs14.4 billion.

Nepal Trans Himalayan Border Commerce Association said the Bahrabise-Tatopani section of the Araniko Highway has remained closed for nearly two weeks due to landslides at different locations, disrupting the transportation of goods, supply management and customs revenue collection. The closure has also affected the livelihoods of local residents, traders and Kailash Mansarovar pilgrims.

Issuing a press release on Sunday, the association said that more than 40 goods-carrying trucks have been stranded on the Nepal side since the customs point closed, while a large number of goods-loaded containers remain stuck in Khasa. The disruption has increased the risk of higher transport costs and damage to goods, it said, urging the government to immediately repair the highway, improve vulnerable sections and implement landslide control measures.

“If the government does not negotiate to open the road, the Tatopani border point could remain closed throughout the monsoon, affecting trade during the festival season. The government should make a special budgetary provision for road maintenance; otherwise, trade will remain halted throughout the monsoon,” said Ram Hari Karki, president of the association.

Tatopani and the Araniko Highway have repeatedly suffered major disasters, including the massive Jure landslide in August 2014 and the April 2015 Gorkha earthquake, which triggered secondary landslides and halted cross-border trade.

“Sunil Lamsal, Minister for Infrastructure Development, and Sobita Gautam, Minister for Law, inspected the customs point and held discussions with local residents on Sunday. A team of road experts is expected to inspect the site and decide on resuming traffic after consulting residents whose houses are at risk if the upper road section is reopened,” said Tul Bahadur Pandey, chief customs officer at Tatopani.

According to Pandey, debris from landslides has blocked the Araniko Highway at three locations. Local residents are opposing the reopening of the upper section, citing concerns over the safety of nearby settlements. Meanwhile, building an alternative route closer to the river will take time because the section is being constructed by Chinese contractors.

According to the Tatopani Customs Office, 27 to 28 loaded containers are currently stranded on the Nepal side due to the landslides. Under normal circumstances, 30 to 40 goods-carrying trucks enter Nepal through the border every day.

Tatopani Customs has set a revenue collection target of Rs25 billion for the current fiscal year, with a monthly target of more than Rs2 billion. The office usually collects up to Rs130 million in customs revenue a day, including duties on electric vehicle imports, but officials say the prolonged closure will significantly affect collections.

Pandey also said Nepal’s exports to China through Tatopani have not resumed since the April 2015 earthquake, as the Chinese side has yet to allow outbound cargo.

Though the Rasuwagadhi border point is currently operational after reopening partially earlier this year, traders say uncertainty persists as the monsoon deepens.

“Even though eight to 10 Nepali goods-carrying trucks are arriving via the Rasuwa border point, it is risky and uncertain when landslides will occur and obstruct the road,” Karki said.

Nepal imported goods worth Rs45.73 billion through the Rasuwagadhi customs point in the last fiscal year, while exports stood at Rs894.6 million. The crossing resumed partial operation in January after a flash flood from the Chinese side last July washed away the border bridge and damaged customs infrastructure. Last year’s disruption left festive consignments stranded in Kerung and affected electric vehicle sales in Nepal.

Traders also turned to Korala, Nepal’s third trade border point with China, after disruptions at Rasuwagadhi. Located at an altitude of 4,650 metres in Upper Mustang, the crossing currently clears only two to three goods-carrying vehicles a day, mainly garments and footwear, according to the Department of Customs. Korala handled imports worth Rs14.4 billion and exports worth Rs205.57 million in the last fiscal year.

Overall, Nepal imported goods worth Rs425.24 billion from China in the last fiscal year, up 24.66 percent from the previous year. Exports declined by 28.13 percent to Rs1.89 billion, leaving Nepal with a trade deficit of Rs423.35 billion.

Nepal mainly imported smartphones, diammonium phosphate, electric cars, jeeps and vans, apples, synthetic fibres, fertiliser grade, laptops and notebooks, iron and steel, textiles, and passenger motor vehicles in the last fiscal year.

articles.title: Sunsari incident exposes high-handedness in mob control
articles.summary:
Sunday’s incident in Dewangunj, Sunsari, has once again exposed the high-handedness of Nepali security forces in crowd management. A young man was killed in police firing, and nine others have sustained bullet injuries. Most of them, including the deceased, Om Prakash Mehta, were shot above the waist. As per the accounts of eyewitnesses, the security personnel opened fire indiscriminately.

This is not the first instance of the police’s excessive use of force in crowd control. Sunsari’s incident is the third in less than a year and a half. Security forces used indiscriminate force against pro-monarchy protesters in March last year in Kathmandu’s Tinkune. It was the disproportionate use of lethal force during the first day of the Gen Z movement on September 8 that led to the deaths of 19 youths, which then instigated unprecedented nationwide violent protests on the following day, resulting in a loss of life three times higher than on the first day, along with huge losses of property, including vital installations.

There are established principles governing the use of force and firearms. A United Nations principle states that lethal weapons must not be used unless there is an imminent threat of death or serious injury. Law enforcement agencies are required to use less-lethal weapons—such as tear gas, water cannons and rubber bullets—safely and proportionately. Nepal’s Local Administration Act 1971 and its regulations have also incorporated these principles. Domestic laws state that firearms may be used only as a last resort, after other crowd-control measures fail and adequate warnings are issued.

However, Nepal has neither followed international standards nor domestic legal provisions. As a result, incidents like the one in Sunsari continue to recur.

Nepal’s security agencies are unprepared for modern crowd management. Many personnel lack specialised training in crowd psychology, negotiation, de-escalation and graduated use of force. Unlike many countries, Nepal does not have dedicated public-order units with advanced training and equipment for handling large and potentially volatile gatherings.

The shortage of less-lethal crowd-control equipment is equally concerning. Years of procurement failures have left the police ill-equipped to respond proportionately. There have even been reports of police using expired tear gas canisters. Likewise, water cannons are available only in Kathmandu and a few major cities, while other essential crowd-control equipment remains scarce. The failure to procure less-lethal options such as rubber or sponge rounds, conducted electrical weapons and other modern restraint equipment has left security personnel with limited alternatives when situations escalate. To make matters worse, Nepal Police continues to rely on ageing firearms, including Second World War-era hunting rifles, that are ill-suited to contemporary public-order policing.

These are long-standing problems that have been discussed for years, yet successive governments have done little to address them. As a result, the human cost continues to stack up. Worse, every death caused by the excessive use of force deepens public anger and often escalates tensions, as the Sunsari incident has already shown by spilling over into other districts.

If the incumbent government’s assurances are to be believed, preparations have begun to procure modern less-lethal crowd-control equipment. That is a welcome step, but it must be accompanied by specialised training for the security personnel. There can be no repetition of such police high-handedness. And there can be no excuse for the loss of human life.

articles.title: Beyond the unreasonable man
articles.summary:
When orthopaedic surgeon Govinda KC began yet another fast on July 23, several words came to mind—an altruist, a stoic, a quixotic campaigner and a tragic idealist. Finally, I settled on ‘an absurd hero’ in the Sisyphean tradition: Someone who knows that goodness may not produce the desired result, yet chooses to be good because goodness, in itself, is worth doing. The similarity with Mahatma Gandhi is tempting at first glance, but neither was Gandhi purely a saint, nor is KC a sage.

Compared with KC’s 24 hunger strikes in about 14 years, Gandhi undertook 18 major political fasts, though his total over 34 years was around 32, many for objectives such as self-purification. The two men also used their fasts somewhat differently: Gandhi saw it as a form of moral and spiritual discipline as well as a political action, whereas KC focused on pressing specific public policy and governance reforms.

Gandhi was an adroit organiser, an outstanding communicator—over his lifetime, he wrote more and perhaps better than either Lenin or Mao—and an effective fundraiser. KC is a lone warrior, writes little, lacks rhetorical polish and uses his own funds for his campaigns. However, what binds them together is perhaps their unreasonableness: The willingness to go to any length to change reality to fit their ideals.

George Bernard Shaw’s oft-quoted aphorism has become a creed for innovators and reformers everywhere: “The reasonable man adapts himself to the world; the unreasonable one persists in trying to adapt the world to himself. Therefore, all progress depends on the unreasonable man.” It is a stirring line, flattering to those who refuse to compromise and comforting to those who imagine history as the work of exceptional individuals.

Yet the old saw mistakes a necessary condition for a sufficient one. Unreasonable people are abundant. Every age has produced its share of zealots, prophets, reformers, cranks, visionaries and dissidents. Most disappear without a trace: The sad fate of philanthropic physician Laxmi Narayan Jha immediately comes to mind. He was made to ‘forcibly disappear’ from his clinic in Janakpur by the Shah regime in June 1985. His whereabouts remain unknown to this day. Few remember him even in his hometown. Similarly, the radical unreason of Rupchandra Bista and his Thaha (comprehension) movement has largely faded from public consciousness.

Only a few unreasonable persons change the course of history or even achieve their specific goals of public service. The difference lies not only in the quality of their conviction but also in the world that receives it. History is less a parade of heroic individuals than an interaction between agency and circumstance.

Ideas succeed when institutions are ready to absorb them, when technologies make them feasible, when publics are willing to embrace them and when crises expose the inadequacies of the old order. An extraordinary individual may light the match, but the fire spreads only if the surrounding conditions are dry.

This is why the question is not whether progress needs unreasonable people—it often does—but why some acts of unreason become history while others become footnotes. The answer lies not in the hero alone, but in the ecology that makes heroism consequential.

Predatory state

Even after the Singha Durbar, the symbolic edifice of absolute control, was burned down in the Chartreuse Revolt, initiating a regime change, the hubristic practice of state dominion in Nepal remains entirely intact. Perhaps a predatory state is inherently an insecure state that lacks the patience and sagacity to respond to grievances as feedback to improve governance. Instead, the government views public voice—howsoever raised—as a challenge to its power.

Forms have changed, but the fundamental character of the ruling elite has remained more or less the same—petty potentates ensconced in their climate-controlled offices still believe they know what is best for everyone else residing in places as far apart as Mustang and Mahottari.

When the state is structurally deaf to dissent because its survival depends on patronage, extraction and the protection of entrenched elites rather than public accountability, even peaceful protests are treated as a nuisance, if not a security threat.

Even though the post-Chartreuse regime is full of supporters and sympathisers of earlier hunger strikes of KC, very few of his consistent demands or agreements with previous governments have been effectively operationalised. However, it will be unjust to blame any particular minister for the lapse. In the political economy of the free market, the quality of education or health is a function of cost; price is set by the supply and demand matrix, circumvention of rules is common, and oversight is often ineffective.

There is a reason for-profit medical or engineering colleges find it difficult to match the standards of the Institute of Medicine or the Institute of Engineering—institutions set up by the government do not have to worry about recovering the cost of land, buildings and other infrastructure, and have benefited immensely from scholarships awarded to their professors in the past. However, the risk that for-profit colleges will pull them down to their level remains high. KC has correctly identified the symptom and is right in raising the demand for their treatment, but the diseases go much deeper.

Apathetic society

The state of Nepal is what it is, but it’s the indifference of the comfortable class in Kathmandu to the shared grievances of the many that makes one wonder if KC is the right man born in the wrong country. KC is an exceptional professional, but a simple person. It requires a team of political scientists, economists and sociologists to frame his demands in terms of more fundamental issues of governance, such as the right to health and education, and the control of corruption in policy and practice. Sadly, he has failed to inspire any other professional body despite his struggles over a decade.

Francis Fukuyama postulated that while China had a strong state and a weak society, India had a weak state and a strong society. Like all generalisations, such a formulation has its weaknesses: Despite its imperial history and communist regime, the reach of Beijing isn’t evenly distributed throughout its large landmass. Even though Brahminism, rather than the Constitution, rules the roost in India, federalism has strengthened the effectiveness of the State in the states of peninsular India. Sandwiched between two global giants with their peculiarities, Nepal has remained a flailing state in terms of capacity and a fragmental society lacking national cohesion largely due to Khas-Arya hegemony over both.

When KC begins a fast in Kailali, there is little or no resonance in Kapilvastu, or when he announces a hunger strike in Kathmandu, few—if any—rise in solidarity in Kaski. The State can’t break his will, but society wouldn’t let it succeed over the apathy of those on whose behalf he is repeatedly risking his life.

It is easy to dismiss him as an unreasonable man obsessed with the need to check the excesses of globally triumphant market forces. But sometimes, the very sight of a lamp challenging the storm, fully aware that it will be extinguished, is morally uplifting.

articles.title: The illusion of margin lending as a financial panacea
articles.summary:
Amid investor grievances that the Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) has struggled to take off under the Balendra Shah administration, the latest unified directives from Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) have eased margin lending rules by wrongly focusing on collateral rather than the debtor. As bulls saluted a Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) landslide victory in the March 5 polls, the index tagged 2,970 on March 25, having bottomed at 2,469 on October 26 last year; Prime Minister Shah assumed office on March 27. The NEPSE closed Tuesday at 2,697, rallying from a low of 2,547 on July 14; the unified directives were published on July 15. So far, so good. The change in margin rules has benefited the bulls thus far.

The NRB’s circular relates to the existing practice of banks and financial institutions (BFIs) offering margin loans of up to 70 percent of the lower of the last day’s closing price or the 180-day average. The BFIs, made up of 20 commercial banks, 17 development banks and 17 finance companies, now have the discretion to raise it to 80 percent by scoring the companies whose shares are used as collateral on paid-up capital, duration of public life, profitability and dividend history, credit rating, regulatory compliance, and timely conduct of general meetings. In essence, the loan-to-value ratio can be increased to 80 percent for companies the BFIs deem fundamentally sound.

The latest tweak to the margin rules is a continuation of the gradual loosening of policy over the last several years. The 2020-21 monetary policy upped the amount that BFIs could offer in margin loans from 65 percent to 70 percent. The 2021-22 monetary policy limited the amount an individual could borrow from one BFI to Rs40 million and a combined Rs120 million from multiple BFIs. That ceiling was first raised to Rs150 million and then to Rs250 million; last October, the lending limit was completely lifted. Additionally, last August, the risk weight for such loans was lowered from 125 percent to 100 percent, which reduced the amount that BFIs were required to set aside to extend such loans.

Restrictive margin policy no more

In a cash account, customers pay the full amount for their purchase. A margin account uses borrowed money to gain more bang for the buck. Someone, let us say, owns shares worth a million rupees, and using that as collateral can get additional buying power through margin loans of up to Rs800,000. Share-backed loans have grown significantly over the years. As of mid-June, BFIs, which charge interest on these loans, were sitting on Rs162.9 billion, up by just under 16 percent in the first 11 months of the last fiscal year, which ended in mid-July, and up from Rs76.5 billion as of mid-July 2023. BFIs’ latest tally makes up 2.7 percent of their total loan portfolio—not huge, but not negligible either.

NEPSE’s history goes back to January 1994. At Rs4,634 billion in market cap (versus Nepal’s nominal GDP of Rs6,600 billion), the size of the stock market has gotten big, yet sophisticated tools, such as derivatives, are still lacking. Shorting, in which borrowed shares are sold and bought back later as the price drops, is not allowed but is likely to be introduced soon. This does not let market participants with a bearish bias actively take part, other than to sell. Long investors naturally would want higher prices and routinely clamour for policy support, applying pressure on the concerned authorities. Bulls successfully lobbied for the steady dilution of the NRB’s restrictive margin policy.

There are two primary issues here. First, margin debt cuts both ways. Excess reliance on leverage can backfire. Just as it helps during market upswings, it hurts during downturns. For borrowers, the advantage is that the use of margin boosts purchasing power, enhancing profit in a rising market. The disadvantage is that the borrower’s pain gets amplified in a falling market. Since these are loans issued against the value of securities borrowers own, the lender will issue a margin call once the account equity drops below the safety limit. In such a case, the borrower is required to either add funds or sell the securities. Otherwise, the lender has the right to recover the loan by selling the securities.

The second issue is the eyebrow-raising idea of determining whether a stock qualifies for more margin lending based on the company’s capital base and profitability. When a bear market hits, stocks—big and small—are vulnerable. Speculative names might take a bigger hit, but that does not mean a blue-chip entity with a solid balance sheet and dividend history will be spared. When an equity index is down by 20 percent to 30 percent, margin calls occur, setting in motion a self-fulfilling prophecy. Once a BFI indulges in forced selling to recover its loan, there will be more downward pressure on prices and that, in turn, will trigger more forced selling elsewhere—regardless of whether the stocks are fundamentally strong or not.

The focus should instead be on the borrower, making sure they understand the importance of proper management of leveraged positions and creating guardrails around that. In bear markets, it is not uncommon to hear of leveraged accounts getting wiped out. BFIs, in this regard, would not mind extending credit using equities as collateral, which is considered relatively safe. They are currently sitting on tons of liquidity—a loan book of Rs5,915 billion against a deposit base of Rs8,268 billion as of July 21. Previously, these banks heavily relied on real estate but, because the sector is stagnant, are unable to sell off the collateral to recover non-performing loans, which stood at 5.6 percent mid-June.

Banks are enablers of leverage. But they are also a breed driven by profit. In this context, regulators need to watch over both the lender and the borrower, as it is not their job to only wish for higher prices. In central banking, there are times when a wink and a nod speak louder than the action itself. The latest NRB directive can be interpreted as a veiled message to the markets that the Biswo Nath Poudel-led bank has investors’ back. If the idea is to kickstart risk appetite and help the economy through the wealth effect of a ripping NEPSE, then this may work for a while, but that would sow the seeds of instability. An unpleasant hangover often follows a late-night party.

articles.title: Nepal’s exam leak is about much more than one WhatsApp group
articles.summary:
The integrity of higher education in Nepal faced a digital betrayal on Friday. Within five minutes of the commencement of the Tribhuvan University’s Master of Business Studies (MBS) first-semester examination for ‘Organisational Behaviour’, the question paper was circulating on a WhatsApp group. A teacher known online as ‘Sulav Sir’, later identified as Sandip Singh, shared the paper and subsequently provided a 16-page handwritten solution while the test was still underway. This brazen act of academic fraud allowed at least 35 active members in a group of over 1,000 to discuss answers in real-time.

Friday’s paper leak is not an isolated case but rather a symptom of a recurring and systemic issue that has plagued Nepal for decades. From the Secondary Education Examination leaks in 2019 to the cancelled MBBS entrance exams in 2014, the history of examination compromises in Nepal is a long and shameful record.

The leak of an examination paper is a blow to the entire student community. For thousands of candidates, these examinations are the culmination of years of study and financial sacrifice by their families. A paper leak shatters the mental health of students by causing stress and anxiety. In many cases, the sudden loss of a fair opportunity drives students toward clinical depression. Families also suffer financial losses from money spent on examination fees, coaching and travel. Honest students lose their motivation to study.

In this context, the response from Education Minister Sasmit Pokharel has been a welcome departure from the usual administrative inertia. He ordered the Nepal Police leadership to conduct a swift, round-the-clock investigation. This rapid coordination led to the arrest of five suspects by the Central Investigation Bureau (CIB) within 24 hours of the incident. Only one remains in custody now. Such swift action is rare in Nepal, where masterminds of past academic rackets have often avoided investigation.

Nepal can draw critical lessons from the recent chaos in neighbouring India. Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned following weeks of mass youth demonstrations organised by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) after the NEET-UG 2026 medical entrance exam was compromised. The Indian government’s initial hesitation and delay in taking high-level accountability only served to fuel public fury and destroy trust in national testing bodies. Nepal must avoid this trajectory by maintaining absolute transparency. The university must establish a clear policy on what constitutes a compromising threshold for an examination.

The current demand for immediate resignation of Minister Pokharel is illogical. Political figures, such as UML leader Mahesh Basnet, are calling for the Minister to step down by citing the moral precedent set in India. This demand is misplaced. Unlike the situation in India where the government hesitated, Pokharel has driven a crackdown on the perpetrators. Preliminary findings indicate that the leak was carried out by a private teacher, not an internal employee of Tribhuvan University.
