A minister should not be forced out because of the rogue actions of an individual outside the university’s direct payroll. Basnet is simply trying to politicise a serious academic crisis for partisan gain.

For now, the government must set a good precedent by going to the root of this incident. Swift action must be taken not just against individuals but against the structural flaws that allow these leaks to recur. Growing commercialisation of education is a primary driver of these scandals. Many institutions now care more about artificially inflating results than they do about the quality of their students. Political patronage has often protected these academic syndicates in the past, leading to a culture of impunity.

The government must ensure that digital security of examination halls becomes a priority. This includes enforcing absolute bans on personal smart devices in examination halls and utilising signal jamming. The current investigation by the CIB must be fast-tracked to ensure that perpetrators face immediate legal consequences. Nepal needs a system that treats academic merit as sacred. Only by addressing the root causes and ignoring political theatre can the university regain its credibility.

articles.title: Madan Krishna Shrestha returns to Paleti stage after 18 years with son Yaman
articles.summary:
Legendary artist Madan Krishna Shrestha is set to return to the Paleti stage after nearly two decades, performing alongside his son, Yaman Shrestha, at nepa-laya’s ‘R’ sala in Kalikasthan this weekend.

Shrestha, who last appeared at the monthly micro-concert series 18 years ago, will perform a mix of his well-known classics and newer compositions during the two-day event scheduled for Friday, July 31, and Saturday, August 1.

Although he is widely known across Nepal for his pioneering satirical comedy as one half of the iconic ‘Maha Jodi’ duo with Hari Bansha Acharya, Shrestha’s artistic journey began with vocal music. Early in his career, his songs were regularly broadcast on Radio Nepal, as well as India’s All India Radio and Doordarshan.

Over the decades, he has produced and performed numerous popular songs, including Arabau Manchheharuma, Kholawari Kholapari, Phulbutte Sari, and Sayathari Baja.

Despite health challenges in recent years, Shrestha has remained active in Nepali cinema and music. His recent recordings, including Birside Bhanchhau Mayalu and Pahad Bho Malai, have continued to attract audiences.

This edition of Paleti is particularly significant as Shrestha will share the stage with his son, Yaman, who is developing his own identity in music and comedy under his father’s guidance. A versatile singer and composer who often creates melodies for his own lyrics, Yaman performs both satirical songs and serious compositions. His popular tracks include Yo Man Badalna Chahanna, Jindagima Sayad Maile, Naulo Basti Dekhe Jaha, and Manchhele Kina Manchhe Lai Marchha.

During rehearsals with the Paleti team ahead of the weekend performances, Shrestha recalled his previous appearance at the series.

“I sang at Paleti 18 years ago, and it was a delightful experience,” he said. “This time, having my son by my side makes it even more special. The audience has always embraced our work, and I am confident they will enjoy this session just as much.”

Yaman also expressed excitement about the performance.

“The rehearsals themselves have been so much fun; the live show is bound to be even more enjoyable,” he said.

The performances will be held at nepa-laya’s venue in Kalikasthan. For music lovers unable to attend in person, the organisers have arranged a live digital broadcast, with access links available through bookings on Paleti’s official website.

articles.title: MENTAL WELLBEING: When disappointment feels like danger
articles.summary:
For some people, disappointing someone is an uncomfortable but ordinary part of life. For others, it can feel like a serious threat. A delayed reply, a disagreement, or a simple ‘no’ may trigger intense guilt, anxiety, and the fear that a relationship will fall apart.

This fear often has roots in childhood. Children who learn that affection, approval, or emotional safety depends on obedience and achievement may grow into adults who constantly monitor the feelings of others. They may become skilled at keeping people happy while gradually losing touch with their own needs, opinions, and desires.

Clinical psychologist Ashim Sharma explains how conditional approval, criticism, family roles, parental expectations, and cultural ideas about obedience can shape the fear of disappointing others.

Why do some adults experience disappointing others as a threat rather than a normal part of relationships?

For some adults, disappointing someone triggers intense guilt, anxiety, or panic rather than ordinary discomfort.

This fear often begins in childhood. If love, attention, or safety seemed to disappear whenever a caregiver was upset, the child may have learned that disappointing others threatens connection and belonging.

Although this response once helped them feel protected, it can continue into adulthood. Even in safe relationships, rejection may still feel dangerous, making disappointment seem like a threat to acceptance and self-worth.

What childhood experiences teach a child that love or approval must be earned?

Children develop their sense of worth through caregivers. When affection and praise depend on achievement, obedience, or keeping adults happy, they may learn that love must be earned.

This can happen when approval comes mainly after good grades or when a child feels responsible for comforting an emotionally unavailable parent. Over time, the child becomes highly sensitive to others’ moods while losing touch with their own feelings.

As adults, they may continue seeking validation because they never learned to feel worthy without performing for approval.

How do criticism, comparison, and high expectations shape this fear later in life?

The way caregivers speak to children often becomes their inner voice. Repeated criticism can create the belief that nothing they do is enough, leading to perfectionism, low self-esteem, and a constant need to prove their worth.

Frequent comparison may make children overly competitive or cause them to stop trying altogether. Similarly, high expectations can produce relentless achievers or people who avoid challenges because failure feels unbearable.

Although these responses look different, both may come from the fear of losing approval. Children generally develop greater confidence when parenting combines clear boundaries with warmth, communication, and emotional safety.

What happens when a child grows up feeling responsible for a parent’s emotions or family peace?

Some children take on responsibilities beyond their age, a pattern known as parentification. Instead of being cared for, they may manage a parent’s emotions, calm conflicts, or look after younger siblings.

They often suppress their own needs and become highly alert to other people’s moods. Over time, this can lead to anxiety, difficulty setting boundaries, and a habit of pleasing others to avoid conflict or rejection.

Even when no danger is present, their nervous system may continue acting as though keeping everyone happy is necessary for safety.

Can being praised as ‘obedient’, ‘mature’, or ‘easy’ make a child ignore their own needs?

Praise becomes harmful when children receive approval mainly for being convenient. Those praised as ‘obedient’ may later struggle to disagree or say no, while children labelled ‘mature’ may take on responsibilities too early.

Similarly, being called ‘easy’ or ‘low maintenance’ can teach children to hide pain and avoid asking for help. If they are not allowed to express disagreement safely at home, they may find it harder to defend themselves in relationships, workplaces, and other situations later in life.

Healthy assertiveness begins when children are given space to express themselves without fearing rejection.

How does the fear of disappointing others appear in adult relationships, workplaces, and major decisions?

In relationships, people who fear disappointing others may apologise excessively, avoid conflict, and hide their needs because they worry mistakes will lead to rejection. This can make genuine emotional intimacy difficult.

At work, they may hesitate to negotiate, share ideas, or challenge unfair decisions, even when they are capable. Major choices may also be guided by what will upset others least rather than what they truly want.

Over time, this can lead to indecisiveness, dependence on approval, excessive self-reliance, and a life shaped more by others’ expectations than personal fulfilment.

Why do people feel guilty after setting a reasonable boundary or saying no?

For people who learned that being ‘good’ meant putting others first, saying no can feel selfish or wrong. Even when they understand that a boundary is reasonable, they may still experience intense guilt.

This reaction often comes from old conditioning. Their nervous system may interpret disagreement as a threat of rejection or loss of love.

Healthy boundaries protect relationships from resentment. They allow people to give freely, rather than out of fear or obligation.

How can the fear of disappointing others lead to resentment, burnout, and a loss of identity?

Neglected needs do not disappear. Over time, constant self-sacrifice can lead to resentment, especially when people give more than they can sustain without expressing their limits.

It can also cause burnout, leaving them mentally, physically, and emotionally exhausted.

The deepest cost may be a loss of identity. When life revolves around pleasing others, there is little room to explore personal values, needs, or desires. External roles and labels may provide belonging, but they should not replace a person’s own sense of self.

In the Nepali context, how do ideas about family duty, obedience, and parental sacrifice reinforce this pattern?

Nepali culture values family responsibility, respect for elders, and collective wellbeing. These values can offer support and belonging, but problems arise when they become rigid or fear-based.

Messages such as ‘do not answer back’ or ‘what will people say?’ may teach children to suppress their needs and treat parental sacrifice as a debt. Personal choices can then feel like betrayal, while family reputation becomes more important than speaking up against unfairness or mistreatment.

Respect should not require silence. Healthy family relationships should also allow confidence, autonomy, and the freedom to question injustice.

How can adults unlearn this fear without feeling selfish, ungrateful, or disconnected from family?

Healing begins by recognising when guilt or people-pleasing comes from old survival patterns rather than the present. Asking, “Is this today’s problem, or yesterday’s fear?” can help create distance from those reactions.

Practising small, respectful boundaries teaches the nervous system that disagreement does not always lead to rejection. Self-compassion also matters, especially when people learn to care for themselves as they would for their younger selves.

Understanding personal emotions, values, and desires helps rebuild a stable identity. The goal is not to stop caring for others, but to give freely rather than from fear or obligation. Disappointing people sometimes is part of living honestly; losing yourself to avoid it carries a greater cost.

articles.title: SKINCARE: Navigating skin reactions triggered by UV rays
articles.summary:
The heat of summer is currently at its peak in Nepal. When the temperature soars in the season, so do the skincare worries. With oily skin, acne flare-ups and irritations, there is one more issue that adds on to the list—that is, photosensitivity. It is when your skin is exposed to UV radiation that you develop an itchy red rash. Although its severity might be heightened during the summer, people who are prone to photosensitivity should take precautions throughout the year, as UV rays are present in every season.

Dr Tapan Pradhan, co-founder and director of Kayakalpa skin and hair clinic shares the causes of photosensitivity and simple preventive tips. He is also a dermatologist at Aavaran Skin and Hair Clinic.

What is photosensitivity, and what are its most common causes?

In simple terms, photosensitivity can be understood as an abnormal immune system reaction to sunlight or UV rays. Mostly, it forms red rashes, patches, skin discolouration and blisters around your skin. There is not a specific type of reaction and it can vary from person to person. Along with sunlight, tanning beds can also trigger photosensitive reactions.

But medical conditions and certain products can also be attributed to its causes:

Lupus erythematosus

Photoeczemas,

Porphyria (a rare metabolic disorder)

Polymorphic light eruption (PMLE) — the most common form

Xeroderma pigmentosum (a genetic condition)

Certain antibiotics, diuretics, and antifungals

Chemotherapy drugs

Nutritional deficiencies (B3 vitamin)

How can people tell the difference between photosensitivity and a regular sunburn?

This is a common misconception most people have. Anyone can develop a sunburn after staying outside for too long. But a photosensitivity reaction only happens to some people. It is not that uncommon in Nepal, and I have seen such persistence in long durations with many of my clients too; however, not everyone is prone to it.

Sunburn takes time to become visible, while a photosensitive reaction can develop within minutes to a few hours after sun exposure, depending on the underlying cause, the person's skin sensitivity, and the intensity of UV exposure. It is not as serious a medical concern as photosensitivity.

When you get a sunburn, your skin is heated and it can feel painful. On the other hand, with photosensitive reactions, there might be a sharp pain, similar to ant bites. Blisters can also gradually be spotted. In more severe cases, the reaction can progress to even induce a fever.

What precautions should people take to protect their skin if they are prone to photosensitivity?

When dermatologists recommend active ingredients such as retinol or tretinoin for nighttime use, it is for good reason. Applying them during the day can make the skin more susceptible to UV damage and trigger photosensitive reactions. First precaution, is timely usage of skincare products, rather than assuming that it can be applied whenever possible.

Secondly, opting for mineral sunscreens is a good option for sun protection and should be reapplied from time to time throughout the day. Remember to choose a broad-spectrum sunscreen, as it protects against both UVA and UVB rays. A generous amount of it should be applied to all the areas prone to sun exposure.

Also, as I mentioned earlier, actively searching and testing whether the antibiotics and antifungal medicines we consume have been activating sensitive skin reactions is important.

Other precautions are simple: preventing active sunlight during the peak hours of 10-4 and carrying an umbrella at all times.

What should someone do if they experience a photosensitive reaction right after sun exposure?

After you spot a reaction, I recommend immediately covering the skin part with a damp cloth, not ice, as a sudden temperature change can further irritate the skin.

If you are aware that your skin is more photosensitive, try to include fragrance-free moisturisers in your daily routine; that is helpful. Avoid scratching or rubbing the infected area.

Over time, according to the nature of the condition, steroids might also be prescribed by dermatologists to control the symptoms.

What happens when skin photosensitivity remains untreated?

Thinking that it's a temporary problem, which can fix itself on its own, is a mistake. Actively discarding the issue and not applying any preventive measures can ultimately lead to chronic inflammation, accelerated ageing, hyperpigmentation, post-inflammatory pigmentation and even scarring.

Not only that, but avoiding the sun or going out develops into a psychological fear after some time. This is a recurring problem, and people who are photosensitive might have to stay guarded with their skincare for a long period in their lives; thus, it shouldn’t be taken very lightly. Patients may develop anxiety at the thought of stepping outside, fearing that even a few minutes of sun exposure could trigger another reaction. Over time, this fear can affect their daily routine, limiting social activities, outdoor exercise, and even simple errands.

articles.title: Budget-friendly places for Nepali students in Ohio
articles.summary:
Athens is a small, scenic college town in southeastern Ohio, shaped largely by Ohio University and its energetic student community. Surrounded by rolling hills, rivers and forests, the town combines historic streets, local businesses and easy access to nature.

The university campus, downtown shops and restaurants are concentrated within a compact area, making daily life manageable without a car. Ohio University students can also use Athens Public Transit free of charge, while nearby trails and forests provide inexpensive options for hiking and outdoor recreation.

Because Athens is a relatively small town, the number of professional internships available locally can be limited. Although Ohio University hosts career fairs and attracts employers from across the country, students may need to look beyond Athens or relocate temporarily for specialised opportunities.

Oxford is a compact, classic college town in southwestern Ohio, built almost entirely around Miami University at its core. Red-brick Georgian buildings, leafy streets and a walkable uptown give it a traditional campus-town character.

The compact layout means campus, uptown restaurants, shops and student housing are all within easy walking distance. The town is also considered quite safe, and Miami University's strong sense of community brings a steady calendar of campus events, traditions and activities that keep student life active without needing to travel elsewhere.

The town's economy is heavily tied to the university, so it can feel quiet or emptied out during breaks and summer months when students are away.

ColumbusColumbus is Ohio's capital and largest city, and it's where The Ohio State University, one of the biggest campuses in the country, is situated. Rather than a self-contained college town, Columbus functions as a full city with sprawling neighborhoods, a job market, and student population that's just one part of a much bigger urban picture.

Pros:Living costs stay reasonable even with everything a major city offers, and students get real exposure to internships and employers across finance, tech, healthcare and government without having to leave town.

Cons:The scale of the city brings more traffic and scattered housing options, so building a close community takes a bit more intention than it would in a smaller town.

Cincinnati is moving to universities like the University of Cincinnati and Xavier University. The city has 300,000 people and many residential areas.

Pros:The city offers people a diverse job market. It is home to many consumer goods, finance and healthcare companies. The cost of living is on the lower end for cities of this size.

Cons:Despite its universities, the city is not generally considered a college town. Younger residents have to actively seek college-town experiences since it is not part of city life. The city is also not walkable.

Toledo is Ohio’s fourth largest city, sitting on the edge of Lake Erie. It is a city of 600,000 people and home to the University of Toledo.

Pros: The University of Toledo sits at the centre of city life. It is the biggest school in town and also the town's biggest employer. Students have a solid pipeline to work experience and internships.

Cons: As a Rust Belt city, its growth has been stagnant over the years. And despite its size, it is considered to be falling behind the other major metros in Ohio.

Based on conversations with local Nepali students in Ohio.

articles.title: Migrant workers can strike under new Qatari labour law
articles.summary:
The Qatari government has introduced a conditional right for migrant workers to stage legal strikes as part of amendments to the country’s labour law.

Under the revised law, workers can go on strike for up to six working days after notifying their employer and the Ministry of Labour in writing, but only if a labour dispute cannot be resolved through negotiation, conciliation or mediation. The provision was introduced through Qatar’s Law No 9 of 2026, which amended the 2004 Labour Law (Law No 14) to strengthen workers’ rights and welfare.

The amended law requires companies with 100 or more employees to establish joint committees made up of management and worker representatives. The committees are intended to improve workplace dialogue, strengthen consultation and help resolve disputes before they escalate.

The reforms also introduce tougher penalties for labour violations. Employers that breach wage protection regulations may face suspension of ministry services, while the Labour Dispute Resolution Committee has been formally authorised to conduct virtual hearings. Recruitment agencies and companies involved in hiring violations may face fines ranging from QAR3,000 to QAR25,000. One Qatari riyal is equivalent to Rs41.66.

Workers exercising their right to strike will not be entitled to wages during the strike period. The law also allows companies to dismiss without notice workers who organise illegal or unjustified strikes without following the required procedures or who disrupt business operations through such actions.

Companies that fail to establish mandatory joint committees may face fines ranging from QAR2,000 to QAR5,000.

Qatar has also strengthened enforcement of its Wage Protection System. The amended law gives the labour ministry greater authority to take action against employers that delay or fail to pay salaries, including suspending services, imposing administrative measures and applying regulatory penalties against repeat offenders.

If a company repeatedly violates wage rules or triggers collective disputes because of unpaid salaries, other companies under the same ownership may also face penalties. The ministry may publish the names of non-compliant companies on its website.

Workers who remain unpaid can request a change of employer or terminate their contracts, with repatriation costs to be covered by the employer.

The Labour Dispute Resolution Committee’s new authority to conduct virtual hearings means workers no longer need to be physically present to pursue labour cases. Employers, workers and verified witnesses can now participate in proceedings online.

Workers must first register disputes with the ministry. Cases are referred to the dispute resolution committee only when efforts to settle them through negotiation fail. Agreements reached through ministry-led mediation will have the status of legally enforceable documents.

The amended law also increases penalties for recruitment-related violations.

Recruitment agencies can be fined between QAR3,000 and QAR25,000 for hiring workers without ministry approval for employment contracts, processing recruitment before mandatory medical examinations or committing other administrative and recruitment-related violations.

Qatari recruitment agencies generally recruit workers in partnership with manpower agencies in Nepal, although some employers also hire directly through Nepali firms.

The new rules also require workers seeking employment in designated technical and professional occupations to obtain certificates confirming that they have completed required training and passed examinations at ministry-approved centres before starting work.

Meanwhile, Qatar has extended the non-compete period, during which an employee can be restricted from joining a competing company after leaving a job, from one year to two years. The change restores a provision that existed before 2020.

If an employee has access to sensitive client information, trade secrets or confidential company data, an employer can prevent them from joining a competitor for up to two years after the termination of employment.

The labour law amendments are aimed at modernising Qatar’s labour market, improving regulatory oversight and creating a more flexible and competitive employment system in line with the Qatar National Vision 2030. Some provisions will require additional decrees and executive regulations before they come into full effect.

“These reforms represent significant shifts that will heavily impact employers, workers, recruitment agencies and the dispute resolution system alike,” Krishna Panthi, president of the Non-Resident Nepali Association Qatar, told Kantipur.

articles.title: 67 Nepalis died in Japan over ten months, 25 killed themselves
articles.summary:
As many as 67 Nepali citizens have died in Japan over the past ten months, including 25 suicides, according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Most of the deceased were individuals who had travelled on student visas and were also working part-time.

The deaths were recorded between mid-July, 2025 and June 1, 2026. While some cases list medical or other causes, many certificates state the reason as “unknown”. Illness-related deaths remain relatively low, officials said.

Acting Nepali ambassador to Japan Harihar Kant Poudel said the rising number of deaths has made body management increasingly difficult. “In some cases, families perform the funeral rites in Japan. In others, the embassy is not informed even after cremation,” he said.

Repatriating a body from Japan to Nepal costs around Rs1.2 million. Educational institutions sending students abroad on student visas are not covering these expenses and are often not in contact with the embassy.

Many students arriving for language studies on student visas have been taking up work. However, they are not required to obtain labour permits from the Department of Foreign Employment. As a result, the Foreign Employment Board does not provide financial assistance for repatriation or related support when deaths occur outside the formal labour system.

Deaths and suicides have been reported mainly among workers in construction, Nepal-run hotels and restaurants, and supply companies. Around 6,000 Nepal-operated hotels and restaurants are estimated to be running in Japan, where labour protections such as health insurance and social security are not consistently ensured.

Education consultancies in Nepal have been sending students to Japan by charging high fees and making what critics describe as misleading promises. Japanese government data shows that by 2025, around 116,000 Nepali students were living in Japan, making Nepal the second-largest source of foreign students after China. Overall, Nepalis are the fifth-largest migrant group in Japan, with a total population of about 309,000, including 9,908 permanent residents.

According to the Non-Resident Nepali Association Japan, many students are under severe financial and psychological pressure due to high-interest loans taken in Nepal.

“Living costs in Japan are high, and earnings from 28 working hours a week are not enough for rent, food and tuition,” said NRNA Japan secretary Sachin Acharya. “When families in Nepal demand loan repayments, it adds mental stress. Switching from student visas to work visas requires language proficiency and other conditions, which are difficult. This is contributing to rising suicides.”

He said many students come on student visas due to easier access, but struggle to find stable work. “Some have to rely on money from Nepal. Many Nepalis are being arrested for exceeding the 28-hour work limit,” he said. “The Nepali embassy is understaffed, which makes it difficult to handle prison visits and related cases.”

Nepali student Uma Khatri, currently in Japan, said the reality is far more difficult than expected. “You need strong Japanese language skills before coming here. It is manageable for those who can work hard, but very difficult for students,” she said. “City living is expensive. Rural areas are cheaper, but jobs are scarce. Attendance requirements are strict, and visa renewal can be affected.”

Hira Shrestha from Baglung, who paid Rs1.35 million to reach Japan, said even working beyond permitted hours does not ease financial pressure. “People expect to repay loans quickly, but many struggle for years,” he said. Survival itself is hard.”

He said consultancy firms often present an overly optimistic picture. “They say you can study language for a year and work, but there is no job guarantee. Competition for part-time work is intense,” he said. “Some take multiple jobs to save money, which is illegal and can lead to visa cancellation.”

Only a small number of Nepalis go to Japan as skilled workers, while many enter as trainees in the agriculture and business sectors. The Nepali embassy has urged authorities to avoid sending workers under individual labour permits through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and labour channels.

In the last fiscal year, 18,744 Nepalis received labour approval from the Department of Foreign Employment, including both institutional and individual permits, with 5,800 women among them.

The embassy said it mainly tracks trainee workers sent through approved channels, where employers or agencies can be held responsible in case of death, making repatriation easier. However, it lacks records of students and individuals who arrive outside formal labour approval systems, complicating assistance and monitoring.

articles.title: Nepali workers among injured in Qatar gas plant explosion, 13 killed
articles.summary:
Nepali workers were among those injured in an explosion and fire at a gas processing facility in Qatar, authorities said, as officials confirmed that 13 people were killed and 66 were injured in one of the country’s deadliest industrial accidents in recent years.

The blast occurred on Sunday night at the Barzan gas processing facility inside the Ras Laffan Industrial City complex, according to Qatar Energy officials. The injured include workers from Nepal, Qatar, India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Kenya, Ghana, Tanzania and Nigeria. Authorities said none of the injured is in a critical condition.

Energy minister and president and CEO of QatarEnergy, Saad bin Sherida al-Kaabi, said in Doha that the incident was a “technical accident” and not linked to sabotage or hostile activity. He said emergency teams and civil defence units brought the fire under control quickly.

Al-Kaabi said production at the Barzan facility had been halted for maintenance since December 2025 and was restarted only two days before the incident. He added that Qatar’s liquefied natural gas operations, export systems and port facilities were not affected.

The people killed were Indian and Pakistani nationals, he said.

Al-Kaabi said Qatar has sufficient gas reserves and alternative supply capacity, and the country’s export commitments will not be affected. He also expressed condolences to the families of the deceased and wished the injured a speedy recovery.

Authorities have launched an investigation into the cause of the explosion, Reuters reported.

Al-Kaabi said the incident is under review, while reiterating that there is no impact on wider energy infrastructure.

Qatar hosts one of the world’s largest liquefied natural gas export hubs at Ras Laffan.

articles.title: सुनसरी घटनाबारे रास्वपा सभापति लामिछानेद्वारा बोलाइएको सर्वदलीय बैठक जारी, को को पुगे ?
articles.summary:
राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी (रास्वपा) का सभापति रवि लामिछानेले आह्वान गरेको सर्वदलीय बैठक सिंहदरबारस्थित सार्वजनिक लेखा समितिको सभाकक्षमा चलिरहेको छ।

सुनसरी घटना लगायतका समसामयिक राजनीतिक विषयमा छलफल गरिने बैठकमा विभिन्न राजनीतिक दलका शीर्ष नेताहरूको उपस्थिति रहेको छ। सिंहदरबारस्थित सार्वजनिक लेखा समितिको हलमा जारी यस बैठकमा नेपाली कांग्रेसका सभापति गगन थापा र संसदीय दलका नेता भीष्मराज आङ्देम्बे सहभागी छन्।

त्यसै गरी, नेपाली कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी (नेकपा) का संयोजक पुष्पकमल दाहाल, नेकपा (एमाले) का महासचिव शंकर पोखरेल, जनमत पार्टीका अध्यक्ष सीके राउत, श्रम संस्कृति पार्टीका आरेन राई, राप्रपाका अध्यक्ष राजेन्द्र लिङदेन तथा सांसद खुस्बु ओलीलगायतका नेताहरू पनि बैठकमा पुगेका छन्।

articles.title: लागूऔषधसहित तीन जना पक्राउ
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं महानगरपालिका १४ गाङखेलबाट मङ्गलबार सशस्त्र प्रहरीले ठूलो परिमाणको लागुऔषधसहित तीन जनालाई नियन्त्रणमा लिएको छ।

नियन्त्रणमा लिइएकाहरूमा भारत घर बताउने २६ वर्षीय राकेशकुमार साह, बारा जिल्ला कलैया ५ का २१ वर्षीय नौसाद अन्सारी र ओखलढुङ्गाको मानेभञ्ज्याङ ५ घर भई हाल ललितपुर महालक्ष्मी थान ६ बस्ने २४ वर्षीय दीपक राई छन्।

उनीहरूले भारतबाट अवैध रूपले नेपाल ल्याई उक्त लागुऔषध बेचबिखन गरिरहेको भन्ने विशेष सूचनाका आधारमा सशस्त्र प्रहरी बल नेपाल इन्टेलिजेन्स व्यूरोको विशेष टोलीले नियन्त्रणमा लिएको प्रहरी नायब उपरीक्षक शैलेन्द्र थापाले बताए।

उनका अनुसार त्यसबेला सो टोलीले उनीहरूको साथबाट डामाडोल नामक लागुऔषध एक लाख २० हजार क्याप्सुल, टाटा कम्पनीको बीएसी ७०१७ नम्बर एउटा हात्ती गाडी, बागमती प्रदेश०२–०६५प ४४८९ नम्बरको मोटरसाइकल, मोबाइल तीन थान र नेपाली रुपैयाँसमेत बरामद गरेको छ।

नियन्त्रणमा लिइएका तीनै जनालाई बरामद लागुऔषध, नेपाली रुपैयाँ, मोटरसाइकल र मोबाइल सेटसहित आवश्यक कारबाहीका लागि सम्बन्धित निकायमा बुझाउने प्रक्रियामा रहेको जनाइएको छ।

articles.title: हरेक घटना मेरै कारण घटेको हो भन्ने मेरो पूजा गर, विरोध नगर : हर्क साम्पाङ
articles.summary:
श्रम संस्कृति पार्टीका अध्यक्ष हर्कराज साम्पाङले सुनसरीको देवानगञ्ज घटनापछि सरकारले गम्भीर बन्नुपर्ने भन्दै दमनको नीति अवलम्बन गरे परिस्थिति विस्फोटक बन्न सक्ने बताएका छन् । सामाजिक सञ्जालमार्फत साम्पाङले सरकारले सुशासन र शान्ति स्थापना गर्न जिम्मेवारीका साथ गर्नुपर्ने बताएका हुन्।

उनले भने, ‘सरकार गम्भीर बन्नुपर्छ। फोन अफ गरेर बस्नु हुँदैन। सरकारले नै सुशासन र शान्ति बहाली गर्ने हो। दमनको नीति लिए विस्फोट हुन्छ। सबैलाई संयमित बन्न आग्रह र अनुरोध गर्दछु। शान्ति, शान्ति, शान्ति।’

साम्पाङले हिन्दु र मुस्लिम समुदायबीच आपसी सद्भाव कायम राख्न आग्रह गर्दै समाजलाई विभाजित गरेर आफ्नो स्वार्थ पूरा गर्न खोज्नेहरूको पछि नलाग्न पनि अनुरोध गरेका छन्।

उनले भने, ‘हे मेरा हिन्दु नेपाली दाजुभाइ हो, हे मेरा मुस्लिम नेपाली दाजुभाइ हो, सबै मिलेर बसौँ। नलडौँ, नजुधौँ। हामीलाई जुधाएर आफ्नो रोटी सेक्ने दुई–चार जनालाई छोडेर सबै मिलौँ।’

यसैबीच, आफूलाई विभिन्न घटनासँग जोडेर आलोचना गर्नेहरूलाई लक्षित गर्दै साम्पाङले व्यंग्यात्मक टिप्पणी पनि गरेका छन्।

‘यदि हरेक घटना मेरै कारणले घटेको हो भन्ने हो भने हावा, खोला, वर्षा, सूर्यको प्रकाश र जीवनको अस्तित्व पनि मेरै कारणले भएको हुनुपर्छ। त्यसो हो भने मलाई भगवान वा ईश्वरको रूपमा पूजा गर, विरोध नगर।’

articles.title: मधेशमा सामाजिक तथा साम्प्रदायिक सद्भाव कमजोर हुने वातावरण बन्दैछ : सीके राउत
articles.summary:
जनमत पार्टीका अध्यक्ष सीके राउतले सुनसरीको देवानगञ्जमा भएको घटनापछि सरकार, नेपाल प्रहरी र सुरक्षा संयन्त्रमाथि प्रश्न उठाएका छन्। राउतले मधेशमा सामाजिक तथा साम्प्रदायिक सद्भाव कमजोर हुने वातावरण सिर्जना भएको दाबी गर्दै राज्य संयन्त्रको भूमिकाप्रति असन्तुष्टि व्यक्त गरेका छन्।

उनले भने, ‘नेपाली सेना, प्रहरी र शासकहरूले त चाहेकै यही छन् कि मधेशी, आदिवासी–जनजाति, मुस्लिम, थारु र दलित कहिले एक नहोस्, मधेशमा दङ्गा फैलियोस् र काटमार होस्।’

राउतले सामाजिक सञ्जालमा द्वेषपूर्ण अभिव्यक्ति, हिंसात्मक गतिविधि र उक्साहटपूर्ण सामग्री खुलेआम फैलिँदा पनि सम्बन्धित निकाय प्रभावकारी रूपमा सक्रिय नभएको आरोप लगाए।

उनले भने, ‘आज कुनै एउटा मन्त्रीको बारेमा केही लेख्नुस्, एक घण्टापछि प्रहरी हिरासतमा पुग्न सकिन्छ। तर समुदाय–समुदायबीच घृणा फैलाउने, हिंसामा उक्साउने गतिविधिमा सम्बन्धित निकायहरू मूकदर्शक बनेका छन्।’

राउतले मधेशमा देखिने विभिन्न विवाद र त्यसको व्यवस्थापनका विषयमा सरकारको नीतिमाथि पनि प्रश्न उठाएका छन्। उनले मधेशमा शान्ति, मेलमिलाप र विश्वासको वातावरण निर्माण गर्नु अहिलेको मुख्य आवश्यकता रहेको बताएका छन्।

उनले भने, ‘अहिले जुन समाजमा हिंसात्मक द्वन्द्व रोपिँदैछ र अराजकता फैलिँदैछ, त्यसको घाउ भर्न र समाजमा विश्वास पुनः जाग्न कति वर्ष वा दशक लाग्ला ?’

राउतले आफ्नो धारणा सार्वजनिक गर्दै वर्तमान परिस्थितिमा सबै पक्षले संयमता अपनाउन, संवादमार्फत समाधान खोज्न र समाजमा मेलमिलाप तथा आपसी विश्वास कायम गर्न आवश्यक रहेको बताएका छन्।

articles.title: सुनसरी घटनाबारे रास्वपा सभापति लामिछानेद्वारा बोलाइएको सर्वदलीय बैठक जारी, को को पुगे ?
articles.summary:
राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी (रास्वपा) का सभापति रवि लामिछानेले आह्वान गरेको सर्वदलीय बैठक सिंहदरबारस्थित सार्वजनिक लेखा समितिको सभाकक्षमा चलिरहेको छ।

सुनसरी घटना लगायतका समसामयिक राजनीतिक विषयमा छलफल गरिने बैठकमा विभिन्न राजनीतिक दलका शीर्ष नेताहरूको उपस्थिति रहेको छ। सिंहदरबारस्थित सार्वजनिक लेखा समितिको हलमा जारी यस बैठकमा नेपाली कांग्रेसका सभापति गगन थापा र संसदीय दलका नेता भीष्मराज आङ्देम्बे सहभागी छन्।

त्यसै गरी, नेपाली कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी (नेकपा) का संयोजक पुष्पकमल दाहाल, नेकपा (एमाले) का महासचिव शंकर पोखरेल, जनमत पार्टीका अध्यक्ष सीके राउत, श्रम संस्कृति पार्टीका आरेन राई, राप्रपाका अध्यक्ष राजेन्द्र लिङदेन तथा सांसद खुस्बु ओलीलगायतका नेताहरू पनि बैठकमा पुगेका छन्।

तस्बिर : विजय राई/नागरिक

articles.title: Patients denied treatment as doctors across Nepal shut outpatient care over assaults on medics
articles.summary:
Hundreds of thousands of Nepalis were deprived of medical care on Tuesday as doctors across the country boycotted services except emergency care to protest against rising incidents of assaults and verbal abuses against health workers.

The nationwide protest of medical doctors was triggered by a Saturday incident at Narayani Hospital in Birgunj, where Dr Pramod Ram was assaulted. After the death of a 45-year-old heart patient in the hospital’s emergency ward, relatives of the patient stormed the hospital, vandalised property and attacked and terrorised doctors and health workers.

The injured Dr Ram was brought to Kathmandu and admitted to the National Trauma Centre. Doctors say he is out of danger.

The Nepal Medical Association, an umbrella organisation of medical and dental doctors, has expressed disappointment that the authorities failed to show urgency in arresting those involved in the incident and taking legal action even after four days of the event.

The association declared a boycott of all non-emergency services across the country, depriving thousands of ailing patients of medical treatment. Doctors and health officials at Narayani Hospital have tendered mass resignations, demanding strict legal action against those responsible and stronger security measures to ensure a safe working environment in hospitals.

“Halting medical care is not our choice,” said Dr Sanjeeb Tiwari, senior vice president of the association. “Physical assaults, and verbal abuse, on our fellow doctors have become frequent. We feel insecure as people threaten to attack wherever they find us while the authorities concerned do not provide proper security.”

Officials said that each week two to three cases of physical assaults, verbal abuse, threat to life and defamation of doctors through Youtube or other social media platforms are reported to the association.

“Over 90 incidents of physical assault and abuse have been reported to the association,” said Tiwari. “Many cases of physical attacks or verbal abuse go unrecorded, as not all doctors file complaints and some incidents are resolved locally.”

The association issues press releases only in cases where complaints have been formally lodged regarding incidents of assault or abuse.

According to the association, Dr Kamlesh Prasad Yadav, acting medical superintendent of Lamkichuha Provincial Hospital in Kailali, was verbally abused and threatened by Lamkichuha mayor Sushila Shahi a few weeks ago.

In Udayapur, the medical superintendent of Katari Hospital, Dr Gaurav Shah, was verbally abused and threatened by some individuals over a postmortem report the hospital had prepared.

In Nepalgunj, a group of people entered the premises of Bheri Hospital, verbally abused doctors and health workers, recorded videos of the incident, and issued death threats against medical professionals.

A doctor serving at the Karnali Academy of Health Sciences was verbally abused by a group of youths while he was having lunch. The incident was recorded and uploaded on YouTube, Facebook and other social platforms.

The suspension of medical services by doctors left thousands of patients across the country without care. While some were forced to return home without treatment, those who had travelled to major cities and the national capital for consultations were compelled to extend their stay by renting hotel rooms or taking refuge with relatives.

Bel Bahadur Shrestha, a trauma patient, was found waiting outside the Emergency Department of the National Trauma Centre until 1pm on Tuesday afternoon, hoping to see the doctor who treated him before.

The 59-year-old resident of Chautara Sangachokgadhi Municipality-9 in Sindhupalchok had arrived at the hospital in the morning for an examination of his fractured leg, which had metal implants and had swollen due to an infection.

“The doctor, who treated my father, sees the patient in the out-patient department only on Tuesdays and Fridays,” complained Kumar, Shrestha’s son. “We could not meet the doctor today and have to come on Friday again. Health workers serving in the local health facility have warned of gangrene if the treatment is not started immediately, and we do not know if the doctor will be available on Friday.”

Usha Yadav, 23, another trauma patient from Bishnupur Rural Municipality-4, Siraha, who underwent surgery due to a rupture of the Achilles tendon some two weeks ago, had taken an appointment with a doctor at the same hospital on Tuesday for dressing the wound. She could not meet the doctor.

“I am worried about suppuration of the wound if dressing is not done today,” complained Yadav. “Employees at the hospital asked me to visit the hospital after the doctors’protest ends.”

Along with Shrestha and Yadav, hundreds of thousands of patients across the country were deprived of treatment on Tuesday. The Bir Hospital alone provides outpatient care to around 4,000 patients a day while the number of patients seeking care at the Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital exceeds 4,000. Around 3,000 patients seek care at Patan Hospital in a day.

Officials at the Ministry of Health and Food Safety said that the number of patients seeking treatment at all health facilities across the country including health posts and primary health centres exceeds 300,000 in a day.

Meanwhile, services at the Narayani Hospital in Birgunj remained suspended for the third day in a row following the incident. Demanding strict legal action against those responsible and stronger measures to ensure a safe working environment in hospitals, doctors and health the hospital submitted their resignations collectively in protest.

Various rights organisations, condemning the acts of attacks on doctors and medics, have also asked the association to refrain from obstructing the health services.

The Consumer Rights Protection Forum said that attacks on hospitals and doctors is a serious criminal act and has urged the government to take strict legal action against those responsible.

“Attacks on doctors and health institutions are criminal acts that are extremely serious in nature and strict legal action must be taken against those involved,” said Bishnu Timilsina, general secretary of the forum.

“However, doctors also commit another offence by halting services and depriving thousands of patients of healthcare. They should adopt other creative forms of protest,” he added.

The National Human Rights Commission also expressed serious concern over the halt to health care services throughout the country. The commission, which carried out on-site monitoring of the incident, said that attacks on doctors and health facilities are condemnable acts, as such actions not only encourage anarchy but also pose a challenge to the rule of law.

The commission also stressed that patients have been affected by the suspension of services and reminded protesting doctors of the citizens’ right to health care.

“The closure of essential services such as healthcare is against the fundamental right to health guaranteed by Article 35 of the Constitution of Nepal,” reads the statement issued by the commission. “It is also against universally accepted principles concerning consumer rights, and prevailing laws. Such actions have infringed upon the health rights of ordinary citizens.”

Meanwhile, the Nepal Medical Association on Tuesday evening decided to give continuity to its protest on Wednesday as well.

articles.title: Nepal’s tiger population rises to 429, latest census shows
articles.summary:
Nepal’s population of the endangered Bengal tiger has increased to 429, according to the latest national tiger census released on Wednesday on the occasion of Global Tiger Day.

The Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation unveiled the census results in Kathmandu in the presence of Minister for Agriculture, Forests and Environment Geeta Chaudhary.

Haribhadra Acharya, information officer at the department, said tiger numbers had increased in all national parks except Bardiya.

The biggest rise was recorded in Parsa National Park, where the tiger population increased to 71 from 41 in the 2022 census. In Banke National Park, the number rose to 51 from 25, while Shuklaphanta National Park recorded an increase from 36 to 50.

Bardiya National Park, however, saw a decline, with tiger numbers falling to 112 from 125 in the previous census.

The census was conducted using camera traps between December 31 and April 23.

The latest count found 145 tigers in Chitwan National Park and surrounding areas, up from 128 in the previous survey.

Chitwan has seen major fluctuations in tiger numbers over the past two decades. Around 2000, the park and surrounding forest areas had an estimated 60 tigers. The number increased to 91 in the 2009 survey and reached 120 in 2013. However, the 2018 census recorded a decline, with the population dropping to 93.

Following Chitwan, Bardiya has the second-highest tiger population in Nepal with 112 tigers, despite the recent decline.

Nepal recorded 355 tigers in the previous national census. The latest figure represents an increase of 74 tigers compared with the 2022 count.

articles.title: Government to cut around 1,800 civil service posts in bureaucracy overhaul
articles.summary:
The government is preparing to cut around 1,800 civil service posts, including ten secretary-level positions, as it moves ahead with a major restructuring of the federal bureaucracy aimed at making the state administration leaner and more efficient.

The planned reductions follow a government-wide Organisation and Management (O&M) survey conducted across all ministries after the Balendra Shah administration pledged to reform the civil service, reduce administrative costs and streamline government operations.

According to the Department of National Personnel Records (Civil), the federal government currently has around 52,000 sanctioned posts across 1,885 ministries, departments and offices. Officials involved in the restructuring said the proposed cuts amount to roughly 3.5 percent of the total workforce, although the final number will be confirmed after all ministries complete reviews of their revised staffing structures.

The Cabinet on May 13 reduced the number of federal ministries to 18, including the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers. Following the decision, the Prime Minister’s Office instructed ministries on May 26 to identify staffing requirements based on their revised responsibilities.

Administrative reform, institutional restructuring and fiscal discipline were among the priorities included in the government’s 100-point governance reform agenda unveiled after Shah took office. Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle also announced in the budget presented on May 29 that the government would make the civil service structure more efficient and less cumbersome.

The Cabinet on July 16 approved revised organisational structures and staffing levels based on the O&M survey, allowing ministries to begin implementing the changes. The revised proposals are currently being reviewed by the Prime Minister’s Office before being forwarded to the Ministry of Land Management, Cooperatives, Federal Affairs and General Administration for final approval.

A joint team from the Prime Minister’s Office, the Ministry of Finance and the federal affairs ministry is working to finalise the remaining staffing structures.

“Some ministries still require another week to complete the review of their O&M reports and finalise staffing levels,” an official involved in the process said. “Overall, around 1,800 posts are expected to be cut.”

The restructuring will remove ten secretary-level posts, including five administrative secretaries and five technical secretaries. It will also reduce 45 joint secretary positions, including 41 from the administrative service, two from the education service and two from other technical groups.

The federal government currently has 73 secretary-level positions and 706 joint secretary posts across all service groups. Both figures will decline under the new structure.

Among administrative services, the largest reduction in joint secretary posts will be in the Ministry of Home Affairs, where nine positions are being cut, followed by seven in the Ministry of Land Management, Cooperatives, Federal Affairs and General Administration.

Four joint secretary posts each will be removed from the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies. Two positions each will be cut from the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers, the Ministry of Health, the Ministry of Youth, Labour and Employment, the Ministry of Infrastructure Development, and the Ministry of Agriculture, Forests and Environment. The Ministry of Information and Communication will lose one joint secretary post.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has proposed cutting seven administrative joint secretary posts and nine under-secretary positions from the administrative and accounts services while retaining all posts under the foreign service.

The proposal has drawn objections from the federal affairs ministry, which argues that administrative officers continue to perform important overseas responsibilities, including heading consulates general and handling economic diplomacy and labour affairs.

The restructuring will also reduce the number of districts with joint secretary-level chief district officers.

The Home Ministry has removed joint secretary-level chief district officer positions in Baitadi, Dadeldhura, Achham, Jumla, Salyan, Jajarkot, Rolpa, Bhojpur and Khotang.

Of Nepal’s 77 districts, 61 currently have joint secretary-level chief district officers. Under the new structure, the number will fall to 52.

The secretary-level position under the Home Ministry at Gautam Buddha International Airport in Bhairahawa has also been removed.

At the same time, the Home Ministry has added one joint secretary post for the newly established Department of Narcotics Control and created 95 new section officer and non-gazetted first class officer positions for the department, Tribhuvan International Airport and district administration offices.

According to sources, the Prime Minister’s Office had proposed reducing the number of joint secretaries at the Home Ministry headquarters from six to four. The proposal was dropped after the ministry argued that its workload required retaining the existing positions.

The newly established Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation will have one secretary, two engineering service joint secretaries and one administrative service joint secretary, with a total approved workforce of 90.

The Ministry of Health will lose 17 posts, including two additional secretary positions.

The newly formed Ministry of Infrastructure, created by merging the former ministries of Water Supply, Physical Infrastructure, and Urban Development, has largely retained its staffing levels. Officials said some technical positions have instead been added.

O&M reviews for district-level offices under the Ministry of Land Management, including land revenue and survey offices, have yet to be completed. As a result, staffing changes in those offices have not yet been finalised. District Coordination Committees have also not undergone restructuring.

The Ministry of Finance itself will retain its current staffing level, but four joint secretary posts under its subordinate agencies will be cut. The reductions include two positions in the Department of Revenue Investigation and one each in the Inland Revenue Department and the Department of Money Laundering Investigation.

Although the Department of Revenue Investigation is being dissolved, not all of its 150 sanctioned posts will be removed. Many employees are expected to be reassigned elsewhere, while around 100 positions are proposed for reduction.

The Ministry of Law is among the few ministries expected to retain its existing staffing structure.

Once the revised staffing structures receive final approval from the Prime Minister’s Office, they will be endorsed by the respective ministries and sent to the Department of National Personnel Records (Civil) for registration.

So far, only the revised staffing structures of the Ministry of Land Management, Cooperatives, Federal Affairs and General Administration and the newly established Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation have reached the record office.

Director General Shravan Kumar Pokharel said the staffing list of the federal affairs ministry was received on Friday, while the science ministry’s list arrived on Monday. A dedicated team has been assigned to process the revised staffing structures as quickly as possible, he said.

articles.title: बङ्गलादेश फर्किँदै शेख हसिना
articles.summary:
बङ्गलादेशकी पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री शेख हसिनाले आफ्नो ज्यान जोखिममा पर्न सक्ने, पक्राउ पर्ने वा जेल जानुपर्ने सम्भावना रहेपनि यही वर्षको डिसेम्बरसम्म स्वदेश फर्किने दृढ अडान व्यक्त गरेकी छिन्।

भारतमा निर्वासनमा रहँदै आएकी उनले आफूलाई बङ्गलादेश फर्किन जनताले निरन्तर आग्रह गरिरहेको बताइन्।

एएफपीसँग इमेलमार्फतको अन्तर्वार्तामा ७८ वर्षीया हसिनाले आफ्नो भविष्यबारे पूर्ण रूपमा जानकार रहेको उल्लेख गर्दै त्यसका बाबजुद मातृभूमि फर्किने निर्णयबाट पछि नहट्ने बताइन्।

उनले आफ्नो ज्यान जान सक्ने, पक्राउ पर्न सक्ने वा जेल सजाय भोग्नुपर्ने अवस्था आउन सक्ने भए पनि त्यसका लागि आफू तयार रहेको धारणा व्यक्त गरिन्।

विद्यार्थी नेतृत्वको आन्दोलनका कारण सन् २०२४ को अगस्टमा उनको १५ वर्ष लामो शासन अन्त्य भएपछि भीडले प्रधानमन्त्री निवास घेरेको थियो। त्यसपछि उनी हेलिकोप्टरमार्फत भारत भागेकी थिइन्।

संयुक्त राष्ट्रसङ्घका अनुसार आन्दोलन दबाउन गरिएको सरकारी कारबाहीमा करिब एक हजार चार सय जनाको मृत्यु भएको थियो।

गत नोभेम्बरमा ढाकास्थित एक अदालतले मानवताविरुद्धको अपराधसम्बन्धी मुद्दामा हसिनालाई दोषी ठहर गर्दै मृत्युदण्डको फैसला सुनाएको थियो। हसिनाले उक्त निर्णयलाई कानूनको आवरणमा गरिएको राजनीतिक प्रतिशोधको संज्ञा दिइन्।

भारतमा गोप्य स्थानमा बसोबास गरिरहेकी हसिनाले आफूलाई स्वदेश फर्किन कुनै बाह्य दबाब नभएको बताइन्। उनका अनुसार ढाकाले भारतसँग आफ्नो सुपुर्दगी माग गरे पनि आफ्नो स्वदेश फर्कने निर्णय त्यससँग सम्बन्धित छैन।

भारतीय अधिकारीहरूले प्रत्यर्पणबारे आफूसँग कुनै छलफल नगरेको र भारतमा सम्मानपूर्वक बसिरहेको उनले उल्लेख गरिन्।

हसिनाको बहिर्गमनपछि बनेको अन्तरिम प्रशासनका कारण केही समय चिसिएको भारत–बङ्गलादेश सम्बन्ध फेब्रुअरीमा तारिक रहमान प्रधानमन्त्री बनेपछि क्रमशः स्थिर हुँदै गएको बताइएको छ।

मानवअधिकार सङ्गठनहरूले हसिनाको शासनकालमा विपक्षीमाथि दमन, गैरन्यायिक हत्या, राजनीतिक हस्तक्षेप तथा विवादास्पद निर्वाचन गराएको आरोप लगाउँदै आएका छन्।

तर हसिनाले ती आरोपलाई राजनीतिक उद्देश्यले सिर्जना गरिएको अभियानको संज्ञा दिँदै प्रत्येक आरोपपछि अनुसन्धान गरिएको र दोषीमाथि कानूनी कारबाही भएको दाबी गरिन्।

उनले विद्यार्थी आन्दोलन दमनका क्रममा अत्यधिक बल प्रयोग गरिएको आरोप पनि अस्वीकार गरिन्। आफ्नो सरकारले धैर्यका साथ आन्दोलनलाई शान्तिपूर्ण समाधानतर्फ लैजान प्रयास गरेको दाबी गर्दै उनले उक्त आन्दोलन सामान्य विद्यार्थी प्रदर्शन मात्र नभई योजनाबद्ध राजनीतिक अभियान भएको आरोप लगाइन्।

भारतमा हालै विद्यार्थी नेतृत्वमा भएका विरोध प्रदर्शनबारे टिप्पणी गर्न उनले अस्वीकार गरिन्। साथै, बङ्गलादेशमा प्रभावकारी रूपमा प्रतिबन्धमा परेको आफ्नो अवामी लिग पार्टीमार्फत स्वदेश फर्किएपछि पुनः सक्रिय राजनीति गर्ने वा नगर्नेबारे पनि स्पष्ट जवाफ दिइनन्।

उनले आफ्नो लक्ष्य सत्ता प्राप्ति नभई जनताको सेवा रहेको बताइन्। आन्दोलनका क्रममा ज्यान गुमाएका सबै परिवारप्रति सहानुभूति रहेको उल्लेख गरे पनि उनले माफी माग्न अस्वीकार गरिन्।

आन्दोलनका क्रममा सरकारले लिएका निर्णयप्रति पछुतो लागेको हो वा होइन भन्ने प्रश्नमा उनले राज्यका निर्णय कुनै एक व्यक्तिले मात्रै नगर्ने भएकाले सम्पूर्ण परिस्थितिलाई अलग गरेर मूल्याङ्कन गर्न नमिल्ने प्रतिक्रिया दिइन्।

articles.title: कप्तानगञ्ज घटना : नेपाली कांग्रेसको सनातन हिन्दुराष्ट्र अभियानद्वारा छानबिनको माग
articles.summary:
सुनसरी जिल्लाको देवागञ्ज गाउँपालिकास्थित कप्तानगञ्जमा हालै भएको झडपको घटनाप्रति नेपाली कांग्रेस, सनातन हिन्दुराष्ट्र स्थापना महाअभियानको केन्द्रीय समन्वय समितिले गहिरो दुःख व्यक्त गरेको छ।

समन्वय समितिका संयोजक शंकर भण्डारीद्वारा जारी प्रेस वक्तव्यमा घटनाको निष्पक्ष छानबिन गर्न माग गरिएको छ। उनले नागरिकको ज्यान जाने र गोली चलाउनुपर्ने अवस्था कसरी सिर्जना भयो भन्दै गम्भीर प्रश्न उठाएका छन्। राज्य पक्षबाट सुरक्षा प्रबन्ध गर्न र संयमित भएर झडप नियन्त्रण गर्न चुक भएको देखिएको उल्लेख गर्दै घटनाको स्वच्छ र निष्पक्ष छानबिन गर्न उनको माग छ। साथै, शान्ति सुव्यवस्था कायम गर्न विशेष भूमिका खेल्न सरकारसँग आग्रह गरिएको छ ।

साउने सोमबारको पावन अवसरमा बोलबम यात्राका लागि निस्केका हिन्दू धर्मावलम्बी युवाहरूमाथि भएको आक्रमण र डिजे बजाउने विषयलाई लिएर भएको हिंसात्मक घटनाले सनातन हिन्दू आस्थामाथि आघात पुगेको वक्तव्यमा उल्लेख छ।

भण्डारीले धार्मिक आस्थामाथिको आक्रमण कुनै पनि हिसाबले स्वीकार्य नहुने जनाउँदै हिन्दूहरूको शान्तिपूर्ण धार्मिक अभ्यासलाई रोक्ने र आस्था परम्परामाथि प्रहार गर्ने प्रयास स्वीकार्य नभएको बताएका छन्। नेपाल सनातन धर्म र संस्कार बाहुल्य देश भएको र आपसी सद्भाव कायम राख्नु सबैको साझा दायित्व भएकोमा उनको जोड छ।
