articles.title: नेपालमा बाघको सङ्ख्या ४२९ पुग्यो
articles.summary:
पछिल्लो गणनाअनुसार नेपालमा बाघको सङ्ख्या ४२९ पुगेको छ। विश्व बाघ दिवसका अवसरमा आज कृषि, वन तथा पर्यावरण मन्त्रालयले बाघको पछिल्लो गणना सार्वजनिक गरेको हो।

कृषि, वन तथा पर्यावरणमन्त्री गिता चौधरीले सार्वजनिक गरेका २०८२ को गणनाअनुसार कुल बाघको सङ्ख्या मुलुकभर ४२९ पुगेको हो।

पछिल्लो गणनाअनुसार चितवन राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्जमा १४५, बर्दिया राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्ज ११२, पर्सा राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्जमा ७१, बाँके राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्जमा ५१ र शुक्लाफाँटा राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्जमा ५० बाघ छन्।

पछिल्ला दिनमा संरक्षण क्षेत्र र बासस्थानमा भएको सुधार, सिकार प्रजातिको वृद्धिलगायतका आधारमा बाघको सङ्ख्या थपिएको बताइएको छ।

नेपालमा प्रायः चार वर्षमा बाघ गणना गरिन्छ। सन् २०२२ को बाघ गणनाअनुसार मुलुकमा बाघको सङ्ख्या ३५५ थियो।

सन् २०२२ को गणनाअनुसार सबैभन्दा बढी बाघ चितवन राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्जमा १२८, त्यसपछि बर्दिया राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्जमा १२५, पर्सा राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्जमा ४१, शुक्लाफाँटा राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्जमा ३६ र बाँके राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्जमा २५ बाघ थिए।

मन्त्रालयले २००९ देखि हरेक चार वर्षमा बाघ गणना गर्दै आएको छ। नेपालमा बाघको सङ्ख्या सन् २०१० मा १२१, सन् २०१४ मा १९८ र २०१८ मा २३५ रहेको थियो।

प्रत्येक वर्ष जुलाई महिनाको २९ मा बाघ दिवस मनाइन्छ। सन् २०१० मा रूसको सेन्ट पिटर्सबर्गमा भएको बाघ शिखर सम्मेलनको घोषणासँगै यो दिवस मनाउन थालिएको हो।

तत्कालीन समयमा बाघको सङ्ख्या तीव्र रूपमा घट्दै गएको अवस्थालाई रोक्न र तिनको प्राकृतिक बासस्थानको संरक्षण गर्ने उद्देश्यले दिवस मनाउन लागिएको हो।

बाघ स्वस्थ पारिस्थिकीय प्रणालीको सूचक र प्राकृतिक खाद्य शङ्खलाको उच्च तहमा रहेको महत्त्वपूर्ण प्रजाति हो।

articles.title: प्रधानमन्त्रीको बचाउ गर्दै अर्थमन्त्रीले भने : सुनसरी घटना समाधान गर्न विशेष पहल गरिरहनुभएको छ
articles.summary:
अर्थमन्त्री डा. स्वर्णिम वाग्लेले सुनसरी घटना समाधानका लागि प्रधानमन्त्रीले विशेष पहल जारी राखेका बताएका छन्।

केही दिनदेखि अशान्त रहेको सुनसरी घटनाको सन्दर्भमा राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी (रास्वपा) का उपसभापति स्वर्णिम वाग्लेले बुधबार बिहान सिंहदरबारमा सर्वदलीय बैठकमा सरकारको तर्फबाट सहभागी हुँदै उनले यस्तो धारणा राखेका हुन्।

सुनसरीमा घटेको दुःखद् दुर्घटना र त्यसपछि उत्पन्न परिस्थितिलाई समाधान गर्न प्रधानमन्त्रीले पर्याप्त पहल लिइरहेका उनको भनाइ छ।

‘सुनसरीमा सामाजिक सद्भाव कायम गर्न, सुरक्षा प्रबन्ध चुस्त राख्न, दुःखद् घटनाका पीडित परिवारलाई क्षतिपूर्ति तथा घाइतेको उपचारलगायतका विषयमा प्रधानमन्त्रीज्यू अत्यन्तै गम्भीर हुनुहुन्छ’, अर्थमन्त्रीले सर्वदलीय बैठकमा भने, ‘उहाँकै समन्वयमा सरकारले यथेष्ट पहल लिइरहेको छ। राजनीतिक दलहरूले लिएको पहलकदमीलाई सरकारले सकारात्मक रूपमा लिएको छ।’

सुनसरी घटनामा स्थिति सामान्यीकरण गर्न र सुरक्षा व्यवस्थाको प्रत्याभूति गर्न सरकारले आवश्यक समन्वयमा प्रयत्न गरिरहेको पनि उनले राजनीतिक दलको नेतृत्वलाई अवगत गराए।

सर्वदलीय बैठकमा उठेका विषय प्रधानमन्त्रीलाई अवगत गराउने भन्दै उनले सबैको प्रयत्नमा साझा समाधान खोजिनुपर्नेमा जोड दिए।

articles.title: बङ्गलादेश फर्किँदै शेख हसिना
articles.summary:
बङ्गलादेशकी पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री शेख हसिनाले आफ्नो ज्यान जोखिममा पर्न सक्ने, पक्राउ पर्ने वा जेल जानुपर्ने सम्भावना रहेपनि यही वर्षको डिसेम्बरसम्म स्वदेश फर्किने दृढ अडान व्यक्त गरेकी छिन्।

भारतमा निर्वासनमा रहँदै आएकी उनले आफूलाई बङ्गलादेश फर्किन जनताले निरन्तर आग्रह गरिरहेको बताइन्।

एएफपीसँग इमेलमार्फतको अन्तर्वार्तामा ७८ वर्षीया हसिनाले आफ्नो भविष्यबारे पूर्ण रूपमा जानकार रहेको उल्लेख गर्दै त्यसका बाबजुद मातृभूमि फर्किने निर्णयबाट पछि नहट्ने बताइन्।

उनले आफ्नो ज्यान जान सक्ने, पक्राउ पर्न सक्ने वा जेल सजाय भोग्नुपर्ने अवस्था आउन सक्ने भए पनि त्यसका लागि आफू तयार रहेको धारणा व्यक्त गरिन्।

विद्यार्थी नेतृत्वको आन्दोलनका कारण सन् २०२४ को अगस्टमा उनको १५ वर्ष लामो शासन अन्त्य भएपछि भीडले प्रधानमन्त्री निवास घेरेको थियो। त्यसपछि उनी हेलिकोप्टरमार्फत भारत भागेकी थिइन्।

संयुक्त राष्ट्रसङ्घका अनुसार आन्दोलन दबाउन गरिएको सरकारी कारबाहीमा करिब एक हजार चार सय जनाको मृत्यु भएको थियो।

गत नोभेम्बरमा ढाकास्थित एक अदालतले मानवताविरुद्धको अपराधसम्बन्धी मुद्दामा हसिनालाई दोषी ठहर गर्दै मृत्युदण्डको फैसला सुनाएको थियो। हसिनाले उक्त निर्णयलाई कानूनको आवरणमा गरिएको राजनीतिक प्रतिशोधको संज्ञा दिइन्।

भारतमा गोप्य स्थानमा बसोबास गरिरहेकी हसिनाले आफूलाई स्वदेश फर्किन कुनै बाह्य दबाब नभएको बताइन्। उनका अनुसार ढाकाले भारतसँग आफ्नो सुपुर्दगी माग गरे पनि आफ्नो स्वदेश फर्कने निर्णय त्यससँग सम्बन्धित छैन।

भारतीय अधिकारीहरूले प्रत्यर्पणबारे आफूसँग कुनै छलफल नगरेको र भारतमा सम्मानपूर्वक बसिरहेको उनले उल्लेख गरिन्।

हसिनाको बहिर्गमनपछि बनेको अन्तरिम प्रशासनका कारण केही समय चिसिएको भारत–बङ्गलादेश सम्बन्ध फेब्रुअरीमा तारिक रहमान प्रधानमन्त्री बनेपछि क्रमशः स्थिर हुँदै गएको बताइएको छ।

मानवअधिकार सङ्गठनहरूले हसिनाको शासनकालमा विपक्षीमाथि दमन, गैरन्यायिक हत्या, राजनीतिक हस्तक्षेप तथा विवादास्पद निर्वाचन गराएको आरोप लगाउँदै आएका छन्।

तर हसिनाले ती आरोपलाई राजनीतिक उद्देश्यले सिर्जना गरिएको अभियानको संज्ञा दिँदै प्रत्येक आरोपपछि अनुसन्धान गरिएको र दोषीमाथि कानूनी कारबाही भएको दाबी गरिन्।

उनले विद्यार्थी आन्दोलन दमनका क्रममा अत्यधिक बल प्रयोग गरिएको आरोप पनि अस्वीकार गरिन्। आफ्नो सरकारले धैर्यका साथ आन्दोलनलाई शान्तिपूर्ण समाधानतर्फ लैजान प्रयास गरेको दाबी गर्दै उनले उक्त आन्दोलन सामान्य विद्यार्थी प्रदर्शन मात्र नभई योजनाबद्ध राजनीतिक अभियान भएको आरोप लगाइन्।

भारतमा हालै विद्यार्थी नेतृत्वमा भएका विरोध प्रदर्शनबारे टिप्पणी गर्न उनले अस्वीकार गरिन्। साथै, बङ्गलादेशमा प्रभावकारी रूपमा प्रतिबन्धमा परेको आफ्नो अवामी लिग पार्टीमार्फत स्वदेश फर्किएपछि पुनः सक्रिय राजनीति गर्ने वा नगर्नेबारे पनि स्पष्ट जवाफ दिइनन्।

उनले आफ्नो लक्ष्य सत्ता प्राप्ति नभई जनताको सेवा रहेको बताइन्। आन्दोलनका क्रममा ज्यान गुमाएका सबै परिवारप्रति सहानुभूति रहेको उल्लेख गरे पनि उनले माफी माग्न अस्वीकार गरिन्।

आन्दोलनका क्रममा सरकारले लिएका निर्णयप्रति पछुतो लागेको हो वा होइन भन्ने प्रश्नमा उनले राज्यका निर्णय कुनै एक व्यक्तिले मात्रै नगर्ने भएकाले सम्पूर्ण परिस्थितिलाई अलग गरेर मूल्याङ्कन गर्न नमिल्ने प्रतिक्रिया दिइन्।

articles.title: इनड्राइभ नेपालद्वारा ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ प्रमाणपत्र प्रदान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं, नेपाल । विश्वव्यापी मोबिलिटी तथा डेलिभरी प्लेटफर्म इनड्राइभले महिलालाई ड्राइभिङ पेसामा अघि बढ्न समान अवसर सिर्जना गर्ने उद्देश्यले सञ्चालन गरेको ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ कार्यक्रमको पहिलो चरण सफलतापूर्वक सम्पन्न गरेको छ ।

कार्यक्रमअन्तर्गत काठमाडौंमा आयोजित प्रमाणपत्र वितरण समारोहमा तीन महिनाको प्रशिक्षण पूरा गरेका १० जना महिलालाई सम्मान गरिएको छ । सुरक्षित र आत्मनिर्भर रूपमा दुईपाङ्ग्रे सवारी चलाउने पेसामा अघि बढ्न आवश्यक सीप, आत्मविश्वास र स्रोतसाधन प्रदान गर्ने उद्देश्यले सहभागीहरूलाई विभिन्न चरणमा प्रशिक्षण दिइएको थियो ।

अप्रिल २०२६ मा सुरु भएको ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ कार्यक्रम विशेषगरी अवसरबाट वञ्चित समुदायका महिलालाई मोबिलिटी क्षेत्रमा आर्थिक अवसरमा पहुँच दिलाउने उद्देश्यले सञ्चालन गरिएको हो । महिलालाई परम्परागत रूपमा पुरुषको वर्चस्व रहेको पेसामा प्रवेश गर्न बाधा पु¥याउने सामाजिक तथा व्यावहारिक अवरोधलाई कम गर्न पनि कार्यक्रमले जोड दिएको छ ।

प्रशिक्षण अवधिभर सडक सुरक्षालाई व्यावसायिक दक्षताको महत्वपूर्ण पक्षका रूपमा समेटिएको थियो । सहभागीहरूलाई व्यावहारिक राइडिङ प्रशिक्षणसँगै सडक सुरक्षासम्बन्धी मार्गदर्शन प्रदान गर्नुका साथै औपचारिक सवारी चालक अनुमतिपत्र (लाइसेन्स) प्राप्त गर्ने प्रक्रियामा समेत सहयोग गरिएको थियो ।

प्रत्येक सहभागीलाई सुरक्षात्मक हेल्मेट तथा प्राथमिक उपचार र स्वास्थ्यसम्बन्धी सामग्रीसहितको सुरक्षा किट प्रदान गरिएको थियो ।

व्यक्तिगत सुरक्षालाई पनि प्रशिक्षणको छुट्टै महत्वपूर्ण पक्षका रूपमा समेटिएको थियो । फाइटब्याक नेपाल सँगको सहकार्यमा उन्नत आत्मरक्षा तालिम सञ्चालन गरिएको थियो, जसले सहभागीहरूलाई सम्भावित सुरक्षा चुनौती पहिचान गर्न, आत्मविश्वास बढाउन र आवश्यक अवस्थामा व्यवहारिक रूपमा सामना गर्न सक्ने सीप विकास गर्न सहयोग गरेको थियो ।

काठमाडौं उपत्यका ट्राफिक प्रहरी कार्यालयका डीएसपी सुनिलजंग शाहले भने, “सडक सुरक्षा सबैको साझा जिम्मेवारी हो र यसमा प्रत्येक चालकको महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका हुन्छ । हामी सहभागीहरूलाई ट्राफिक नियमको पालना गर्न, सडकमा सधैं सचेत रहन र अनुभव बढाउँदै निरन्तर सिकिरहन आग्रह गर्छौं । सबै सहभागीलाई बधाई दिँदै व्यावसायिक चालकका रूपमा उनीहरूको सुरक्षित र सफल यात्राका लागि शुभकामना व्यक्त गर्दछौं ।”

मोबिलिटीमा महिलाको पहुँच विस्तार यस समूहका महिलाका लागि सवारी चालक अनुमतिपत्र केवल आम्दानीको माध्यम मात्र नभई आफ्नो काम, शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य सेवा तथा बजारसम्म आफ्नै समयअनुसार स्वतन्त्र रूपमा पुग्ने अवसर पनि हो । यसले सार्वजनिक यातायातको समयतालिका वा परिवारका अन्य सदस्यमा निर्भर रहनुपर्ने अवस्थालाई कम गर्न सहयोग पु¥याउँछ ।

दुईपाङ्ग्रे सवारीमा आधारित राइड–हेलिङ सेवाले चारपाङ्ग्रे सवारी पुग्न कठिन हुने साँघुरा गल्ली तथा अन्तिम गन्तव्यसम्म पनि सेवा पु¥याउन सक्छ । सामान्यतया यसको भाडा पनि चारपाङ्ग्रे सवारीको तुलनामा कम हुने गर्दछ । राइड–हेलिङ सेवामा महिलाको सहभागिता बढ्दा यात्रुहरूले आफूलाई उपयुक्त चालक छनोट गर्ने थप अवसरसमेत पाउनेछन् ।

प्रमाणपत्र वितरण समारोह प्रमाणपत्र वितरण समारोहमा साझेदार संस्थाका प्रतिनिधि, सरकारी निकायका सरोकारवाला, सञ्चारकर्मी तथा विशिष्ट अतिथिहरूको सहभागिता रहेको थियो ।

समारोहमा इनड्राइभका प्रतिनिधि तथा इनड्राइभ नेपालकी ब्रान्ड एम्बेसडर स्वस्तिमा खड्काले कार्यक्रम सफलतापूर्वक सम्पन्न गरेका १० जना सहभागीलाई प्रमाणपत्र, सुरक्षा किट तथा मायाको चिनो प्रदान गरे । कार्यक्रममा सहभागी १० जना महिलाको ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ यात्रालाई समेटिएको भिडियोसमेत प्रदर्शन गरिएको थियो ।

समारोहका क्रममा सहभागीमध्ये एक जनालाई विद्युतीय स्कुटर, तीन जनालाई स्मार्टफोन र छ जनालाई स्मार्टवाच प्रदान गरिएको थियो । यी सामग्रीले उनीहरूलाई व्यावसायिक ड्राइभिङ यात्राको सुरुवातमा थप सहयोग पुग्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ ।

इनड्राइभ साउथ एसियाकि कम्युनिकेसन म्यनाजर शेरिन एर्विना कौरले भनिन्, “हामीले विभिन्न बजारमा एउटै अवस्था देखिरहेका छौं, राइड माग्ने यात्रुमध्ये धेरै महिला छन्, तर उनीहरूलाई राइड दिने चालकमा महिलाको संख्या निकै कम छ । यो महिलाले यस्तो काम गर्न चाहन्छन् कि चाहँदैनन् भन्ने विषय थिएन। मुख्य प्रश्न उनीहरूका लागि यो पेसामा प्रवेश गर्ने बाटो उपलब्ध थियो कि थिएन भन्ने थियो । नेपालमा सञ्चालन गरिएको पहिलो समूहले तालिम, लाइसेन्स र प्लेटफर्ममा पहुँचलाई एउटै यात्राका रूपमा जोड्दा कस्तो परिवर्तन सम्भव हुन्छ भन्ने देखाएको छ। हामी अन्य बजारमा पनि यसबाट सिक्दै कार्यक्रमलाई अघि बढाउनेछौं ।”

इनड्राइभ नेपालकी कम्युनिकेसन्स म्यानेजर मञ्जिता गुरुङले भनिन्, “सीप विकास तालिम यस यात्राको एउटा हिस्सा मात्र हो । सामाजिक सोच र धारणाले पनि उत्तिकै महत्व राख्छ, र महिलाले ड्राइभिङ सुरु गरेपछि उनी प्रवेश गर्ने वातावरण पनि महत्वपूर्ण हुन्छ । ‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ महिलालाई लाइसेन्स प्राप्त गर्नेदेखि आत्मविश्वास विकास गर्ने, परिवारमा यसबारे संवाद गर्ने र आम्दानीको अवसर सिर्जना गर्नेसम्म हरेक पक्षमा सहयोग गर्ने गरी तयार गरिएको हो । जब धेरै महिलाहरू यो पेसामा आउँछन्, यात्रुहरूले पनि लाभ पाउँछन्, उनीहरूसँग आफूलाई राइड गराउने चालक छनोट गर्ने थप विकल्प हुन्छ ।”

इनड्राइभ नेपालकी सिनियर ड्राइभर अपरेसन्स स्पेसलिस्ट सुनिता जीमी राईले भनिन्, “इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ महिलाका लागि थप सहयोगी वातावरण निर्माण गर्ने दिशामा महत्वपूर्ण कदम हो । जब धेरै महिलाहरूले सवारीको स्टेयरिङ समाउँछन्, उनीहरूले नेपाललाई थप समावेशी भविष्यतर्फ अघि बढाउन पनि भूमिका खेलिरहेका हुन्छन् ।”

इनड्राइभ नेपालकी ब्रान्ड एम्बेसडर स्वस्तिमा खड्काले भनिन्, “‘इनड्राइभ ड्राइभिङ नारी नेपाल’ ले अन्यायलाई चुनौती दिँदै समुदायमा सकारात्मक परिवर्तन ल्याउने इनड्राइभको प्रतिबद्धतालाई प्रतिबिम्बित गर्छ । मानिस र समानतालाई केन्द्रमा राखेर अघि बढाइएको यस पहलको हिस्सा बन्न पाउँदा म गर्व गर्छु ।”

articles.title: नारायणी अस्पताल घटना: पर्साका एसपी सुदीप पाठक जिम्मेवारीबाट हटाइए
articles.summary:
वीरगञ्जस्थित नारायणी अस्पतालमा चिकित्सकमाथि भएको कुटपिट, अस्पतालमा भएको तोडफोड तथा त्यसपछिको विवादका बीच जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय पर्साका प्रमुख प्रहरी उपरीक्षक (एसपी) सुदीप पाठकलाई जिम्मेवारीबाट हटाइएको छ।

गृह मन्त्रालयले एसपी पाठकलाई तानेर उनको स्थानमा काठमाडौं प्रहरी परिसरका प्रवक्ता एसपी पवन भट्टराईलाई पर्साको प्रहरी प्रमुखका रूपमा सरुवा गरेको छ।

नारायणी अस्पतालमा उपचारका क्रममा एक बिरामीको मृत्यु भएपछि मृतकका आफन्तले अस्पतालमा तोडफोड गर्नुका साथै चिकित्सक र स्वास्थ्यकर्मीमाथि कुटपिट गरेका थिए। त्यसपछि जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय पर्सामा भएको छलफलका क्रममा पनि चिकित्सकहरूमाथि दुर्व्यवहार भएको भन्दै नेपाल चिकित्सक संघले विरोध जनाएको थियो।

घटनाको विरोधस्वरूप नेपाल चिकित्सक संघले देशभर आकस्मिक सेवाबाहेकका स्वास्थ्य सेवा बन्द गर्दै दोषीमाथि कानुनी कारबाही, स्वास्थ्यकर्मीको सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित तथा जिम्मेवार अधिकारीमाथि कारबाहीको माग गर्दै आन्दोलन जारी राखेको छ। वीरगञ्जस्थित नारायणी अस्पतालका चिकित्सकहरूले सामूहिक राजीनामा समेत बुझाएका छन्।

यसैबीच स्वास्थ्य तथा जनसंख्या मन्त्रालयले दोषीलाई कानुनी दायरामा ल्याइने प्रक्रिया अघि बढाइएको जनाउँदै स्वास्थ्य सेवा अवरुद्ध नगर्न सबै अस्पताललाई आग्रह गरेको छ। आन्दोलनका कारण देशभरका धेरै स्वास्थ्य संस्थामा नियमित उपचार सेवा प्रभावित भएको छ भने बिरामीहरूले संविधानले प्रत्याभूत गरेको आधारभूत स्वास्थ्य सेवाको अधिकारको प्रयोगमा कठिनाइ भोगिरहेका छन्।

यसै घटनाक्रमबीच पर्साका प्रहरी प्रमुखको सरुवालाई सुरक्षा व्यवस्थापन र घटनापछिको प्रशासनिक जिम्मेवारीसँग जोडेर हेरिएको छ। यद्यपि सरुवाको औपचारिक कारणबारे सम्बन्धित निकायले विस्तृत जानकारी सार्वजनिक गरेको छैन।

articles.title: प्रस्तावित निर्वाचन आयुक्तको कार्ययोजना : निर्वाचनमा भाग नलिने दललाई खारेजीको प्रस्ताव
articles.summary:
प्रस्तावित प्रमुख निर्वाचन आयुक्त मानबहादुर कार्कीले निर्वाचनमा भाग नलिने राजनीतिक दलको दर्ता खारेजी सम्बन्धमा कानुनी व्यवस्था गर्न सकिने कार्ययोजना पेस गरेका छन्।

सङ्घीय संसद्को सुनुवाइ समितिको आजको बैठकमा आफ्नो कार्ययोजना प्रस्तुत गर्दै कार्कीले निर्वाचन सहभागी नहुने दललाई एकापसामा एकता गराउन भने सकिने सुझाव प्रस्तुत गरे।

प्रस्तावित प्रमुख आयुक्त कार्कीले भने, ‘राजनीतिक दलभित्रको आन्तरिक लोकतन्त्र सुदृढ, समानुपातिक, समावेशी प्रतिनिधित्वको कार्यान्वयन तथा निर्वाचन आयोग र राजनीतिक दलबीच संस्थागत संवादलाई सुदृढ बनाउन आवश्यक छ।’

कुनै पनि उम्मेदवारलाई भोट दिन्न (नो भोट) भन्ने अवधारणालाई कानुनमै व्यवस्था गरेर जान सकिने बताउँदै उनले बदर मत घटाउन मतदाता शिक्षा प्रभावकारी बनाउन आवश्यक रहेको धारणा व्यक्त गरे।

प्रस्तावित प्रमुख निर्वाचन आयुक्त कार्कीले निर्वाचनका सन्दर्भमा मतदाता नामावली दोहरिन नदिन तीन तहबीच अन्तर–आबद्धतालाई जोडेर सुरक्षित डाटा सेन्टर बनाउन सकिने सुझाव प्रस्तुत गरे।

नेपालको निर्वाचन प्रणालीलाई समयानुकूल, प्रविधिमैत्री, मितव्ययी र थप विश्वसनीय बनाउन विदेशमा रहेका नेपाली नागरिकलाई मतदानको अधिकार प्रदान गर्ने तथा अन्तर–जिल्ला मतदान र एकीकृत निर्वाचन कानुन निर्माणलाई प्रमुख प्राथमिकतामा राख्ने उनले सङ्कल्प गरे।

प्रस्तावित प्रमुख आयुक्त कार्कीले बदलिँदो लोकतान्त्रिक परिवेशमा निर्वाचनलाई थप स्वच्छ, स्वतन्त्र, निष्पक्ष र विश्वसनीय बनाउनु अहिलेको प्रमुख चुनौती भएको उल्लेख गर्दै निर्वाचन सुधारका समसामयिक मुद्दामा केन्द्रित कार्ययोजना दिए।

कार्ययोजनाअनुसार विदेशमा रहेका नेपाली नागरिक तथा आफ्नो निर्वाचन जिल्ला बाहिर बसोबास गर्ने मतदाताको मताधिकार सुनिश्चित गर्न आवश्यक कानुनी तथा पाविधिक व्यवस्था गरिने प्रस्ताव गरिएको छ।

निर्वाचनलाई कम खर्चिलो र धान्न सकिने तुल्याउने, राजनीतिक दलको आर्थिक कारोबारलाई पारदर्शी बनाउने तथा निर्वाचनप्रतिको जनविश्वास अभिवृद्धि गर्ने विषयलाई उनले प्रमुख सुधार एजेन्डाका रूपमा अघि सारेका छन्।

कार्ययोजनामा सूचना प्रविधिको अधिकतम प्रयोगमार्फत शुद्ध मतदाता नामावली, व्यापक मतदाता सहभागिता तथा प्रभावकारी आचारसंहिता कार्यान्वयनमा जोड दिइएको छ।

निर्वाचन आयोगका सम्पूर्ण सेवाहरूलाई प्रविधिमैत्री बनाउने, मतदाता नामावलीको अनलाइन दर्ता, बायोमेट्रिक पहिचान, जिआइएस तथा जिपीएस प्रविधिको प्रयोग, आधुनिक डाटा सेन्टर स्थापना तथा निर्वाचन व्यवस्थापनमा डिजिटल प्रणाली विस्तार गर्ने प्रस्ताव कार्ययोजनामा समावेश छ।

निर्वाचन खर्च नियन्त्रणका लागि राजनीतिक दल र उम्मेदवारको आर्थिक कारोबार अनिवार्य रूपमा बैंकिङ प्रणालीमार्फत सञ्चालन गर्ने, निर्वाचन खर्चको नियमित लेखापरीक्षण गराउने तथा प्रचारप्रसार खर्चको सीमा पुनरावलोकन गर्ने योजना पनि कार्ययोजनामा समावेश गरिएको छ।

यस्तै मतदाता नामावलीलाई स्वचालित र अद्यावधिक बनाउन राष्ट्रिय परिचयपत्र तथा व्यक्तिगत घटना दर्ता प्रणालीसँग अन्तर–आबद्धता कायम गरी जन्म, मृत्यु र बसाइँसराइँजस्ता विवरण स्वतः अद्यावधिक हुने प्रणाली विकास गरिने उल्लेख गरिएको छ।

मतदाता शिक्षालाई विद्यालय तहदेखि नै संस्थागत गर्दै मतदान प्रतिशत बढाउने तथा बदर मत घटाउने लक्ष्यका साथ निर्वाचन शिक्षा कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन गर्ने योजना पनि कार्ययोजनामा प्रस्तुत गरिएको छ।

कार्ययोजनामा विदेशमा रहेका नेपाली नागरिकको मताधिकार सुनिश्चित गर्न योग्य मतदाता पहिचान, सम्बन्धित मुलुकसँग कूटनीतिक समन्वय तथा मतदानको उपयुक्त विधि छनोट गरिने उल्लेख गरिएको छ।

प्रस्तावित प्रमुख आयुक्त कार्कीले मतपेटिका, हुलाक, इन्टरनेट र प्रतिनिधिमूलक मतदान प्रणालीको अध्ययनपछि नेपालको सन्दर्भमा हुलाकमार्फत मतदान र इन्टरनेट मतदानको व्यवस्था पनि गर्न सकिने आफ्नो योजना प्रस्तुत गरे।

समिति सदस्यले कार्कीसँग उनको कार्ययोजना र समसामयिक निर्वाचन मुद्दाका आधारमा जिज्ञासाहरु राखेका थिए। यसअघि आजै समितिमा कार्कीविरुद्धका उजुरीकर्तासँग छलफल गरिएको थियो।

संवैधानिक परिषद्को गत असार १९ गतेको बैठकले प्रमुख निर्वाचन आयुक्तमा कार्कीसहित आयुक्तमा गुरुप्रसाद वाग्ले र डा राजीव सुब्बाको नाम प्रस्ताव गरी संसदीय सुनुवाइका लागि पठाएको थियो।

articles.title: संसदीय कार्य प्रभावकारी बनाउन सभामुख अर्याल सक्रिय, प्रधानमन्त्री शाहसहित शीर्ष नेतासँग छलफल
articles.summary:
प्रतिनिधि सभाको बैठकलाई थप प्रभावकारी, मर्यादित र परिणाममुखी बनाउने उद्देश्यका साथ सभामुख डीपी अर्यालले विभिन्न राजनीतिक दलका शीर्ष नेताहरूसँग छुट्टाछुट्टै भेटवार्ता गरेका छन्।

सभामुख अर्यालले प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन्द्र शाह, नेकपा (एमाले) का संसदीय दलका नेता रामबहादुर थापा, विपक्षी दलका नेता भिष्मराज आङदेम्बे तथा नेपाली कम्युनिष्ट पार्टीका नेता वर्षमान पुनसँग छुट्टाछुट्टै भेट गरेका छन्। भेटमा संसद्को कार्य सञ्चालन, दलहरूबीचको समन्वय र आगामी संसदीय कार्यसूचीबारे छलफल भएको सभामुख अर्यालकाे सचिवालयले जनाएको छ।

भेटका क्रममा प्रतिनिधि सभाको बैठकलाई थप व्यवस्थित, प्रभावकारी र उपलब्धिमूलक बनाउने विषयमा धारणा आदानप्रदान भएको थियो।

यसैबीच, मंगलबार नै सभामुख अर्यालले विभिन्न राजनीतिक दलका प्रमुख सचेतक र सचेतकहरूसँग पनि छुट्टै छलफल गर्नुभएको थियो। उक्त छलफलमा प्रतिनिधि सभाको कार्य सञ्चालनलाई अझ व्यवस्थित बनाउने, आगामी बैठकका कार्यसूचीलाई समयमै टुंग्याउने तथा संसद्को प्रभावकारी सञ्चालनका लागि आवश्यक समन्वयका विषयमा विचारविमर्श भएको जनाइएको छ।

articles.title: पोखरा प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठानको कुलपतिमा सरस्वती ‘प्रतीक्षा’ नियुक्त
articles.summary:
पोखरा प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठानको कुलपतिमा साहित्यकार सरस्वती ‘प्रतीक्षा’ नियुक्त भएकी छन्।

महानगरपालिकाकी उपप्रमुख मञ्जुदेवी गुरुङ नेतृत्वको समितिले सिफारिस गरेबमोजिम पोखरा महानगरपालिकाले प्रतीक्षालाई कुलपतिमा नियुक्त गरेको हो।

त्यस्तै, उपकुलपतिमा पुन आर्टका सञ्चालक तथा साहित्यकार तिलक पुन पुर्जा मगर र सदस्य–सचिवमा जीवन दाहाल (लोकगीत, संगीत) नियुक्त भएका छन्।

प्रतिष्ठानको प्रज्ञा परिषद् सदस्यहरूमा श्रीजङ्ग गुरुङ, हरेराम जोजिजु , दिलीप गायक र प्रमीला ताम्राकार तुलाचन नियुक्त भएका छन्।

यसैगरी, प्रतिष्ठानको प्राज्ञ सभा सदस्यहरूमा भास्करध्वज श्रेष्ठ (संगीत तथा व्याण्ड), कल्पना चिलुवाल (साहित्य), कृष्णप्रसाद गौतम (संस्कृति), गमबहादुर परियार (नृत्य), ज्योति गुरुङ (फाइन आर्ट, ललितकला), नवराज अधिकारी (लेखनाथ साहित्य प्रतिष्ठान), प्रेमराज अधिकारी (लोकगीत), रवीन्द्र माकाजु (साहित्य तथा ईतिहास), रिता पहारी (साहित्य तथा कला) र शिवहरि ढुङ्गाना (लोक तथा दोहोरी गीत) नियुक्त भए।

महानगरले पदाधिकारी रिक्त रहेको डेढ वर्षपछि मात्रै नयाँ पदाधिकारी नियुक्त गरेको थियो। प्रतिष्ठानका पदाधिकारी डेढ वर्षसम्म नहुँदा पोखरामा भाषा, साहित्य, कला, संगीतलगायतका क्षेत्रका गतिविधि ठप्प भएका थिए।

नियुक्त भएका कुलपति प्रतीक्षासहित सबैलाई पोखरा महानगरपालिकाका प्रमुख धनराज आचार्यले बुधबार बिहान जिम्मेवारीसहित नियुक्ति पत्र प्रदान गरेका छन्। प्रतिष्ठानको कार्यालय महानगरले हालै बनाएको पोखरा घरमा रहेको छ।

कार्यक्रममा मेयर आचार्यले प्रतिष्ठानका गतिविधिहरू मार्फत पोखरा महानगरपालिका क्षेत्रको साहित्य, कला, संस्कृति, भाषा लगायत समग्र प्राज्ञिक क्षेत्रको उन्नयन र विकासमा उल्लेखनीय योगदान पुग्ने विश्वास व्यक्त गरे।

उनले भने,‘प्रतिष्ठानका गतिविधिहरूलाई चुस्त र प्रभावकारी बनाउनुहुनेछ भन्ने विश्वास व्यक्त गर्दछु।’ उनले प्रतिष्ठानका लागि बजेटको अभाव हुन नदिने प्रतिबद्धतासमेत जनाए।

कार्यक्रममा बोल्दै उपप्रमुख मजुदेवी गुरुङले नगर क्षेत्रको साहित्य, कला, भाषा, सृजना र संस्कृतिको विकासमा प्रतिष्ठानले महत्त्वपूर्ण टेवा पुग्ने विश्वास व्यक्त गरिन्।

नवनियुक्त कुलपति प्रतीक्षाले आफूहरूलाई प्रदान गरिएको जिम्मेवारी निष्ठापूर्वक बहन गर्ने प्रतिबद्धता जाहेर गरिन्। पोखरेली प्राज्ञिक क्षेत्रको विकास र श्रीवृद्धिमा आफूहरू समर्पित भएर लाग्ने उल्लेख गर्दै उनले भनिन्,‘पोखरा प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठानलाई नमुना प्रतिष्ठानका रूपमा स्थापित गर्ने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गर्दछु।’

प्रतिष्ठानको संस्थापक कुलपति पद्मराज ढकाल बनेका थिए। महानगरले पर्याप्त बजेट नदिँदा उनको कार्यकाल अभावै अभावमा बितेको थियो।

articles.title: नारायणी अस्पताल घटना: पर्साका एसपी सुदीप पाठक जिम्मेवारीबाट हटाइए
articles.summary:
वीरगञ्जस्थित नारायणी अस्पतालमा चिकित्सकमाथि भएको कुटपिट, अस्पतालमा भएको तोडफोड तथा त्यसपछिको विवादका बीच जिल्ला प्रहरी कार्यालय पर्साका प्रमुख प्रहरी उपरीक्षक (एसपी) सुदीप पाठकलाई जिम्मेवारीबाट हटाइएको छ।

गृह मन्त्रालयले एसपी पाठकलाई तानेर उनको स्थानमा काठमाडौं प्रहरी परिसरका प्रवक्ता एसपी पवन भट्टराईलाई पर्साको प्रहरी प्रमुखका रूपमा सरुवा गरेको छ।

नारायणी अस्पतालमा उपचारका क्रममा एक बिरामीको मृत्यु भएपछि मृतकका आफन्तले अस्पतालमा तोडफोड गर्नुका साथै चिकित्सक र स्वास्थ्यकर्मीमाथि कुटपिट गरेका थिए। त्यसपछि जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालय पर्सामा भएको छलफलका क्रममा पनि चिकित्सकहरूमाथि दुर्व्यवहार भएको भन्दै नेपाल चिकित्सक संघले विरोध जनाएको थियो।

घटनाको विरोधस्वरूप नेपाल चिकित्सक संघले देशभर आकस्मिक सेवाबाहेकका स्वास्थ्य सेवा बन्द गर्दै दोषीमाथि कानुनी कारबाही, स्वास्थ्यकर्मीको सुरक्षा सुनिश्चित तथा जिम्मेवार अधिकारीमाथि कारबाहीको माग गर्दै आन्दोलन जारी राखेको छ। वीरगञ्जस्थित नारायणी अस्पतालका चिकित्सकहरूले सामूहिक राजीनामा समेत बुझाएका छन्।

यसैबीच स्वास्थ्य तथा जनसंख्या मन्त्रालयले दोषीलाई कानुनी दायरामा ल्याइने प्रक्रिया अघि बढाइएको जनाउँदै स्वास्थ्य सेवा अवरुद्ध नगर्न सबै अस्पताललाई आग्रह गरेको छ। आन्दोलनका कारण देशभरका धेरै स्वास्थ्य संस्थामा नियमित उपचार सेवा प्रभावित भएको छ भने बिरामीहरूले संविधानले प्रत्याभूत गरेको आधारभूत स्वास्थ्य सेवाको अधिकारको प्रयोगमा कठिनाइ भोगिरहेका छन्।

यसै घटनाक्रमबीच पर्साका प्रहरी प्रमुखको सरुवालाई सुरक्षा व्यवस्थापन र घटनापछिको प्रशासनिक जिम्मेवारीसँग जोडेर हेरिएको छ। यद्यपि सरुवाको औपचारिक कारणबारे सम्बन्धित निकायले विस्तृत जानकारी सार्वजनिक गरेको छैन।

articles.title: Cabinet clears bill raising domestic airline liability to $100,000
articles.summary:
The Cabinet on Wednesday gave in-principle approval to table in Parliament a long-pending bill governing domestic airlines’ liability and insurance responsibilities, reviving a reform process that has remained stalled since the draft was first prepared in 2019.

The bill seeks to overhaul Nepal’s domestic aviation liability and insurance regime, renewing efforts to align the country’s aviation laws with international standards years after ratifying the Montreal Convention 1999.

Although the Montreal Convention governs liability only in international air travel, the proposed legislation seeks to bring Nepal’s domestic aviation liability framework closer to global norms by clearly defining airlines’ responsibilities in cases of accidents, delays, baggage loss and flight disruptions.

The bill establishes passengers’ rights and carriers’ obligations while introducing comprehensive provisions on compensation, cargo liability, insurance coverage and the circumstances under which airlines may be exempt from liability.

The Ministry of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation had published the draft for public feedback in July last year before forwarding it to the Ministry of Law for legal scrutiny. However, the government was toppled by the September Gen Z movement, halting progress on the legislation.

“We have revised the draft and resubmitted it to the law ministry under the new government,” Indu Ghimire, joint secretary at the Tourism Ministry, told the Post in a recent interview.

Under the proposed law, domestic airlines would be liable to pay compensation of up to $100,000 if a passenger suffers serious injury, disability or dies in an accident during boarding, the flight or disembarkation. In the event of a passenger’s death, compensation would be paid to the deceased’s nearest legal heir.

The minimum compensation for the death or injury of a passenger on a domestic flight in Nepal is currently $20,000. For crew members, the minimum compensation is typically $40,000 per person.

By comparison, the Montreal Convention currently sets airline liability at up to $202,500 for passenger death or injury on international flights. The liability limit was last revised on December 28, 2024.

The Montreal Convention follows a two-tier liability system. Under the first tier, airlines are strictly liable for proven damages up to $202,500 and cannot contest liability unless the passenger contributed to the injury. For damages exceeding that threshold, there is no upper limit. Airlines remain liable for the full amount unless they can prove that the accident did not result from their negligence or was caused solely by a third party.

The draft bill also requires airlines to provide appropriate medical treatment to passengers who suffer non-fatal injuries or disabilities. In the event of a fatal accident, airlines must arrange for the return of the deceased’s body to the family and provide advance payments to help cover immediate funeral and transportation expenses.

The legislation introduces clear obligations regarding flight delays and cancellations. Airlines would be required to notify passengers with valid tickets at least three hours before a revised departure time if a scheduled flight is delayed or cancelled.

If a flight is overbooked or a ticketed passenger cannot be accommodated, the airline must either arrange a seat on another carrier operating to the same destination at a similar time, provide an alternative means of travel at no additional cost, or issue a full refund immediately.

The draft also sets compensation standards for baggage loss and damage. Airlines would be required to compensate passengers up to $20 per kilogram, subject to a maximum of $5,000, for lost or damaged checked baggage, with payments made in Nepali currency.

For unchecked baggage carried into the cabin, compensation of up to $400 would be payable for loss or damage.

Cargo liability has also been addressed. Airlines would be liable for up to $20 per kilogram for lost or damaged cargo unless the shipper had declared a higher value in writing. Carriers would be responsible for losses arising from negligence by the airline, its employees or authorised agents.

The bill also requires compensation for delayed cargo deliveries. Cargo would be considered undelivered if it failed to arrive within three days when no delivery deadline had been agreed upon. It would be deemed officially lost if it were not delivered within 15 days of the scheduled date or within 30 days of acceptance where no delivery period had been specified.

The proposed legislation specifies situations in which airlines would not be held liable. These include delays or cancellations caused by adverse weather, natural disasters, airport or air traffic service disruptions, and security restrictions imposed by government authorities.

Similarly, airlines would not be liable if injuries resulted from a passenger’s gross negligence or a pre-existing medical condition, provided they could produce evidence to support the claim.

The bill also introduces provisions governing third-party liability arising from aircraft accidents.

It proposes mandatory insurance coverage based on aircraft weight, requiring $25 million for aircraft weighing up to 10,000 kilograms, $35 million for aircraft weighing between 10,001 and 35,000 kilograms, and $60 million for aircraft exceeding 35,000 kilograms.

Passengers seeking compensation for injuries or medical expenses would have to file claims with the airline or its authorised agent within 60 days, supported by the necessary documentation. If the airline rejects the claim, the passenger would be entitled to file a lawsuit in the appropriate court within 35 days of receiving the airline’s decision.

The draft also introduces the principle of unlimited liability in certain cases. Compensation for injuries or disabilities would be determined according to the severity of the harm, the resulting loss of income and the long-term impact on the victim’s earning capacity.

In addition, the government would be required to review compensation limits every 10 years, adjusting them to account for inflation and prevailing market conditions. Any revisions would have to be published in the Nepal Gazette.

articles.title: Koshi announces relief for Dewanganj violence victims
articles.summary:
The Koshi provincial government has announced relief for victims of the violence in Dewanganj, Sunsari, pledging Rs200,000 for the family of each person killed and Rs50,000 for those injured and families whose homes or shops were damaged in arson attacks.

The announcement was made on Wednesday after an all-party meeting convened by Chief Minister Hikmat Kumar Karki to discuss the aftermath of the Sunday violence in Dewanganj.

The meeting adopted an eight-point resolution aimed at restoring social harmony, maintaining peace and strengthening security.

Under the agreement, political parties, civil society organisations and the local administration will work together to promote mutual brotherhood and social harmony. The provincial government also decided to organise all-party and multi-stakeholder meetings at the local level to encourage dialogue and reconciliation.

The resolution also calls for goodwill marches, public appeals, and other outreach programmes to be conducted in coordination with local authorities to foster trust and harmony within affected communities.

The meeting urged organisations representing all religious communities to issue a joint appeal and play an active role in preserving communal harmony.

The meeting urged organisations representing all religious communities to issue a joint appeal and play an active role in preserving social harmony.

Participants also called on security agencies to remain vigilant against any undesirable activities that could originate from border areas. The federal government was requested to ensure proper treatment for the injured and provide relief to the families of those killed.

The meeting further urged closer coordination with district administrations in Sunsari and surrounding districts to strengthen security measures and prevent similar incidents from recurring.

Addressing the meeting, Karki said all stakeholders must act responsibly and exercise restraint to maintain social harmony during the sensitive period.

He urged everyone to refrain from any activities that could undermine social harmony.

The meeting was attended by Chandra Bahadur Rai, provincial chair of the Rastriya Swatantra Party; Uddhav Thapa, provincial president of the Nepali Congress; Ghanshyam Khatiwada, provincial chair of the CPN-UML; representatives of other political parties, heads of provincial security agencies and senior government officials.

articles.title: Nepal once had a vibrant civil society. Now it is faded and fragmented
articles.summary:
Devendra Raj Panday was known less for his formal titles as an economist, former minister and planner than for his role as a “citizen leader.”

Standing outside active party politics, he consistently questioned the state, governments and political parties. His views on Nepal’s political crises, democratic backsliding and issues of public interest were difficult for governments and political parties to ignore.

Panday died on July 17 at the age of 87.

His death came at a time when the independent civic voice he represented has become far quieter than it once was. The civil society and citizen movement that played a crucial role in Nepal’s democratic struggles, creating public pressure for democracy, human rights and accountability while challenging governments and political parties, now appears fragmented, particularly after the constitution was promulgated in 2015.

Has Nepal’s civil society and citizen movement weakened, or has it simply taken a new shape in response to changing circumstances?

Analysts say that at a time when parliamentary opposition has weakened, and the role of the press has narrowed, the broad civic coalition that once spoke with a collective voice has splintered into separate campaigns and movements without a common platform.

Analyst Dovan Rai believes the once-powerful citizen movement has weakened and become ‘tired’.

“When we were fighting regression in the past, we knew exactly what we were fighting for and against. That clarity is missing today,” she said. “The leaders of the citizen movement have failed to grasp the political moment. Once the Balendra Shah government claimed ownership of ideas like youth, change and a new political order, the citizen movement was left without a distinct message of its own.”

The Balendra Shah-led government was formed after the Rastriya Swatantra Party won the March elections with nearly a two-thirds majority, months after the youth-led movement in September last year.

Rai’s assessment points to a deeper crisis: as Nepal’s political landscape has changed, the citizen movement has struggled to redefine what it stands for.

The roots of this crisis go beyond recent political developments. For years, Nepal’s civil society, often described as the citizen movement, has faced the challenge of maintaining the collective power and public authority it demonstrated during earlier democratic struggles.

Several studies have noted that Nepal’s citizen movement has been most influential during periods of political transition. During the struggle against the Panchayat system, lawyers, professors, writers, journalists and professional organisations formed the intellectual foundation of the democratic movement. The citizen movement emerged as an organised force during the 2006 People’s Movement

Many studies define Nepal’s “civil society” primarily as non-governmental organisations or registered civic institutions. For instance, the Asian Development Bank’s 2024 publication Civil Society Brief: Nepal analyses civil society mainly through the lens of civil society organisations, including NGOs, community organisations and professional bodies.

According to the brief, institutional presence of such organisations remains extensive in Nepal, cooperation with the government continues at various levels, international donor support remains significant, and the World Social Forum held in Kathmandu in 2024 demonstrated the organisational capacity of Nepali civil society.

However, after the 2006 People’s Movement, the independent civic voice that intervened in matters of public concern outside political parties increasingly came to be identified not as ‘civil society’ but as a ‘citizen movement’.

Analyst CK Lal, in his July 22 column in Kantipur, argues that the term “citizen movement” was chosen instead of “civil society” based on his own proposal during discussions among independent citizens, including Panday, about the movement. The movement brought together human rights activists, lawyers, professors, journalists, writers, former bureaucrats and leaders of professional organisations. They campaigned for democracy and peace, questioned governments and political parties, and demanded accountability.

In his article in the Martin Chautari publication ‘Civil Society in Democracy: A 25-Year Review’, Chudamani Basnet writes that before the 2006 People’s Movement, intellectuals were worried that political parties would be unable to mobilise citizens.

There were doubts that people would take to the streets under the leadership of parties that had been associated with corruption and disorder since the restoration of democracy in 1990. It was amid this uncertainty that the citizen movement emerged.

After the February 2005 state of emergency, political space gradually opened up, while the royal regime came under mounting international pressure. Many intellectuals who had left the country returned and began meeting at the Nepal South Asia Centre in Anamnagar for discussions.

Panday had established the centre soon after the 1990 democratic movement.

Basnet writes that among the senior figures who gathered there were Panday, Padma Ratna Tuladhar, Khagendra Sangraula, Krishna Khanal, Saroj Dhital, Daman Nath Dhungana, Sundar Mani Dixit, Shyam Shrestha, Mahesh Maskey and Krishna Pahadi.

Although they held different ideological positions, they were united against the royal takeover.

Young researchers and activists from smaller organisations such as the Collective Campaign for Peace (COCAP), Martin Chautari and the Human Rights and Peace Society gradually joined the movement.

The citizen leaders had experience in struggles, but not in mass mobilisation.

According to Panday’s own account, one incident pushed him to act. On July 19, 2005, the seven political parties had called a ‘session’ of the dissolved House of Representatives at the Nepal Academy.

When leaders including Girija Prasad Koirala and Madhav Nepal arrived, security personnel stopped them at the main gate, forcing them to return home.

Panday, then 65, watched the scene with his young colleague Anil Bhattarai. Disappointed that the political parties had no clear strategy against King Gyanendra’s takeover, Panday wrote in his autobiography ‘Ek Jyan, Duijuni’ that he told Bhattarai: “Let us take to the streets without waiting for the inspiration and blessing of the seven parties.”

Following that decision, a group of independent citizens announced a demonstration at the restricted Ratna Park on July 25.

Basnet writes that the Ratna Park protest, along with the police’s heavy-handed response, propelled the “Citizen Movement for Democracy and Peace” into public consciousness. The movement, later known simply as the “citizen movement”, quickly emerged as a powerful civic force.

With media support and public participation, a mass gathering was organised at New Baneshwar on August 5. Around 10,000 people attended the rally, making it the largest protest since King Gyanendra seized power on February 1, 2005, Basnet writes.

Panday said the citizen movement had neither an organisation nor financial resources. Yet it managed to organise rallies across the country.

From the east to the west, the same slogan echoed: “Maoists, give up your weapons. The seven parties, give up the king.”

The 2006 People’s Movement eventually became a turning point in Nepal’s political history. King Gyanendra was forced to hand power back to political parties, while the 240-year-old monarchy was subsequently abolished.

The civil society that played an important role during that historic transition remained active for another decade, continuing to question governments and political parties.

After the Constituent Assembly elections, individuals involved in civil society and the citizen movement continued participating in public debates on federalism, inclusion, human rights and transitional justice.

But that presence began to fade after the constitution was promulgated.

Some argue that the citizen movement completed its historic mission once the democratic transition ended with the promulgation of the constitution. Others say the movement lost public trust because it was dominated by Kathmandu-based, male elites who failed to listen to groups dissatisfied with the constitution.

Writer and columnist Chandrakishore argues that the decline of civil society’s influence began accelerating after the constitution was promulgated in 2015.

“The Nepali Congress, UML and then Maoists grew more confident as they came together to bring in the constitution. They started believing that their consensus itself represented the national interest,” he said. “As a result, they began dismissing the role of civil society. That gradually weakened the citizen movement’s influence.”

Chandrakishore argues that debates over identity further divided the movement. Many prominent civil society figures struggled to take a clear position on movements by Madhesi, Tharu and Janajati communities demanding greater recognition of their ethnic and regional identities.

“Earlier, the movement had a clear target: Gyanendra and the active monarchy,” he said. “But when identity-based movements emerged, it became much harder to decide which causes to support and which positions to take.”

Questions remained over acceptance of the constitution among large sections of society when the constitution was promulgated on September 20, 2015. But the citizen movement, which had played a prominent role in street protests and public debates before its adoption, no longer appeared as a force with the same influence.

“Madhesh was observing it as a day of mourning at a time when Kathmandu was celebrating the constitution. Where was civil society then?” Chandrakishore wondered. “When Kathmandu’s citizen movement did not support identity-based movements, it lost trust among people on the ground. At the same time, the state also ignored it. The citizen movement was trapped between the two.”

The movement’s decline has also been linked to the fact that some prominent figures who had previously been active in it entered electoral politics, received appointments to constitutional bodies, became government advisers or joined donor-funded institutions.

A study published in the Journal of Peace Research in 2026, based on research into 26 civil society organisations in Bhojpur, Sarlahi and Kapilvastu districts, concluded that “the entry of experienced civil society actors into politics after the People’s Movement weakened institutional leadership, limited effective generational transition and changed the direction of organisations in line with donor priorities.”

During the conflict years, issues such as enforced disappearances, torture, extrajudicial killings and press freedom were central concerns of civil society. After the peace process, transitional justice remained a major focus for several years.

But after the constitution, collective civic interventions on issues such as civil liberties, economic rights, state accountability, public services and digital rights became far less visible.

Writer and activist Sanjeev Uprety believes there are structural reasons behind this decline.

“The 2006 movement brought together many people, including Devendra Raj Panday, Krishna Pahadi and others. I was also involved,” he recalled. “But after the political transformation, the citizen movement began to lose momentum. We were unable to maintain the same level of mobilisation.”

“Sustaining it was difficult because it was a volunteer-based movement. It was neither a political party nor an NGO. People moved on to their own paths. We remained part of civil society, but not as a movement.”

Uprety says the movement regained some momentum after then-prime minister KP Sharma Oli dissolved Parliament in 2020 in what critics called an unconstitutional move.

“After that, we realised the citizen movement had to continue in some form,” he said. “Even after Parliament was restored, movements by sugarcane farmers, Chure conservation activists, usury victims and squatters continued.”

“The difference is that in 2006, the goal was to transform the political system itself. Today, movements are focused on the concerns of ordinary citizens. At that time, party cadres came to the streets. Now it is sugarcane farmers and victims of sexual violence who are coming forward.”

While citizens continue to raise issues through various campaigns, these movements include not only affected communities but also professionals and public figures who collectively represent civil society. However, analysts and activists acknowledge that the absence of the kind of unified civic voice seen in the past remains a major weakness.

They argue, however, that this should not be interpreted as the death of civil society in Nepal.

Uprety says societies do not have a single civil society but multiple civil societies. Nepal, like other countries, sees fragmented groups come together during moments of major crisis, but keeping them connected during normal times remains difficult.

“We tried to bring together movements around land rights and usury victims. Dalit rights, indigenous rights and squatters’ rights should have been connected, but we could not do that,” he said.

“The Koshi identity movement, the Chure conservation campaign and the struggle of usury victims have not been able to come together. That fragmentation has prevented them from becoming a more powerful civic force.”

The youth-led movement of September last year not only changed Nepal’s political landscape but also transformed how ordinary citizens view society and politics.

In this changed environment, questions have emerged over the future shape of civil society and the citizen movement, particularly because leaders have yet to develop a clear position on broader public concerns such as economic rights, public services and digital freedoms.

Rai argues that the citizen movement has become even more uncertain after the youth movement because it lacks a clear political narrative.

“It looks as though they have not been able to grasp the new political reality,” she said. “What does today’s politics represent? Is it progressive or regressive? Should we support it or oppose it? When the Balendra Shah government appoints a woman minister, are we supposed to welcome it or criticise it? The movement seems to have lost its direction.”

She warns that the weakening of the movement affects society more broadly.

“When reform-minded people within political parties look for advice, whom do they consult? Who stands alongside them? That creates a vacuum,” she said. “The recent mistreatment of Majid Ansari was serious. Last year’s September movement also saw widespread violence and deaths. When older generations fail to offer strategic direction, younger people end up carrying the risks of confrontation on their own.”

Uprety does not believe civil society has disappeared. Instead, he argues that its form has changed.

He says civic interventions that once appeared as nationwide movements have now spread across local campaigns, issue-based activism and digital platforms.

In recent years, public reactions against the Guthi Bill, environmental concerns over the proposed Nijgadh airport, the Citizenship Bill, the TikTok ban and social media regulation demonstrated strong civic engagement.

“Digital activism is part of a broader civil society. People are writing and speaking out. But a citizen movement happens on the streets,” Uprety said. “When a crisis emerges, these scattered groups come together again and return to the streets.”

Today, the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party holds nearly a two-thirds majority in Parliament, leaving opposition parties weakened. Questions have also been raised about the credibility of other public institutions.

Critics of the government say they do not see a strong commitment to democratic values.

In such a situation, Birgunj-based writer Chandrakishore says the citizen movement has weakened, and the voice of dissent in Kathmandu has become quieter.

The silence in the capital, he says, appears unusual.

“I am watching Kathmandu right now. There is silence. Why is everyone afraid? Why is nobody speaking?” he asked.

He believes the root of the problem lies in ethics.

“People are afraid to speak, perhaps because some feel constrained by questions of personal ethics and accountability,” he said.

He also pointed to concerns that this government could weaken the constitutional framework and, in return, erode democracy itself.“Yet even at such a moment, there is no one willing to speak out,” he said.

Uprety also sees such risks.

“I cannot predict where the country’s politics will go, but I see a major risk to democracy. The current government is showing signs of danger to democratic institutions,” he said.

Chandrakishore believes the current government itself may eventually bring fragmented civic leaders back together.

“I think this government will once again unite citizen leaders who are scattered today in the struggle for justice. During Gyanendra’s rule, circumstances brought them together. It will happen again,” he said.

Rai shares a similar hope.

“There is still a group that worked together during that period. As the crisis deepens, perhaps that group will consolidate again,” she said.

Sociologist Chaitanya Mishra concluded his obituary, published in NepalNews, for Panday with a warning about the possible democratic crisis Nepal faces today.

“In the changed political context, citizens are once again beginning to feel fear. Dr Panday remained concerned about this until his final days,” Mishra wrote. “If this crisis deepens, we will once again need independent, committed and courageous intellectual citizens like him.”

articles.title: Road upgrade debris disrupts traffic on Rapti Highway
articles.summary:
Road users along the Kapurkot–Tulsipur section of the Rapti Highway have been facing disruptions for the past week after debris from ongoing road widening works was left piled on the road, narrowing the route and creating hazardous travel conditions.

A contractor working on the highway upgrade project has been using an excavator and a breaker machine to widen a sharp bend at Ramri. However, rocks and soil excavated while cutting the hillside have been dumped on the road instead of being removed, making it difficult for vehicles to pass.

The unmanaged debris has narrowed the highway, while rainwater has turned the affected sections muddy. Falling rocks have also repeatedly blocked the road, forcing vehicles to stop and causing delays for people travelling between Salyan, Rukum, Rolpa and Dang.

The situation has increased the risk of accidents, with drivers and riders forced to navigate the narrow and slippery road. The disruption has affected local commuters, transport operators, traders and residents who rely on the highway for access to markets, schools, health facilities and other essential services.

The road section is being upgraded to improve mobility, but the work has created additional challenges during the monsoon season. The contractor began cutting the hillside at Ramri on July 22 after large rocks above the road became unstable due to continuous rainfall, raising the risk of landslides and posing a threat to nearby settlements.

Following requests from residents living in vulnerable areas, the contractor deployed an excavator and a breaker machine to remove the unstable rocks and reduce the risk of accidents. However, the debris generated during the work was not cleared, leaving the highway partially obstructed.

"The authorities were right to take action to prevent a possible disaster, but the problem arose because the rocks and soil were not managed immediately," said Dal Bahadur Oli of Bagchaur Municipality-11 in Salyan.

He said the combination of scattered rocks and muddy conditions had made travel difficult, particularly for motorcycles and other two-wheelers. Some riders had slipped and fallen because of the slippery road surface, he added.

Vehicle driver Purna Reul said driving through the section at night had become particularly dangerous because of the debris left on the road.

"A small mistake could lead to an accident," Reul said, criticising the decision to carry out hill-cutting work during the rainy season.

"If the work had been carried out for a few hours in the morning and the debris removed by trucks at the same time, the situation would not have become this difficult," he said. "When rocks pushed by excavators block the road, vehicles have to wait for more than half an hour and long queues form. Passengers may wait, but the situation becomes much more serious if an ambulance carrying a patient gets stuck."

Kiran Rokaya of Siddhakumakha Rural Municipality said travellers were already facing problems on the Rapti Highway because sections such as Aringalepedi had become muddy and vulnerable to landslides during the monsoon. The debris piled up at Ramri had further disrupted vehicle movement, he said.

Ashok Chaudhary, information officer at the Road Division Office in Dang, said the road widening work had been delayed because continuous rainfall caused large and hard rocks above the highway to become unstable, putting nearby settlements at risk.

"The unstable rocks had to be removed carefully, and that took time. Because of this, the debris dumped on the road could not be cleared immediately," Chaudhary said.

He said the hill-cutting work was nearing completion, and the rocks and soil piled on the highway would be removed from Thursday.

articles.title: इरानलाई कडा प्रहार गर्ने चेतावनी दिँदै ट्रम्पले भने : उनीहरूले नराम्रोसँग कुटाइ खानेछन्
articles.summary:
मध्यपूर्वमा एकाएक बढेको तनाव र जोर्डनस्थित अमेरिकी सैन्य अड्डामाथिको इरानी क्षेप्यास्त्र आक्रमणको प्रयासपछि अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रम्पले कडा सैन्य प्रतिकारको चेतावनी दिएका छन्।

फक्स न्युजसँगको विशेष कुराकानीका क्रममा राष्ट्रपति ट्रम्पले इरानमाथि कडा सैन्य कारबाही गर्ने चेतावनी दिँदै भने, ‘हामी उनीहरूलाई कडा प्रहार गर्नेछौं, उनीहरूले नराम्रोसँग कुटाइ खानेछन्।’

ट्रम्पले अमेरिकी सेनासँग जोर्डनमाथिको आकस्मिक आक्रमणलाई असफल बनाउन केही मिनेट मात्र बाँकी रहेको अवस्थामा रक्षा प्रणालीले लक्ष्यमा पुग्नुअघि नै क्षेप्यास्त्रहरू आकाशमै सफलतापूर्वक नष्ट गरेको जानकारी दिए। साथै, उनले आक्रमणको समयमा अमेरिकी सेनाले वास्तविक समयमा स्थान संकेत दिएको भिडियोसमेत समीक्षा गरेको बताए।

यसअघि इरानको इस्लामिक रिभोलुसनरी गार्ड कोर्प्स (आईआरजीसी) ले जोर्डनस्थित मुवाफक साल्टी एयर बेस र अमेरिकी सेनाको केन्द्रीय कमान्डको मुख्यालयलाई लक्षित गर्दै ब्यालिस्टिक मिसाइलहरू प्रहार गरेको जनाएको थियो। जोर्डनको सेनाले आफ्नो आकाशमा आएका पाँच वटा इरानी मिसाइल आकाशमै नष्ट गरिएको पुष्टि गरेको छ।

इरान समर्थित समूहहरूले साउदी अरेबियाका तेल खानी र ऊर्जा केन्द्रहरूमा लगातार ड्रोन आक्रमण गरेपछि अमेरिका र साउदी अरेबियाले संयुक्त रूपमा इराकमा रहेका इरान समर्थित सशस्त्र समूहहरूमाथि ठूलो हवाई आक्रमण गरेका हुन्। इराकको पपुलर मोबिलाइजेसन फोर्स (पीएमएफ) ले दिएको जानकारी अनुसार अमेरिका-साउदी आक्रमणका कारण सातवटा प्रान्तमा कम्तीमा २० जना लडाकु मारिएका छन् र ३२ जना घाइते भएका छन्।

राष्ट्रपति ट्रम्पले इराकमा गरिएको उक्त रातारातको आक्रमण इराकी सरकारसँगको समन्वयमै भएको स्पष्ट पार्दै इरान समर्थित समूहहरूलाई ‘संसारको क्यान्सर’ को रूपमा चित्रण गरेका छन्। उनले इरानी समर्थित समूहविरुद्ध थप कडा कदम चालिने चेतावनीसमेत दिएका छन्।

तर, अमेरिका र साउदी अरबको संयुक्त आक्रमणपछि इराकले कडा आपत्ति जनाएको छ। इराकी सरकारले यसलाई आफ्नो देशको सार्वभौमिकताको स्पष्ट उल्लंघन भनेको छ। साथै, इराकले आफ्नो भूभाग छिमेकी देशहरूविरुद्ध आक्रमण गर्ने अखाडा बन्न नदिने बताउँदै आएको छ। यस तनावका बिच इराकी प्रधानमन्त्री मोहम्मद शिया अल-सुडानीको साउदी अरेबिया भ्रमण अनिश्चितकालका लागि स्थगित भएको छ।

यो नयाँ सैन्य द्वन्द्वले विश्वव्यापी ऊर्जा आपूर्तिमा गम्भीर असर पारेको छ। व्यापारका लागि अति संवेदनशील मानिने होर्मुज जलमार्ग र रेड सी क्षेत्रमा देखिएको तनावका कारण तेलको मूल्यमा भारी बृद्धि भएको छ। अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय बजारमा कच्चा तेलको मूल्य करिब सात प्रतिशतले बढेर प्रति ब्यारेल ९० डलरको नजिक पुगेको छ।

ओमानले होर्मुज जलमार्गमा जहाजहरूको ट्रान्जिट व्यवस्थापन गर्न राखेको प्रस्तावलाई इरानले अस्वीकार गरेको छ। यता, यमनका हुथी विद्रोहीहरूले साउदी अरेबियाका तेल डिपोहरूलाई लक्षित गरेर नाकाबन्दीको घोषणा गरेपछि क्षेत्रीय द्वन्द्व थप फैलिने जोखिम बढेको छ। विश्लेषकहरूले यो द्वन्द्व कूटनीतिक माध्यमबाट समाधान नभएमा यसले विश्व अर्थतन्त्र र मध्यपूर्वको शान्तिमा दीर्घकालीन असर पार्ने चेतावनी दिएका छन्। अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय सञ्चार माध्यमहरूको सहयोगमा

articles.title: ऊर्जामन्त्री श्रेष्ठ फिल्डमा उत्रेपछि एकदिनमै हट्याे थापाथली क्षेत्रकाे अव्यवस्थित तार
articles.summary:
थापाथली क्षेत्रका अव्यवस्थित तार एक दिनमै हटेकाे छ ।

ऊर्जा, जलस्राेत तथा सिँचाइ मन्त्री विराज भक्त श्रेष्ठकाे अग्रसरतामा बुधबार लामो समयदेखि थापाथली क्षेत्रमा सडकका पाेलमा गुजुल्टाे परेर लत्रिएका तथा प्रयाेगविहीन अवस्थामा रहेका विद्युत्, इन्टरनेट, टेलिफाेन र टेलिभिजनका तार व्यवस्थापन गरिएकाे हाे ।

मंगलबार राति तारहरूकाे गुजुल्टाेमा आगलागी भएपछि विहानैदेखि मन्त्री श्रेष्ठ थापाथली पुगेर व्यवस्थापनमा जुटेका थिए। उनले अवरुद्ध सेवा तत्काल सूचारू र तार व्यवस्थापनका लागि सम्बन्धित निकायसँग समन्वय पनि गरेका थिए ।

फिल्डबाटै मन्त्री श्रेष्ठले सञ्चारमन्त्री विक्रम तिमिल्सिना, नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरण, नेपाल विद्युत प्राधिकरण, दूरसञ्चार सेवा प्रदायक, इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायक संस्था, काठमाडौं महानगरपालिका तथा अन्य सम्बन्धित निकायसँग सम्पर्क गरेर साे क्षेत्रकाे तार हटाएका हुन् ।

मन्त्री श्रेष्ठले सम्बन्धित निकायकाे समन्वयमा सफलरूपमा तार व्यवस्थापन गरिएकाे र अन्य क्षेत्रमा पनि हटाइँदै जाने बताए। जोखिमपूर्ण अवस्थामा रहेका तारहरूको तत्काल व्यवस्थापन गर्न र दीर्घकालीन रूपमा व्यवस्थित तार व्यवस्थापन गरिने उनकाे भनाइ छ ।

मन्त्री श्रेष्ठले काठमाडौंका विभिन्न क्षेत्रमा वर्षौंदेखि गुजुल्टिएर रहेका तारलाई व्यवस्थित बनाउने अभियानलाई थप तीव्रता दिइने समेत स्पष्ट पारे।

articles.title: कांग्रेस एकताका लागि जनप्रतिनिधिको दबाब: साउन १६ को राष्ट्रिय भेला २७ मा सर्‍यो
articles.summary:
नेपाली कांग्रेस समर्थित जनप्रतिनिधिहरूको ‘पार्टी एकताका लागि संयुक्त राष्ट्रिय दबाब अभियान’ ले पार्टीभित्रको एकतालाई समयको अपरिहार्य आवश्यकता भएको भन्दै दबाब अभियानलाई निरन्तरता दिने घोषणा गरेको छ।

अभियानले वरिष्ठ नेता गोपालमान श्रेष्ठको निधन का कारण साउन १६ गतेका लागि तय गरिएको देशभरका कांग्रेस समर्थित जनप्रतिनिधिहरूको राष्ट्रिय भेला साउन २७ गतेका लागि सारिएको जनाएको छ।

बुधबार जारी गरिएको प्रेस विज्ञप्तिमा पार्टी स्थापना कालदेखि नै निरंकुशताविरुद्ध, नागरिक अधिकार र स्वतन्त्रताको पक्षमा संघर्ष गर्दै आएको कांग्रेस अहिले फेरि नागरिक अधिकारको रक्षाका लागि संघर्षको संघारमा रहेको उल्लेख गरिएको छ। यस्तो अवस्थामा पार्टीभित्रको अन्तरविरोधले नागरिक स्वतन्त्रता र राष्ट्रिय एकतालाई कमजोर पार्न खोज्ने शक्तिलाई अनुकूल वातावरण बनाइदिएको भन्दै पार्टीभित्र बृहत्तर एकता अपरिहार्य रहेको विज्ञप्तिमा उल्लेख छ।

अभियानका अनुसार कांग्रेस समर्थक मात्र नभई शुभेच्छुकहरूले समेत पार्टीभित्रको एकतालाई आवश्यक ठानेका छन्। पार्टी एकताका विषयमा सभापतिसहित शीर्ष नेताहरूसँग भएका छलफल सकारात्मक रहेको जानकारी पनि विज्ञप्तिमार्फत दिइएको छ।

विज्ञप्तिमा पछिल्लो समय समाजमा बढ्दो अराजकता र असहिष्णु व्यवहार नियन्त्रण गर्नु राज्यको दायित्व भएको उल्लेख गर्दै सुनसरीको देवानगञ्ज क्षेत्रमा भइरहेको धार्मिक द्वन्द्वले थप संकटको संकेत गरेको जनाइएको छ। देशलाई विभाजनतर्फ जानबाट रोक्न, समाजलाई जोड्न र साम्प्रदायिक हिंसाबाट बाहिर निस्केर सहिष्णुता र सामाजिक एकता कायम गर्न सबै पक्षसँग अपिल गरिएको छ।

त्यस्तै, उक्त घटनामा ज्यान गुमाएकाप्रति भावपूर्ण श्रद्धाञ्जलि अर्पण गर्दै घाइतेहरूको शीघ्र स्वास्थ्यलाभको कामना गरिएको छ।

अभियानले औपचारिक राष्ट्रिय भेला पछि सारिए पनि पार्टी एकताका लागि अनौपचारिक दबाब अभियान भने निरन्तर सञ्चालन हुने स्पष्ट पारेको छ। साथै देशभरका कांग्रेस समर्थित जनप्रतिनिधि, शुभेच्छुक र समर्थकलाई आ–आफ्नो क्षेत्रबाट पार्टीका शीर्ष नेताहरूमाथि एकताका लागि दबाब अभियान जारी राख्न हार्दिक अपिल गरेको छ।

प्रेस विज्ञप्तिमा स्वर्गीय वरिष्ठ नेता गोपालमान श्रेष्ठप्रति भावपूर्ण श्रद्धाञ्जलि व्यक्त गर्दै शोकसन्तप्त परिवारप्रति गहिरो समवेदना पनि प्रकट गरिएको छ।

articles.title: ठूलो ब्याट्री र प्रिमियम फिचर्ससहित नेपाली बजारमा नयाँ टाटा पन्च ईभी
articles.summary:
टाटा मोटर्सले नेपाली बजारमा ठूलो ब्याट्री क्षमता, आकर्षक डिजाइन र अत्याधुनिक प्रविधिसहितको नयाँ टाटा पन्च ईभी सार्वजनिक गरेको छ। कम्पनीका अनुसार नयाँ संस्करणले लामो रेन्ज, शक्तिशाली प्रदर्शन र थप स्मार्ट फिचर्समार्फत विद्युतीय सवारी प्रयोगकर्तालाई नयाँ अनुभव दिने लक्ष्य राखेको छ।

नयाँ टाटा पन्च ईभीमा प्रिमियम इन्टेरियर, आधुनिक कनेक्टिभिटी फिचर्स तथा आरामदायी ड्राइभिङ अनुभवलाई प्राथमिकता दिइएको छ। उच्च ग्राउन्ड क्लियरेन्सका कारण यो सवारी नेपाली सडकको विविध भूगोल र यात्राका लागि उपयुक्त हुने कम्पनीको दाबी छ।

सुरक्षालाई समेत प्राथमिकतामा राखिएको यस विद्युतीय एसयूभीले ५-स्टार सुरक्षा रेटिङ प्राप्त गरेको छ। कम्पनीका अनुसार यसले चालक र यात्रुको सुरक्षासँगै विश्वसनीय प्रदर्शन सुनिश्चित गर्नेछ।

लामो रेन्ज, ठूलो ब्याट्री क्षमता र एसयूभीको आकर्षक डिजाइनका कारण नयाँ टाटा पन्च ईभी नेपाली बजारमा विद्युतीय सवारीको विकल्पका रूपमा थप प्रतिस्पर्धी बन्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

articles.title: इरानलाई कडा प्रहार गर्ने चेतावनी दिँदै ट्रम्पले भने : उनीहरूले नराम्रोसँग कुटाइ खानेछन्
articles.summary:
मध्यपूर्वमा एकाएक बढेको तनाव र जोर्डनस्थित अमेरिकी सैन्य अड्डामाथिको इरानी क्षेप्यास्त्र आक्रमणको प्रयासपछि अमेरिकी राष्ट्रपति डोनाल्ड ट्रम्पले कडा सैन्य प्रतिकारको चेतावनी दिएका छन्।

फक्स न्युजसँगको विशेष कुराकानीका क्रममा राष्ट्रपति ट्रम्पले इरानमाथि कडा सैन्य कारबाही गर्ने चेतावनी दिँदै भने, ‘हामी उनीहरूलाई कडा प्रहार गर्नेछौं, उनीहरूले नराम्रोसँग कुटाइ खानेछन्।’

ट्रम्पले अमेरिकी सेनासँग जोर्डनमाथिको आकस्मिक आक्रमणलाई असफल बनाउन केही मिनेट मात्र बाँकी रहेको अवस्थामा रक्षा प्रणालीले लक्ष्यमा पुग्नुअघि नै क्षेप्यास्त्रहरू आकाशमै सफलतापूर्वक नष्ट गरेको जानकारी दिए। साथै, उनले आक्रमणको समयमा अमेरिकी सेनाले वास्तविक समयमा स्थान संकेत दिएको भिडियोसमेत समीक्षा गरेको बताए।

यसअघि इरानको इस्लामिक रिभोलुसनरी गार्ड कोर्प्स (आईआरजीसी) ले जोर्डनस्थित मुवाफक साल्टी एयर बेस र अमेरिकी सेनाको केन्द्रीय कमान्डको मुख्यालयलाई लक्षित गर्दै ब्यालिस्टिक मिसाइलहरू प्रहार गरेको जनाएको थियो। जोर्डनको सेनाले आफ्नो आकाशमा आएका पाँच वटा इरानी मिसाइल आकाशमै नष्ट गरिएको पुष्टि गरेको छ।

इरान समर्थित समूहहरूले साउदी अरेबियाका तेल खानी र ऊर्जा केन्द्रहरूमा लगातार ड्रोन आक्रमण गरेपछि अमेरिका र साउदी अरेबियाले संयुक्त रूपमा इराकमा रहेका इरान समर्थित सशस्त्र समूहहरूमाथि ठूलो हवाई आक्रमण गरेका हुन्। इराकको पपुलर मोबिलाइजेसन फोर्स (पीएमएफ) ले दिएको जानकारी अनुसार अमेरिका-साउदी आक्रमणका कारण सातवटा प्रान्तमा कम्तीमा २० जना लडाकु मारिएका छन् र ३२ जना घाइते भएका छन्।

राष्ट्रपति ट्रम्पले इराकमा गरिएको उक्त रातारातको आक्रमण इराकी सरकारसँगको समन्वयमै भएको स्पष्ट पार्दै इरान समर्थित समूहहरूलाई ‘संसारको क्यान्सर’ को रूपमा चित्रण गरेका छन्। उनले इरानी समर्थित समूहविरुद्ध थप कडा कदम चालिने चेतावनीसमेत दिएका छन्।

तर, अमेरिका र साउदी अरबको संयुक्त आक्रमणपछि इराकले कडा आपत्ति जनाएको छ। इराकी सरकारले यसलाई आफ्नो देशको सार्वभौमिकताको स्पष्ट उल्लंघन भनेको छ। साथै, इराकले आफ्नो भूभाग छिमेकी देशहरूविरुद्ध आक्रमण गर्ने अखाडा बन्न नदिने बताउँदै आएको छ। यस तनावका बिच इराकी प्रधानमन्त्री मोहम्मद शिया अल-सुडानीको साउदी अरेबिया भ्रमण अनिश्चितकालका लागि स्थगित भएको छ।

यो नयाँ सैन्य द्वन्द्वले विश्वव्यापी ऊर्जा आपूर्तिमा गम्भीर असर पारेको छ। व्यापारका लागि अति संवेदनशील मानिने होर्मुज जलमार्ग र रेड सी क्षेत्रमा देखिएको तनावका कारण तेलको मूल्यमा भारी बृद्धि भएको छ। अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय बजारमा कच्चा तेलको मूल्य करिब सात प्रतिशतले बढेर प्रति ब्यारेल ९० डलरको नजिक पुगेको छ।

ओमानले होर्मुज जलमार्गमा जहाजहरूको ट्रान्जिट व्यवस्थापन गर्न राखेको प्रस्तावलाई इरानले अस्वीकार गरेको छ। यता, यमनका हुथी विद्रोहीहरूले साउदी अरेबियाका तेल डिपोहरूलाई लक्षित गरेर नाकाबन्दीको घोषणा गरेपछि क्षेत्रीय द्वन्द्व थप फैलिने जोखिम बढेको छ। विश्लेषकहरूले यो द्वन्द्व कूटनीतिक माध्यमबाट समाधान नभएमा यसले विश्व अर्थतन्त्र र मध्यपूर्वको शान्तिमा दीर्घकालीन असर पार्ने चेतावनी दिएका छन्। अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय सञ्चार माध्यमहरूको सहयोगमा

articles.title: Doctors end protest after shutting down health services across Nepal for two days
articles.summary:
Nepal Medical Association has called off its nationwide strike after shutting down all hospital services except emergency care for two days as it reached a five-point agreement with the government.

According to a statement issued by the association, the Ministry of Home Affairs will take legal action against those involved in the attack on a doctor and the vandalism at the Narayani Hospital, Birgunj in accordance with the Health Workers and Health Institutions Security Act, 2009.

Likewise, for amending Sections 2, 3, and 15 of the Health Workers and Health Institutions Security Act, 2009, as well as Sections 232 and 233 of the National Penal (Criminal) Code 2017, the Ministry of Health and Population will table the proposed amendments in the upcoming session of the House of Representatives and the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs will facilitate necessary coordination and support.

A committee comprising representatives of the Nepal Medical Association will be formed within seven days to amend health related issues in the Consumer Protection Act (2018). As agreed, another committee will be formed within three days to review all past agreements reached with the association.

The association agreed to call off all protest programmes from Wednesday evening and resume all services.

“We have agreed to call off all protest programmes and resume the service immediately," said Dr Bishwa Raj Dawadi, general secretary of the association. “Halting services was not our choice. How can we treat patients when our fellow doctors are assaulted physically while providing treatment and are abused verbally? It is not possible to provide care in the environment of fear and insecurity.”

Affronted by the lackadaisical approach of the authorities concerned to punishing those involved in the attack on doctors and the health facility in Birgunj, the umbrella organisation of medical doctors had launched an indefinite nationwide strike on Tuesday.

Following the death of a 45-year-old heart patient undergoing treatment in the emergency department of Narayani Hospital, his relatives entered the emergency ward, vandalised property and assaulted doctors and health workers. Dr Pramod Ram, who was on duty, was brutally assaulted. He was brought to Kathmandu and admitted to the National Trauma Centre. According to doctors, his condition is out of danger.

Hundreds of thousands of patients from across the country had been deprived of health care services since Tuesday due to the doctors’ strike.

Dr Manohar Pradhan, an adviser to Health Minister Neesha Mehta, said the ministry was positive about most of the demands of the agitating doctors but it took time to reach an agreement as the association included the consumer court’s provision in the demand.

Due to prolonged strike in the outpatient care, the number of people seeking emergency care increased significantly. Emergency departments of major hospitals including Bir Hospital were overwhelmed with seriously ailing patients. Hospitals treated multiple patients in a single bed and in some cases male and female patients from different locations were placed on the same bed.

“We cannot deny service to seriously ailing patients. Therefore, we have been accommodating three to four patients in a single Emergency bed,” said Dr Prabha Chapagain, acting director at Bir Hospital. “Comapred to other days, the number of patients seeking care in the emergency ward was higher in our hospital.”

Doctors say treating multiple patients in a bed increases the risk of infections spreading from one patient to another.

articles.title: Inside Nepal’s security response after Sunsari violence
articles.summary:
A day after communal violence in Sunsari’s Dewanganj Rural Municipality left one person dead and 22 others injured, Nepal’s top security officials gathered at the government’s central secretariat to assess the situation, discuss the risk of further escalation, and decide how the state should respond.

The Central Security Committee meeting, held at 5 pm on July 27 under the chairmanship of Home Minister Sudan Gurung, brought together senior officials from Nepal’s security and administrative establishment: Nepali Army Lieutenant General Pradeep KC, Home Ministry Secretary Raj Kumar Shrestha, Defence Ministry Secretary Kedarnath Sharma, Nepal Police Inspector General Dan Bahadur Karki, Armed Police Force Inspector General Narayan Dutta Poudel, and National Investigation Department Chief Tekendra Karki. The meeting at the Home Ministry continued until around 9 pm.

The discussion was held after authorities faced questions over the handling of the Dewanganj incident. Earlier that day, the government had begun changing key security officials responsible for the area.

Koshi Province Police Chief Binod Ghimire was recalled and was replaced by DIG Shekhar Khanal from Nepal Police Headquarters. Sunsari Chief District Officer Basudev Ghimire was transferred and replaced by Sankhuwasabha CDO Ishwari Prasad Aryal. Sunsari Police Chief SP Keshav Thebe was recalled, and SP Pushparaj Malla from Gautam Buddha International Airport was sent to Sunsari.

The DSP of the Armed Police Force company based in Kaptanganj, Nandakishor Mahato, who was present in the area during the incident, was also recalled and replaced by DSP Madan Nath from Armed Police Force Headquarters.

At least five people — including security officials and ministry officials familiar with the meeting — told Kantipur what transpired during the July 27 discussion.

According to one official, who spoke on condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of the matter, Home Minister Gurung appeared visibly upset with the security response. Gurung, the official said, also raised concerns over increasing smuggling activities along the border, the lack of effective action against smuggling, and what he described as mistakes by security agencies during the communal violence in Sunsari.

Gurung directed authorities to increase security deployment along the border and install drones and CCTV cameras. The official said the discussion appeared to be moving away from the immediate crisis and measures to address it.

“He was fidgety, at times extremely dissatisfied that security personnel had failed to do their work,” the official added.

Meanwhile, concerns were mounting over whether tensions could escalate further. During the Central Security Committee meeting, security chiefs raised the possibility that the violence could spread to other parts of the country.

According to officials present at the meeting, Army Lieutenant General Pradeep KC and the chiefs of Nepal Police, Armed Police Force, and the National Investigation Department — Dan Bahadur Karki, Narayan Dutta Poudel, and Tekendra Karki — emphasised the need for measures to manage the situation and prevent similar incidents elsewhere.

Another account of the meeting, from a source familiar with the discussion, described a different emphasis from the military side.

Army Lt. General KC, according to the security source, argued that field-level security agencies and officials were already aware of the operational requirements and that the role of the centre should be “to coordinate rather than direct every tactical decision.”

The source said Lt. General KC explained that decisions such as where to deploy security personnel, where to position equipment such as CCTV cameras and drones, and how to mobilise forces were matters traditionally handled at the field level.

“These are tactical and strategic issues,” the source quoted Lt. General KC as saying. “Such matters have been handled from the field rather than from above, and security personnel should be deployed effectively according to that approach.”

KC told the meeting that field-level mechanisms were aware of the situation and that coordination from the centre was necessary.

The source said the heads of other security agencies also informed the meeting that efforts were underway to bring the situation under control. However, the source claimed that the Home Minister appeared more focused on expressing anger than listening to those assessments.

“At such a time, such a temperament does not help,” the source added.

On July 28, Home Minister Gurung held another security meeting at the Home Ministry with officials from Nepal Police, Armed Police Force, and the National Investigation Department.

The meeting instructed subordinate agencies to work toward maintaining social harmony.

However, tensions continued, and violent demonstrations between the two groups resumed in the evening. The incident also triggered a political response.

On July 29, an all-party meeting was held on the initiative of Rabi Lamichhane, chairman of the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party.

The meeting included representatives of parties represented in Parliament — RSP, Nepali Congress, UML, Nepali Communist Party, Shram Sanskriti Party and Rastriya Prajatantra Party — as well as leaders of parties outside Parliament, including Janata Samajbadi Party, Janamat Party, and JSP Nepal.

Prime Minister Balendra Shah did not attend the meeting. Nor did Home Minister Gurung.

The meeting issued a seven-point agreement, including condolences for those killed in the incident, sympathy for the victims and the injured, an appeal for social harmony and peace, calls for local-level all-party mechanisms, stronger coordination and leadership from the centre, control of rumours, and the responsible use of social media.

Questions over Nepal’s security response model

The Sunsari incident has once again raised broader questions about how Nepal manages communal tensions and coordinates security responses across its federal structure.

Under Nepal’s federal system, provincial police chiefs legally come under the authority of provincial governments.

Provincial security committees, led by provincial home ministers, are also responsible for security management and developing strategies.

However, a security official said the transfer of the Koshi Province police chief was carried out without coordination with the provincial government.

“This reflects a wider problem in Nepal’s transition to federal governance,” the official added.

The District Administration Office (headed by the Chief District Officer) remains under the direct command and control of the federal government. Since laws related to the Nepal Police and the federal civil service have not been fully implemented, transfers and deployments of Chief District Officers and provincial police structures continue to be controlled from Kathmandu, the federal capital.

As a result, when security incidents occur in the provinces, coordination between Chief District Officers and provincial mechanisms has not yet become an established practice. Since Chief District Officers, who lead the district security committees, are direct appointees of the Home Ministry, when security incidents occur, they report to Kathmandu, not to the provincial minister for internal affairs, who heads the provincial security committee.

This has created a gap between federal institutions and provincial structures, according to officials familiar with the issue.

Incidents affecting religious and communal harmony have occurred in different parts of the country in the past as well. However, security forces are often deployed only after tensions have already escalated.

Critics argue that the current approach focuses heavily on a control mechanism — using security forces to contain situations after they become violent.

A different approach would focus on management and prevention, involving local governments, provincial governments, federal agencies, civil society groups, and representatives of different communities before tensions turn into violence.

Such an approach would require dialogue and coordination mechanisms to identify warning signs and prevent escalation.

The argument is that managing communal tensions cannot rely only on force after violence occurs; it requires sustained engagement before a crisis develops.

Pradhumna Karki, a former AIG of Nepal Police, said the situation in Devanganj, Sunsari, along with similar incidents that have occurred in different places at different times, suggests that weaknesses in crowd control and crowd management have often resulted in the loss of life and property and disrupted social harmony.

“Different religious communities have their own ways of life, customs and beliefs. They coexist by maintaining social and religious harmony,” he told Kantipur. “However, there are always elements that seek to provoke tensions between them. This is where the security apparatus and the administration must focus their attention.”

Karki also pointed to the lack of crowd-control capacity and non-lethal equipment within the security agencies.

“There is a tendency to acknowledge these shortages only after an incident has occurred — saying that this or that resource was lacking and promising that such shortages will not be allowed in the future,” he said. “This approach needs to end. The necessary resources should be made available in time.”

A prior risk assessment is key, he said, as it helps avert a crisis.

“Had the administration, local government, civil society, political parties and other stakeholders assessed the sensitivity of the issue in advance and acted accordingly, the situation would not have deteriorated.”

Questions over intelligence assessment

The role of Nepal’s National Investigation Department has also come under scrutiny following the Sunsari incident.

The National Investigation Department, which was recently brought under the Prime Minister’s Office, is the country’s main intelligence agency. It is mandated to collect information independently and assess situations, with reports expected to move through a chain of command before other security agencies develop strategies based on those assessments.

Questions have been raised about whether the department had adequately assessed the situation before the Sunsari violence.

The National Investigation Department’s Koshi Province chief is Investigation Director Indra Lama, a DIG-level officer. Its Sunsari chief is Deputy Investigation Director Bimal Ghimire, an SP-level officer.

While officials from other security agencies and the Chief District Officer were recalled or transferred after the incident, officials from the National Investigation Department continued in their positions.

Devraj Bhatta, a former Additional Chief Investigation Director at the National Investigation Department, said there were indications that warning signs had emerged well before the Sunsari incident but were ignored.

“While the local government, security agencies and the administration overlooked those warning signs, the intelligence agencies assigned to monitor the situation also do not appear to have carried out their primary responsibilities,” Bhatta told Kantipur. “Another question is this: if similar incidents had occurred in the past, why were precautionary measures and a strategy not put in place beforehand? That is the central question.”

Bhatta also believes that, after the incident occurred, intervention from the centre to prevent further escalation and restore calm either came too late or was neglected.

“All of these factors contributed to the unfortunate incident in Sunsari, which disrupted religious and social harmony,” he said. “The police, Armed Police Force, intelligence agencies and the local administration were preoccupied with their own interests. Instead of assessing the situation properly, they were focused on their own priorities.”

articles.title: करातेका स्वर्ण विजेता सुनिल र उदयीमान खेलाडी याङ्तेन सम्मानित
articles.summary:
मम्स इन्टरनेसनल नेपालले ११औँ दक्षिण एसियाली खेलकुद (साग) का स्वर्ण पदक विजेता सुनिल लामा र उदयीमान कराते खेलाडी याङ्तेन लामालाई सम्मान गरेको छ।

त्रिपुरेश्वरस्थित वर्ल्ड ट्रेड सेन्टरमा बुधबार आयोजित कार्यक्रममा नेपाली कराते खेलको विकास र विस्तारमा पुर्‍याएको योगदानको कदर गर्दै सुनिल र याङ्तेनलाई सम्मान गरिएको हो।

सुनिल लामा बंगलादेशमा सम्पन्न ११औँ साग तथा १३औँ एसिया प्यासिफिक सितोरियो कराते च्याम्पियनसिपका स्वर्ण पदक विजेता हुन्। अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय स्तरमा नेपाललाई सफलता दिलाउन निरन्तर योगदान पुर्‍याउँदै आएका सुनिलको खेल यात्रा र समर्पणको सम्मान गर्दै मम्स इन्टरनेसनल नेपालले उनलाई सम्मान गरेको जनाएको छ।

कार्यक्रमका प्रमुख अतिथि चर्चित सांगीतिक समूह एक्स ब्यान्डका ड्रमर सुरेन्द्र श्रेष्ठ र मम्स इन्टरनेसनल नेपालकी प्रमुख कार्यकारी अधिकृत (सीईओ) रन्जिता लामाले सुनिल र याङ्तेनलाई सम्मानपत्र तथा खादा ओढाएर सम्मान गरे।

त्यस्तै, १३औँ सागका दोहोरो स्वर्ण पदक विजेता तथा राष्ट्रिय कराते टोलीका प्रशिक्षक मन्देकाजी श्रेष्ठ र अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय कराते खेलाडी सुमन तिमल्सिनाले पनि दुवै खेलाडीलाई खादा ओढाउँदै बधाई दिएका थिए।

बाबुको बाटो पछ्याउँदै याङ्तेनको उदय

उदीयमान खेलाडी याङ्तेन लामा सुनिल लामाका छोरा हुन्। विभिन्न प्रतियोगितामा उत्कृष्ट प्रदर्शन गर्दै सफलता हासिल गर्दै आएका याङ्तेनलाई पनि कार्यक्रममा सम्मान गरिएको हो।

हाल अमेरिकाको न्युयोर्कमा बसोबास गर्दै आएका सुनिल लामाले काठमाडौंको रानीवनमा ‘च्याम्पियन्स मार्सल आर्ट्स एकेडेमी’ स्थापना गरी कराते खेलको प्रवर्द्धनमा सक्रिय भूमिका निर्वाह गर्दै आएका छन्।

मम्स इन्टरनेसनल नेपालकी सीईओ रन्जिता लामाले नेपाली करातेका स्थापित खेलाडी सुनिल र उदीयमान खेलाडी याङ्तेनलाई एउटै मञ्चमा सम्मान गर्न पाउनु संस्थाका लागि खुसीको क्षण भएको बताइन्।

उनले च्याम्पियन्स मार्सल आर्ट्स एकेडेमीले नेपालबाट अमेरिका पुग्ने खेलकर्मीलाई स्वागत तथा सत्कार गर्दै आएको योगदानको प्रशंसा गरिन्।

सम्मान कार्यक्रममा सुनिल लामाले आफू र छोराको खेल उपलब्धिको उच्च मूल्याङ्कन गर्दै सम्मान गरेकोमा मम्स इन्टरनेसनल नेपाल परिवारप्रति आभार व्यक्त गरे।
